design.expected_failure_signature: A successful factorization would separate accurate grasp from independently directed carry in crossed cells. Its falsifiable weakness is off-demonstration phase ambiguity: a missed grasp, slip, or weak action-change label may make the router emphasize lift or carry prematurely. That should appear as stable phase-like motion without object attachment or premature descent, rather than simply a wrong global x sign. Gate floors mitigate but do not eliminate this risk. No measured performance is asserted.

design.reusable_regularity: Grasping depends chiefly on hand/object coupling, whereas transport depends on the independent goal and obstacle. Four learned feature branches specialize in approach, lift, transport and settling; a learned causal router softly weights them. The approach branch has no goal inputs. The router has no absolute object_x or goal_x input, so correlated layout signs cannot directly become phase identifiers. Router supervision is a weak training-only proxy extracted from demonstrated action change points, not a supplied runtime stage. A 0.1 gate floor, ungated world branch and explicit relation skip prevent hard stage decisions from erasing essential dependencies. There is still just one action-generating common DP, not four controllers.

design.expected_failure_signature: A wrong attachment proxy or rapid change in the acquisition direction can rotate the chart prematurely and cause lateral oscillation near grasp. Phase products may encourage premature crossing if the inferred clearance is misleading. If the heading prior helps only transport, successful lifts should still be followed by fewer wrong-x tendencies but acquisition may remain unreliable at extreme object positions; this is a hypothesis, not a measured result. Near cancellation of chart directions is handled by a native +y fallback but may be a discontinuity.

required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Let direction=(1-held)*(object_xy-hand_xy+[0,0.02])+held*(goal_xy-object_xy), c=direction_y/norm and s=direction_x/norm. Encoded lateral=c*world_dx-s*world_dy, forward=s*world_dx+c*world_dy, z=world_dz, grip=gripper. Inverse world_dx=c*lateral+s*forward, world_dy=-s*lateral+c*forward. Unit fallback c=1,s=0 for vanishing direction. Translation units remain 0.01 m per native action. Only host native cube clipping follows decoding.
required_runtime_fields.conditioning: 88 deterministic features per observation: 52 ungated geometry/dynamics/chart/phase features and 36 phase-by-relation products. Fixed metric scales and smoothness constants, no support-fit state or learned encoder. The 0.09 m clearance soft midpoint is evidence-motivated by the observed transport onset; it is not a hard safety or success boundary.
required_runtime_fields.input: raw_history [B,2,45] and raw_current [B,45]; hand 0:3 and 18:21, aperture 3:4 and 21:22, object 4:7 and 22:25, xyzw quaternions 7:11 and 25:29, goal 36:39, wall center 39:42, wall half sizes 42:45

design.reusable_regularity: Factor movement direction from movement magnitude by an invertible horizontal coordinate chart. At chunk start a soft causal attachment proxy blends hand-to-object displacement (regularized toward native +y near zero distance) with object-to-goal displacement. The unit blended direction defines the local forward axis. Once attached, transport primarily along local forward can decode into the required world x/y components even for unseen x combinations. A four-way soft acquisition/lift/cross/place descriptor is supplied as features and as products with relations, never used to select or generate actions. All action sequences, including grasp timing and vertical motion, remain diffusion predictions.
design.title: Causal acquisition-to-transport chart with soft phase products

design.change_summary: Initial distinct scientific design: three learned causal relation branches plus an auxiliary-supervised causal gate, positive gating floor and raw geometric skip features. design.coverage_gap: The support pairs object and goal x signs. Reaching for the object and transporting toward the goal therefore do not require disentangling these factors in support. The same end-effector height can also occur during descent and ascent, so a height-only stage prior could confuse them. This model tests a learned, causal behavioral-regime factorization rather than relying on a single unstructured state embedding.
dependencies_preserved: The reach relation and the goal-object relation have separate direct gated linear skips in addition to learned encoders. The positive gate floor avoids discarding goal or grasp geometry based on a predicted stage.

Absolute hand and wall centers preserve robot/world position; both object xyzw quaternions, current/previous aperture and native-previous hand/object increments preserve pose and temporal information.

World axes and fixed gripper orientation are retained. No rotation/translation symmetry is imposed on the robot. Only declared absent object2 fields are unused.
Branch and gate parameters are all registered in build_modules and participate in the same joint optimizer loss as the untouched common U-Net.

required_runtime_fields.scaling: Relations/clearance use 0.1 m; native-previous position increments use 0.01 m; world hand/wall centers use 0.5 m. No support variance amplification of goal-object x.

design.reusable_regularity: Separate reach, lift and carry MLPs represent distinct relations. Reach sees no goal coordinates; lift sees contact motion and wall clearance but no goal coordinates; carry sees independent goal-hand/object/wall edges. A small learned gate uses aperture, hand-object separation, vertical/y motion, object/hand/goal height, wall-relative y and top clearance, plus horizontal goal distance. It sees no signed absolute object_x or goal_x. Its soft probabilities modulate separate 32-dimensional branches, with a 0.05 floor preserving access when uncertain. Gates are predictions from observations, never teacher-forced stages. The common single four-action DP consumes the 142-dimensional per-observation representation. This is not an expert controller or a mixture of multiple DPs.
design.support_fit: No nonlearned fitted statistics. training_targets constructs labels only for the supplied exact D_N windows.
design.title: Contact-conditioned factorized reach/lift/carry encoder

training_only_targets.definition: Label 1 when native action_z>0.5 and abs(action_y)<0.2; otherwise label 2 when object_z exceeds wall top or object_y exceeds far wall face; otherwise label 0. These are coarse lift/carry/reach pseudo-labels derived from the supplied support, not oracle contact/success labels.
training_only_targets.inference_isolation: Only predicted logits/probabilities computed in condition are used in the action DP. No true stage label is supplied to condition, denoise or action mappings. Labels are not stored in deployment state.
training_only_targets.loss: 0.1 times cross entropy on the two causal-history stage logits. Each window contributes mask[:,0] to each of its two labels; denominator is max(1,2*sum(mask[:,0])). This is separate from the unchanged weight-1 action epsilon MSE with denominator mask.sum()*4.
training_only_targets.name: phase_labels
training_only_targets.source_fields: For each D_N window start t and its causal-history partner max(0,t-1): support actions[step,1:3] and obs[step,5:7], wall center[40:42], wall half-size[43:45].

design.change_summary: Initial A2: geometric yaw action/condition frame plus causal soft branch factorization and one support-fitted clearance scalar. Distinct from ungated world-relational A1; no auxiliary diffusion channels or losses. No structural repairs at authorship.
design.coverage_gap: Five diagonal LL/HH layouts scarcely vary the lateral direction of transport. The grasp-lift-carry sequence is represented, but mixed-sign object/goal pairs and larger transverse errors are not. A world-axis policy may memorize forward-y transport rather than the changing goal direction.
dependencies_preserved: Frame yaw is provided explicitly and all wall face distances remain world-axis quantities. Hand and wall world positions and all wall half sizes preserve robot workspace, finite wall x edges, and axis-dependent native clipping rather than assuming full rotational symmetry.

All relative position and velocity vectors used in local coordinates are rotated by the same chunk-start basis as action xyz. Object current/previous xyzw quaternions remain explicitly labeled world-frame channels. Gripper is never rotated.

Hand/object positions, aperture and its change, object orientation and native-previous motion remain visible in the core. Goal distances enter the soft transport branch and goal bearing also defines the action frame; this is not a claim of strict goal independence before grasp.

Both history observations use the one current chunk-start frame; phase weights use each observation's causal measured state. No cached episode clock, future state, environment handle, or runtime grasp label is needed.

expected_failure_signature: Near a missed or slipping grasp, closed aperture plus short distance may falsely activate carry; the falsifiable signature is premature y transport with a stationary or falling object.

required_runtime_fields.action_frame: At chunk start f=(goal_xy-object_xy)/norm, right=(f_y,-f_x), up=world_z. Encoded action is [right dot world_dxy, f dot world_dxy, world_dz, gripper]; decoding is its orthonormal inverse, with no rescaling or offset. When horizontal norm <=1e-6 m, f=(0,1). One frame is reused for all sixteen actions and both history observations. Decoded native xyz uses the public 0.01 m scale; only the host clips native action4 and executes the fixed prefix of four.
required_runtime_fields.encoder_details: 48 core channels + three 16-dimensional gated embeddings + three gates; 21/22/25 -> 64 -> 16 SiLU MLPs registered during build_modules.
required_runtime_fields.source: causal_context.raw_history [B,2,45] and raw_current [B,45]; no normalized raw history features are used

design.reusable_regularity: Use a horizontal orthonormal frame aligned to the current object-to-goal bearing while leaving gravity vertical. Approach, lift and transport get separate small learned encoders, softly weighted by aperture/proximity and object height or far-side position. Only the transport branch receives direct goal displacement vectors. This aims to reuse a mostly forward carry in new lateral layouts and reduce goal leakage into grasping. Phase weights are conditioning features, not action selection, control commands, plans, or an oracle. The single common diffusion model still generates the entire action chunk.

support_fit.deployment: Save and restore only transfer_margin_m and fit_episode_count as JSON. The config fallback is used only if no support transition matches; the runtime gate consumes the fitted margin, never a future label.
support_fit.scope: Only obs[0:T] and actions[0:T] of the exact five complete D_N episodes supplied to fit_support.
support_fit.statistic: Per episode, find first action with world_dy>0.5, gripper>0.5 and object_z>0.05 m; record object_z-wall_center_z-wall_half_size_z at that causal observation. Median of those margins is the transfer height offset. No model is fit to actions, no rollouts or optimizer steps occur in fitting, and no per-episode trajectory is retained.

design.title: Chunk-start transport frame with soft causal interaction-phase encoders

design.action_frame_semantics: For f=(fx,fy)=(goal_xy-object_xy)/norm, local x axis is (fy,-fx,0), local y is (fx,fy,0), and local z is world z. Encode [fy*ax-fx*ay, fx*ax+fy*ay, az, grip]; decode is its transpose. For horizontal norm<=1e-5 m choose f=(0,1). All channels retain native units, no scaling/centering of action4, no clipping or residual rule. Rotation is orthonormal, preserving the isotropic action epsilon objective. A rotated native cube need not be a local cube: only the host clips after world decoding. The first four of ten diffusion channels are exactly these encoded actions.
design.architecture: One untouched factory common conditional U-Net with 64 conditioning features per observation and ten diffusion channels. No separately initialized networks or pretrained modules. All common parameters participate in the action-plus-motion epsilon loss.
design.change_summary: Third initial independent design: goal-yaw action/condition mapping plus joint training-only hand/object displacement channels, with full wall/world orientation context. No feedback used and no pre-check structural edits.
design.coverage_gap: Object-to-goal lateral separation is near zero in matched-sign training but can be much larger with opposite signs, especially in E. In world action coordinates the support has little sustained x transport. Hand displacement alone is also an imperfect proxy for carrying because the object is initially stationary and later follows the hand with an offset.
dependencies_preserved: Local-frame hand/object/goal relative vectors coexist with basis orientation, world hand position, world wall center, wall half sizes and signed world-axis box-face clearances. The wall's entire oriented box is reconstructible in the local frame; its left/right extent is not collapsed to wall-top height.

Gravity, table-relative heights and fixed native gripper orientation remain observable through world z and the two heading components. Current and previous object quaternions stay in explicitly declared world xyzw coordinates with canonical sign; they are not incorrectly treated as displacement vectors.

Both gripper apertures and local one-step hand/object differences preserve causal contact and motion evidence. All active current and native-previous physical entities are present; only declared absent object2 channels are omitted.

The same latest chunk-start basis rotates both history observations, all sixteen action targets, all sixteen decoded actions and the training motion targets. It is not recomputed using future predicted or ground-truth object positions within the chunk.

evidence_refs.detail: Exact twenty-episode support only; no development or hidden test states.

design.expected_failure_signature: If the rotated carry regularity transfers, crossed cells should exhibit larger correctly signed world-x transport without needing that sustained native-x pattern in support. Possible falsifying failures are yaw-dependent approach/grasp drift (fixed finger orientation is not symmetric), obstacle strikes if orientation context is underused, or confident empty-hand transport when joint motion diffusion hallucinates attachment. Near-zero horizontal goal-object separation makes the frame unstable; an explicit identity fallback handles only the numerical singularity, not that modeling weakness. No performance is claimed.

design.reusable_regularity: At each chunk start use the observed object-to-goal horizontal direction as local forward y, leaving gravity z fixed. Diffuse future hand and object displacements jointly with action4 to encourage coherent grasp/transport dynamics instead of equating hand motion with object motion. Auxiliary displacements are generated at inference, never supplied. Goal alignment is a coordinate choice, not a claim that wall or fixed gripper orientation can be ignored.

training_only_targets.definition: training_targets creates world displacements. diffusion_targets rotates both vector triples by the same causal chunk-start heading and appends them after the unchanged encoded action4. Padded labels are zero and are excluded by the common horizon mask.
training_only_targets.inference: The six motion channels are sampled and denoised jointly using only causal condition and host noise. Their ground truth is never read or injected at inference; only decoded first four channels are executed. No planner or simulator is called.
training_only_targets.loss: Additional 0.15 times auxiliary epsilon squared error summed over valid six-dimensional motion channels, divided separately by mask.sum()*6 (empty-mask denominator clamped). design.change_summary: Initial A3: learned typed relational message passing and seven joint future-outcome diffusion channels, unlike the fixed relations of A1 and the causal phase/action-frame bias of A2. No structural repairs at authorship.
design.coverage_gap: Only LL and HH object/goal pairs appear in D5. A small set of action sequences need not teach independent grasp and transport dependencies, especially when most lateral transport errors are nearly zero. dependencies_preserved: Node order and type indicators distinguish hand, object, goal and obstacle; graph averaging is over incoming messages, not over interchangeable final entity outputs.

Node positions relative to the wall, world heights, wall half sizes and skip wall world center preserve finite obstacle geometry and absolute workspace/gravity dependence. All directed pair positions and causal velocities are supplied. The wall is not reduced to a point-only obstacle because all half sizes remain node attributes and skip features.

Object xyzw orientation and its native-previous difference, current aperture and native-previous aperture change, and hand/object motion are included. Static goal and wall velocities are zero by declared task semantics; absent object2 channels are not modeled.

The two complete causal observations are encoded independently and concatenated by the frozen DP. All learned encoder and update parameters participate in the common and auxiliary joint training loss.

design.reusable_regularity: Encode hand, manipulated object, goal and finite wall as four typed entities. Shared directed-edge networks process relative positions and velocities, with two shared message/update rounds, so interaction computations are reused rather than assigning unrelated networks to individual coordinate slots. A 32-channel geometric skip avoids forcing precise control geometry through a learned bottleneck. Jointly diffuse future object-minus-hand, goal-minus-object and aperture to encourage consistent attachment and progress trajectories alongside actions. These are sampled latent outputs at deployment, never known future conditioning. There is no stage schedule, fixed grasp gate, or action rotation in this design.
design.support_fit: No fitted inference statistics or cached support labels; deployment state is empty. Future targets are produced only by training_targets on the exact D5. Learned modules are created only by build_modules and trained from scratch with the frozen common optimizer budget.
design.title: Typed relational message passing with joint future-relation diffusion

training_only_targets.inference: No target arrays, masks or future truth are consulted by condition, denoise or decode. The host initializes all eleven channels as noise, jointly samples them with the one common DP, and discards generated auxiliary channels before native action decoding.
training_only_targets.loss: 0.25 * sum(mask * squared auxiliary epsilon error)/(7*mask.sum()), denominator floor 1 only for an entirely invalid mask. This finite nonnegative auxiliary term is separate from the untouched weight-1 action4 epsilon term with denominator 4*mask.sum(). No additional action reconstruction objective or action reweighting.
training_only_targets.name: future_relations
training_only_targets.source: For support window at (episode,t) and valid j in 0:16, take observation t+j+1 from that exact episode: channels 0:3=(object[4:7]-hand[0:3])/0.1 m, 3:6=(goal[36:39]-object[4:7])/0.1 m, 6=2*aperture[3]-1. Validity requires t+j < len(actions). Invalid tail values are zero and excluded by the common window mask.

design.change_summary: Initial pre-feedback design. Introduces weight-shared learned typed-edge embeddings and seven joint motion/aperture diffusion channels with a separately normalized nonnegative auxiliary loss. Keeps native action frame, one unmodified factory U-Net, fixed action loss, history/horizon/execution prefix and all common training budgets. No explicit phase thresholds, support fitting, action prior controller, planner, pretrained encoder or extra demonstrations.
design.coverage_gap: Two short successful episodes couple object_x and goal_x and do not identify all causal stage transitions from raw marginals. The same nearby hand-object configuration can occur while approaching or lifting, and the dataset has little lateral goal-relative action variation. There is enough within-episode motion to supervise whether hand and object move together, without acquiring extra demonstrations.
dependencies_preserved: 31 ungated metric bypass channels retain world wall center, size, hand/object/goal wall-relative positions, both object xyzw quaternions, current/previous aperture and hand/object increments. All relevant current/previous physical poses remain reconstructible; only absent object2 channels are omitted.

The edge coordinates and actions remain in native world axes. World gravity, finite wall dimensions, signed native box-face offsets and top clearances remain explicit. No obstacle-independent rotational or reflection invariance is assumed.
The four edge roles remain distinct after a weight-shared encoder, rather than being pooled into an unordered average. The common U-Net learns their interactions and temporal behavior.

Inference condition receives only raw causal history. Auxiliary future channels are jointly generated diffusion variables, never future observations supplied to the inference condition. No predicted trajectory is passed to a planner or analytic controller; auxiliary channels are discarded by the public action decoder path.

design.expected_failure_signature: If extra predicted-motion channels mostly memorize the two trajectories, the model may produce plausible lifts without the required lateral goal correction on C/E. If the auxiliary objective competes with action precision, grasp timing or closing may degrade despite plausible hand/object co-motion predictions. A learned encoder may overfit aperture or orientation traces rather than actual contact. These signatures are hypotheses, not observed outcomes.

required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Identity native world action4 is the first four diffusion channels. World xyz is measured in native 0.01 m/action units; gripper is unchanged. Host alone clips the decoded native cube and executes the fixed four-step prefix.
required_runtime_fields.conditioning: 127 dimensions per observation: four 24-dimensional learned edge embeddings plus a 31-dimensional metric bypass. Each edge starts with 24 deterministic values including its four-way role. Shared MLP 24->64->24 with SiLU and LayerNorm. Every learned module is registered only in build_modules and participates in the joint optimizer loss.
required_runtime_fields.deployment_state: No fitted statistics, label caches or training episode data are retained. The edge-role identity matrix is a registered checkpoint buffer. Common normalizer and optimizer settings are untouched; representation uses physical scales rather than support marginal normalization.
required_runtime_fields.input: causal_context.raw_history [B,2,45], using hand 0:3 and 18:21, aperture 3:4 and 21:22, object 4:7 and 22:25, xyzw quaternions 7:11 and 25:29, goal 36:39, wall center 39:42 and wall half size 42:45

design.reusable_regularity: A shared small MLP encodes four typed directed relations separately: hand-to-object, object-to-goal, hand-to-wall, object-to-wall. It sees relative displacement, distance, relative motion, aperture and native obstacle clearances. The acquisition edge has no goal endpoint; the transport edge explicitly uses the independent current goal. Concatenated role-specific embeddings let the single DP compose these relations. Jointly diffusing future hand displacement, object displacement and aperture with action4 encourages a latent contact/motion structure without hand-written stage gates. It is a learned relational and predictive-supervision prior, not the action chart of A2 or the fixed feature-only policy of A1.
design.title: Typed shared-edge encoder with joint action and motion diffusion

training_only_targets.loss: Additional 0.20 times auxiliary epsilon squared error, multiplied by the common valid transition mask and divided by 7*mask.sum() (safe denominator floor 1 for an empty mask). This normalization is separate from, and cannot change, the public weight-1 action epsilon loss denominator 4*mask.sum().
training_only_targets.meaning: First three channels: future hand minus chunk-start hand in world meters / 0.10. Next three: future object minus chunk-start object / 0.10. Last: 2*(future aperture-0.5). Invalid padded future slots are zeros, not repeated terminal truth.
training_only_targets.name: future_motion
training_only_targets.source: Only exact D_N support episodes passed to training_targets. For window (episode,t), valid step k uses obs[t+k+1,0:3], obs[t+k+1,4:7], obs[t+k+1,3] and chunk-start obs[t]. No reward, success, expert source or environment internals.
training_only_targets.use: Appended after unmodified encoded action4, producing diffusion_action_dim=11. Host-owned diffusion noise and the single common U-Net jointly model all channels. During inference all eleven channels are sampled/denoised without any future label lookup; only the first four are decoded as actions.

design.change_summary: Initial third scientific design: chunk-fixed horizontal action/representation rotation plus joint action-and-interaction-outcome diffusion with separate masked auxiliary loss. Substantively distinct from a fixed world-only action model and from learned contact-stage gating. No performance feedback used. No structural repairs as authored.
design.coverage_gap: Matched object/goal x in the ten demonstrations produces mostly world-y transport and limited lateral transport. The absent LH/HL combinations and larger E offsets require a new horizontal travel direction, not simply a larger copy of a familiar absolute x coordinate. Furthermore, action-only training can imitate hand motion without representing whether the object follows or clears the wall.
dependencies_preserved: The 67-dimensional condition includes six relative vectors in the one chunk-start frame, both hand/object native-previous increments and previous hand-object relation.
Absolute hand and wall centers, frame cosine/sine and world xyzw object quaternions retain the robot workspace and fixed gripper-axis dependence. This is not a claim of exact robot yaw invariance.

World-axis wall half-sizes and six signed inside-face distances for each of hand and object retain the full finite axis-aligned box without incorrectly rotating half-sizes as vectors. Current hand/object/goal world heights retain gravity/table dependencies.
Current and previous aperture, aperture difference, distances, goal-hand/object/wall vectors retain grasp state and independent goal coordinates. Only absent object2 fields are omitted.
All translational action and future-vector transforms use the identical frame defined from chunk-start raw_current. No future state is used to construct any inference frame.

evidence_refs.use: Limits all labels to exactly this ten-episode support bundle.
Training factor confounding, C/E direction changes, shared runtime wall geometry and native action semantics.
Small initial goal-object x separation in the inspected LL/HH episodes; wall is a finite obstacle offset along world x. A fully obstacle-blind rotation prior would not be justified.
Actual wall separates initial object and raised goal.
Actual object is raised with the gripper before crossing.
Actual object remains associated with hand near the goal.
Another actual raised carry posture over the finite wall inspected.

Shows near-constant approximately 0.04 m vertical hand-object offset during carrying, hand/object co-motion, passage across wall y=0.75 while object z is about 0.24, and lift followed by largely world-y transport. This motivates attachment, motion and wall-clearance auxiliary targets and horizontal-frame actions.
Joint targets must retain encoded action4 first; frames must be causal and chunk-fixed; auxiliary channels are sampled at inference without labels.
Separate common action epsilon denominator and auxiliary loss; no diffusion clipping before native decoding; executor owns native action clipping.

expected_failure_signature: If the frame prior helps transport but hurts grasping, C/E should show lateral drift during descent or rotated approach errors despite suitable transport headings. Explicit world orientation is available but may not be learned from narrow support.

The robot and wall are not rotationally symmetric. Cross-sign cells may show different collision or grasp failure rates even at the same local goal distance; retained orientation/face features may be insufficient to learn this dependency from D10.

If joint outcome learning merely models correlations, the diffusion may sample apparent hand-object attachment while a real missed grasp leaves the object behind. There is no simulator-based correction or action filter.

Very near horizontal goal coincidence the direction frame can turn rapidly or fall back to world +y; repeated chunk replanning may then yield lateral jitter. The frame is fixed within each full sixteen-action chunk.

The auxiliary denoising objective can consume capacity without improving actions, and its added sample channels can increase fixed-method inference latency. This is a falsifiable risk, not a claimed gain.

required_runtime_fields.action_frame: encode xyz = R^T native_xyz; decode xyz = R encoded_xyz. Encoded channels are forward,lateral,world-up,gripper in native delta units; no translation of action vectors, no axis rescaling, no gripper rotation. Native 0.01 m scale and [g,-g] actuator convention remain unchanged. No candidate clipping, including no local cube clipping: host clips the decoded world cube and executes four of sixteen. Frame orientation cannot depend on future object poses or sampled future channels.
required_runtime_fields.frame_definition: At chunk start d = goal_xy - object_xy. For ||d||>1e-6 m let c=d_x/||d||, s=d_y/||d||; otherwise c=0,s=1. Columns of R are (c,s,0),(-s,c,0),(0,0,1), a right-handed orthonormal frame. Both history elements use this same frame.
required_runtime_fields.inference_joint_channels: The common sampler draws all 16 channels from its own Gaussian stream. The shared DP jointly denoises them with causal conditioning. Only sampled channels 0:4 are decoded/executed; the other 12 are discarded. No extra sampler, rollout, planner or test-time guidance.
required_runtime_fields.source: causal_context.raw_history [B,2,45] and raw_current [B,45], both from the common two-observation state history. No targets/masks/IDs/timer/environment handles at inference.

design.reusable_regularity: Express translation in a horizontal object-to-goal frame while preserving gravity and explicitly retaining its orientation relative to the world, robot and wall. Learn a single joint diffusion density over action4 and twelve future interaction channels. These auxiliary trajectories tie commands to carried-object displacement, hand-object attachment and observed-wall clearances. They are not plans, are not executed, and receive no test-time optimization or geometric guidance. The common U-Net and all training schedules remain fixed. No extra encoder or stage classifier is used.
design.support_fit: No fitted statistics; physical scales and degeneracy tolerance are fixed architecture choices. Only training-only targets use exact D_N future observations.
design.title: Horizontal task-frame action and interaction-outcome diffusion

training_only_targets.definition: Twelve channels: future hand displacement from start /0.1 m (3); future object displacement from start /0.1 m (3); future object-minus-hand offset /0.05 m (3); 2*future aperture-1 (1); future object z minus chunk-start wall top /0.1 m (1); future object y minus chunk-start wall far face /0.1 m (1). First nine vector channels rotate into the same causal chunk-start frame in diffusion_targets; aperture/clearance scalars are not rotated. Padded slots beyond the last action have all auxiliary clean values zero. Final valid transitions may use obs[T].
training_only_targets.inference_isolation: Only training_targets and diffusion_targets access future labels. condition, inherited denoise, encode_actions and decode_actions never read labels. No support cache or deployment labels are stored. Inference auxiliary values are sampled, not truth.
training_only_targets.loss: 0.25 * sum(mask[...,None]*(epsilon_aux-noise_aux)^2) / max(1,12*mask.sum()). Action channels 0:4 are exactly the encoded native actions and retain the host weight-1 epsilon loss with denominator 4*mask.sum(). Auxiliary channels neither replace nor reweight the common action loss.
training_only_targets.name: future_world
training_only_targets.source_fields: For each exact D_N window at t and valid offset k=0..15, obs[t+k+1,0:7] supplies next hand xyz, aperture and object xyz; obs[t,0:7] supplies start positions and obs[t,39:45] supplies observed wall geometry. No labels outside this support.

design.action_frame_semantics: Exactly A3: f=(goal_xy-object_xy)/norm, local x=(fy,-fx,0), local y=(fx,fy,0), local z=world z. Encode [fy*ax-fx*ay,fx*ax+fy*ay,az,grip], inverse transpose for decode. Norm<=1e-5 m uses identity heading f=(0,1). Fixed for both causal observations and the entire sixteen-action chunk. Native translation stays 0.01 m/unit; gripper unchanged. Action4 remains first in joint diffusion, orthonormal rotation preserves isotropic error geometry, no candidate clipping or scripted action residual. Host alone clips world actions and executes four.
design.architecture: Original A3 path features64 + current/previous world object-minus-hand skip6 + learned grasp32 =102 per observation. design.expected_failure_signature: Hypothesis: a goal-independent world grasp stream reduces sensitivity of approach/attachment to the goal-frame yaw while retaining crossed-E carry gains. A useful result would improve the remaining HL/LL success rates without losing E-LH/HH. This is not a claim that the observed truncations were grasp failures. The hypothesis is weakened if A4 regresses on crossed E, suggesting the added world view reintroduces layout shortcuts, or if residual failures persist, consistent with another bottleneck such as carry/settling or attachment ambiguity. More parameters and latency are an explicit cost; ties still use the frozen latency rule.

design.coverage_gap: A2 is the q3 winner at 0.900 but its remaining failures are confined to the HL cell: C 8/10 and E 3/5, versus perfect other reported cells. The revised model tests an action-frame bias specifically after the object is raised, while preserving A2's successful reach/lift/carry factorization.
dependencies_preserved: A2's reach/lift/carry branches, dimensions, 17-feature native-world causal phase input, positive gating floor and phase-label rule are retained. Reach/lift do not directly receive goal edges; carry does. At low object height the frame is exactly native-world identity.

The DP condition expands from 142 to 144 features solely to include frame cosine/sine. Absolute hand and wall centers, world object quaternions, both apertures and native increments preserve robot pose, workspace and fixed gripper orientation.

World-axis wall half-sizes and all twelve hand/object face distances stay unrotated. Top clearance and gate y/vertical motion remain world-axis quantities. Rotated vector edges plus explicit orientation retain the obstacle orientation rather than treating the finite box or robot as yaw invariant.

No learned modules, losses, update counts, scheduler settings or control semantics outside the allowed candidate representation and invertible action frame are changed. Four diffusion channels only; no future joint channels, action filter, direct controller or additional DP.

expected_failure_signature: Directional hypothesis: improvement should be concentrated in HL transport-related generalization while already successful cells remain strong. If HL truncations come from grasp/contact or asymmetric robot/wall mechanics instead, this frame may not improve them at all. No physical failure subtype is claimed as observed.
An elevated but poorly attached object still activates the clearance frame; height is not contact truth. Rotation may amplify slips or incorrectly generalize a world-y command into a lateral motion.

The smooth transition can create changing local action coordinates over successive chunks during ascent or descent. Chunk-internal rotation is fixed, but poorly learned transitions may cause lateral hesitation or jitter.

The goal-heading regularization uses an 0.08 m minimum forward component to avoid near-goal yaw instability. Very short/behind-goal displacements are not fully aligned and can still undershoot or stall.

Native gripper and finite wall geometry break exact yaw symmetry. Despite retaining orientation and face distances, cross-sign E orientations lie outside much of support and may cause worse collisions or reaching behavior. A4 can underperform A2; q4 must retain the negative result if so.

required_runtime_fields.action_frame: encode translation=R^T*native_delta_xyz; decode translation=R*encoded_delta_xyz. required_runtime_fields.frame_definition: Using raw_current only, top=wall_z+half_z, u=clamp((object_z-top)/0.08,0,1), weight=u*u*(3-2*u), d=goal_xy-object_xy. yaw=weight*atan2(-d_x,max(d_y,0.08)). Let c=cos(yaw), s=sin(yaw), R columns (c,s,0),(-s,c,0),(0,0,1). This is exactly identity for object_z<=top and tends to local +y goal alignment for an elevated object and d_y>=0.08. The clamp is on a geometric frame descriptor, never on actions. Both history observations and all sixteen action offsets use this one frame.

This is a coordinate transform, not an action prescription or a collision-free planner. All actions still come from the one common diffusion U-Net. The same causal frame rotates relation vectors and translational action channels consistently. The independent learned behavioral phase gate from A2 remains observation-only and is trained with the same small auxiliary cross entropy.

design.expected_failure_signature: If premature goal influence during closure contributes to A2's residual truncations, A4 should improve robustness when pickup and transport directions disagree. If those failures instead come from vertical placement or unrelated policy errors, there may be no gain. Delaying the chart can also hurt: basis rotation may occur too late or too rapidly during the first centimeters of lift, reducing C/E success. A pushed or tilted object can create false lift evidence, and a different support surface height would violate the fitted resting-height assumption. Aggregate development feedback cannot yet distinguish these mechanisms.

required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Exactly A2's invertible rotation law after the revised direction is normalized: c=direction_y/norm, s=direction_x/norm; lateral=c*world_dx-s*world_dy, forward=s*world_dx+c*world_dy, native z and gripper unchanged. Inverse x=c*lateral+s*forward, y=-s*lateral+c*forward. Vanishing direction falls back to c=1,s=0. Units remain native 0.01 m/action and host alone clips in the world action cube.
required_runtime_fields.conditioning_and_training: 88 deterministic conditioning channels; one common factory DP with diffusion_action_dim=4. No auxiliary target/loss, learned encoder, additional model parameters, optimizer change or scheduler change relative to A2. All predicted commands remain learned by the DP.

Replace A2's attachment weight only in direction=(1-weight)*(object_xy-hand_xy+[0,0.02])+weight*(goal_xy-object_xy). The 0.04 m confirmation span is a fixed local length-scale hypothesis, not fitted to development successes. At/below resting height, the chart direction does not depend on the goal. The fitted median comes only from support, not development observations.

design.reusable_regularity: Acquisition and transport should have different conditional dependencies: closeness and gripper closure can justify starting a lift, but object elevation supplies additional evidence before orienting a transport frame toward a remote goal. Retain A2's original soft phase features for deciding motions, while multiplying only the frame's goal-blend weight by smooth causal lift evidence. This gives a goal-independent frame at resting height and recovers the successful A2 chart once the object is elevated. The model still receives the true goal in ungated relations and can learn anticipatory actions. This is an action-coordinate prior, not a grasp oracle, safety guarantee or command generator.
design.title: Lift-evidence-gated interaction chart: separating acquisition from transport

design.change_summary: One new post-feedback A4 training slot, initialized from scratch rather than a selected or warm-started checkpoint. Relative to A2, replace goal-only yaw with causal approach-to-goal shortest-angle interpolation, using averaged current/native-previous approach error and the existing held affinity; append the interpolation scalar to the condition (99 -> 100). Branch architectures, physical scales, phase thresholds, support-fit clearance statistic, native clipping semantics and action-only loss are otherwise unchanged. A1-A3 remain immutable. No structural repairs at authorship.
design.coverage_gap: A2 largely closes the compositional gap but leaves an asymmetric extrapolation gap: E LL and LH each succeed 5/5, whereas E HH is 1/5 and E HL is 0/5. Thus high object_x, not simply goal_x sign or opposite-side pairing, marks its remaining weak cells. Feedback contains only native truncation/success categories, so it does not establish whether the failure is grasp, lift, wall crossing or final placement. A4 tests the specific hypothesis that extrapolated positive hand-to-object approach geometry is insufficiently canonicalized by A2's goal-only frame.
dependencies_preserved: As in A2, hand and wall world positions, wall half sizes and world-axis face coordinates remain in the core. Frame yaw remains explicit. No global rotation or translation symmetry is asserted for the finite wall, robot workspace or native action cube.

Object current/previous world xyzw quaternions, aperture/change, hand/object native-previous displacements, grasp proximity, height above the wall and far-side relation are retained. Absent object2 zero fields are still omitted.

Goal displacement enters the transport branch; goal bearing and current/past hand-object bearing determine the frame. Goal dependence is not removed from early approach, and obstacle dependence is not gated away.

The action frame and added mixing coefficient use only raw_current plus its native-previous slices. Both history observations are expressed in that one chunk-start frame, which is fixed throughout sixteen-step encoding/decoding. Initial repeated history is naturally supported.

evidence_refs.use: A2 C=0.95, E=0.55, frozen score=0.75; E HH=0.2, HL=0, LH=1, LL=1. A1/A3 each score 0.25. A2 is q3's unique maximizer. The same feedback only labels failures native_truncated, so the approach-stage explanation remains a hypothesis, not an observed failure diagnosis.
Same exact D5; no development observations or extra demonstrations are added.
Object_x extrapolation, fixed gravity/world action semantics, causal native-previous fields and finite wall geometry.

Initial positive-object demonstrations have hand-to-object vectors approximately (0.014,0.035,-0.180) and (0.020,0.041,-0.180) m; the first negative-object example has approximately (-0.029,0.003,-0.180) m. These mix x and y differently and motivate approach-bearing rather than purely goal-bearing canonicalization.

Initial lateral action points predominantly negative x, then closure/lift occurs at small hand-object separation. This motivates fading approach yaw near alignment instead of normalizing a nearly zero vector.

Initial lateral action is mostly positive y with a smaller positive x component, while later motion switches from vertical lift to forward transport. This supplies both distinct interaction bearings within the same exact support.
Newly inspected actual HH approach frame; hand is displaced above the object and the goal is across the finite wall.
Previously inspected actual HH transport frame supporting retention of A2's carry representation.
Causal chunk-start frame inverse, one common DP and support-state restoration requirements.

expected_failure_signature: If high-object E failure was mainly approach-direction extrapolation, A4 should improve E HH/HL while keeping much of A2's C and low-object E performance. Continued high-object failures with no gain would reject that sufficiency hypothesis.

If the actual bottleneck is wall crossing, grasp-point asymmetry, or transport-stage dropout, changing only the approach frame may not help. No claim that those failure stages were measured in feedback is made.

As horizontal approach error falls through the 0.02 m crossover, yaw changes more quickly. An unfavorable outcome is contact-time dithering or a regression of already-successful LL/LH approaches despite preserving the carry limit.

The shortest-angle interpolation has an antiparallel branch cut and averaging two native-previous errors introduces slight lag. Unexpected backward approach or overshoot can therefore remain unstable; the frame gives no collision or grasp guarantee.
design.feedback_interpretation: Selection and revision are distinct. q3=A2 by the frozen equal-C/E rule, not by IID or training loss. A1 and A2 final action losses are both about 0.0025-0.0027 but their development scores differ sharply, so more updates are not justified or permitted. A3's graph/joint-outcome design does not improve this development score and has higher measured latency; this single A4 revision therefore does not add its auxiliary machinery. Those confounded comparisons are not proofs about individual components.

required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Encode xyz as [right dot world_dxy, f dot world_dxy, world_dz], append unchanged gripper, and decode by the orthonormal inverse using the identical causal frame. No offsets, scaling, clipping or action correction is added. Native xyz still means 0.01 m per unit; the host alone clips action4 and executes four of sixteen.
required_runtime_fields.encoder_details: A2's 48 core channels plus the chunk-start mix scalar, three unchanged 16-dimensional gated embeddings, and three unchanged phase gates. Same 21/22/25 -> 64 -> 16 SiLU branch encoders; no new learned head.
required_runtime_fields.frame_definition: Let g be normalized goal_xy-object_xy (fallback (0,1) below 1e-6 m), a the arithmetic mean of current and native-previous object_xy-hand_xy, and d=norm(a). Let held equal A2's product of aperture-closure and 3D-proximity sigmoids. Set mix=(1-held)*d^4/(d^4+0.02^4). Yaw angle measured from world +y toward +x is atan2(g_x,g_y) + mix*atan2(a_x*g_y-a_y*g_x, a_x*g_x+a_y*g_y). Then f=(sin(yaw),cos(yaw)), right=(f_y,-f_x). At zero approach error mix is zero, so the goal-bearing frame remains; angles do not define control targets.
required_runtime_fields.source: causal_context.raw_history [B,2,45] and raw_current [B,45]; normalized history unused

design.reusable_regularity: Retain A2's successful causal phase encoders and gravity-preserving local action representation. Extend the chunk-start yaw frame so that, far from a grasp, forward tends toward the measured hand-to-object horizontal bearing; near alignment or a held-like configuration it returns toward the object-to-goal bearing. The same rotation is applied to all local condition vectors and action xyz. This shares approach direction computations across left/right object offsets while preserving the transport prior. The blend is continuous in horizontal distance and uses a shortest-angle interpolation to avoid cancellation of opposite vectors. It is a coordinate mapping only, not a servo, plan, waypoint generator or action override.

design.change_summary: Initial executable design. Replaces raw coordinate conditioning by explicit two-center geometry and sign-invariant orientation; leaves action encoding, action epsilon loss, all masks, diffusion schedules and optimizer unchanged. No performance feedback used.
design.coverage_gap: The exact twenty demonstrations contain ten LL and ten HH layouts, but no LH or HL. Separate world nut and peg x channels can therefore stand in for one another. The observed handle is not the ring center; treating the native object site as the insertion point would introduce an approximately 0.13 m offset.

Current and native-previous gripper, hand/handle increments, and both wxyz orientations converted to continuous rotation columns preserve contact and inertial cues. The two whole causal observations preserve measured ring motion.

No obstacle channels exist beyond the declared table/world and peg geometry. Absent object2 zero fields are omitted; no undeclared geometry is used. Fixed world axes preserve gravity and the native fixed gripper orientation.

design.reusable_regularity: Grasping depends on the hand-to-handle edge, while assembly alignment depends on the ring-to-peg edge. Supply these relations explicitly in world axes, with fixed physical units rather than narrow-support coordinate standard deviations. A second smooth signed proximity scale emphasizes centimeter errors without losing long-range edges. design.reusable_regularity: Learn separate handle-centric grasp and ring-to-peg carry encoders, plus a five-state probability head driven only by causal distances, heights, aperture and velocities. The single world-action diffusion U-Net receives both routed branches, stage probabilities and explicit world/state skips. The gate predicts stage from observations at deployment; it is not an expert controller or a persistent oracle state.

design.expected_failure_signature: If approximate heading canonicalization is insufficient, E cross-sign trials should pick up but accumulate lateral error, especially where native cube saturation differs from local coordinates. Heading changes across replans could produce lateral wobble close to insertion; the 0.05 m regularizer predicts less instability at small ring-goal distances than an unregularized radial frame, but this is unmeasured. Joint future-edge channels may instead harm control by modeling a plausible attached ring even after a failed grasp, or by spending capacity on predictable geometry rather than sharp action switches. required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Encode native xyz by [c*ax-s*ay, s*ax+c*ay, az] and decode with the transpose inverse; native 0.01 m scale is not changed. Scalar gripper is copied exactly. No origin subtraction from actions, local clipping, scale fitting, future-dependent frame or auxiliary-channel execution. The public executor alone clips the decoded world native cube and executes four of sixteen actions.
required_runtime_fields.frame_definition: At chunk start let dx=goal_x-ring_x, dy=goal_y-ring_y, lift=sigmoid((ring_z-rest_height-0.04)/0.015), theta=lift*atan2(dx,sqrt(dy^2+0.05^2)). With c=cos(theta), s=sin(theta), basis columns are e_lateral=(c,-s,0), e_forward=(s,c,0), e_up=(0,0,1). Both history observations, every target vector and all sixteen actions use this one fixed start frame.

design.reusable_regularity: Model actions jointly with future grasp and insertion relations, making attachment and task progress part of the same stochastic sequence rather than using a stage classifier. During observed lift, smoothly rotate horizontal vector/action coordinates toward the currently observed ring-to-peg direction. This makes long transports more similar in local axes. Near the table the frame is nearly world-aligned; near the peg a finite forward regularizer prevents an ill-defined radial heading. These are coordinate operations, not a target controller, planner, simulator model or test-time optimization.
design.support_fit: Only median initial ring z from the exact current D_N is stored as rest_height_m, to center the smooth lift frame gate; JSON restoration occurs before build_modules. All other scales are finite physical design constants, not fitted using other support or evaluation data.

design.reusable_regularity: Grasping is controlled by the handle relative to the hand; seating is controlled by the physical ring center relative to the peg goal, not the handle site relative to the peg. Expose both relations in world-aligned metric coordinates and at a fine contact scale, while retaining a coarse absolute robot position. The 45-channel deterministic representation includes an information-preserving core plus smooth distances, planar proximities and a regularized seating direction. Fixed physical scales rather than small support variances avoid artificially magnifying nearly constant channels. No controller, waypoint, action residual or time-based stage rule is used.

design.expected_failure_signature: Falsifiable: factorization should reduce sign-correlated pickup errors in C without having to infer a new pickup strategy from goal_x. Failure may instead cluster at phase boundaries: a missed grasp can be interpreted as lift, or a large E transport error can keep a ring in transport too long. design.expected_failure_signature: Falsifiable: if horizontal directional coverage is the main limitation, C/E transport errors should become less tied to the world sign of nut_x-goal_x, without altering vertical grasp/lower semantics. Failures may instead come from atypical hand reach in the rotated frame, inaccurate generated ring motion after a failed grasp, or rapid heading changes near an overshot goal. required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Let v=(goal_x-ring_x, goal_y-ring_y+.05) at chunk start and (cs,sn)=v/||v||. If ||v||<1e-6, use (cs,sn)=(0,1). Native xyz scale remains .01 m, scalar gripper is copied unchanged, and no encoded or native candidate clipping occurs. design.reusable_regularity: Express horizontal relationships and actions in a chunk-start frame tilted toward the observed ring-to-peg direction. Keep vertical actions and scalar gripper semantics unchanged. Jointly diffuse native-equivalent action4 with future hand and ring displacements to make learned contact/transport dynamics part of the denoising problem. The auxiliary future channels are generated at inference rather than used as ground-truth conditions. Relative future displacements are translation-independent and expose the coupled motion after grasp, unlike absolute future positions. The world-y bias regularizes the frame near seating; this is a soft directional prior, not a claim that the robot is exactly yaw-invariant.

design.change_summary: Initial independent design: shared 17-to-16 typed edge encoder, 28-to-16 world encoder, learned three-edge attention, direct geometric bypass, 92 conditioning channels, and orthonormal causal action reparameterization. design.coverage_gap: With only the five LL/HH demonstrations, the range of ring-to-peg lateral displacement is narrow relative to the unobserved LH/HL and extrapolated cells. Learning only world-axis lateral commands could bind transport to the layout's absolute x. Distinct grasp and insertion geometry also have to be reused at different causal stages.
dependencies_preserved: The ring center is not substituted for the handle grasp site. Three distinct typed edges explicitly represent grasp, assembly alignment and rigid handle/ring linkage.

The frame is only a reparameterization: current hand world xyz, basis components, absolute heights, both current and previous object orientations, hand/handle finite differences and aperture history enter the encoder. Thus robot reach, fixed world gripper orientation, table and peg clearance are not treated as invariant under arbitrary rotation or translation.
The full signed goal-ring vector is retained even when the frame's forward-y term uses a nonnegative regularizer. The frame does not remove backward error or prescribe motion.

All input information comes from the common deployment observation, including goal position as peg geometry. Object2 is declared absent and omitted. No additional obstacle pose, grasp success flag, task phase, collision query or environment state is requested.

dependencies_preserved: The handle and ring are distinct nodes. The ring-to-handle edge and sign-invariant body orientation columns preserve eccentricity and tilt; hand-to-handle is not substituted for ring-to-peg alignment.

All four heights, the hand-to-peg edge and ring-to-peg edge preserve table/gravity, clearance and peg obstacle dependencies. The fixed native gripper and world-action axes are retained.

Shared raw two-observation history, native previous translational/aperture fields, measured hand/site/ring displacements and body axes allow the network to infer binding and motion. No time index or phase oracle is supplied.

required_runtime_fields.action_frame: The first four diffusion channels are unchanged native world_dx, world_dy, world_dz and gripper. required_runtime_fields.inference_auxiliaries: Seven additional joint channels start as host-owned diffusion noise and are denoised jointly. They are generated internal outputs, discarded by the executor, never future ground-truth conditioning and never used for rollout, search or planning.
required_runtime_fields.representation: Each of four edges has 21 inputs: signed displacement3, 3D range1, planar range1, source/target heights2, relative measured displacement3, role one-hot4, body axes6 and aperture1. design.reusable_regularity: Represent four typed relations with a shared learned edge encoder: hand-to-handle acquisition, ring-to-handle rigid link, ring-to-peg alignment, and hand-to-peg proximity. Mix the ordered relation embeddings and retain a physical skip path. Jointly denoise actions and future ring-goal / handle-hand / aperture trajectories so the common temporal U-Net is trained to associate commanded motion with the object's relative evolution. This tests learned relational dynamics without prescribing phase thresholds or rotating actions.
design.support_fit: None; no fitted statistics, pretrained weights, extra demonstrations or cached trajectories. Physical feature and target scales are fixed constants. The common support normalizer is left unchanged.

design.change_summary: Initial independent design: 35 direct metric features, learned 32-dimensional phase latent, five 35-to-16 conditioning experts with soft predicted-mode mixing, five logits, for 88 conditioning channels. One common DP jointly diffuses 11 channels. Adds separately normalized geometry epsilon and mode cross-entropy losses. Identity action frame. No performance-driven revisions.
design.coverage_gap: Five correlated-layout successes provide limited contact and transition coverage. World-coordinate shortcuts are one problem, but the same near-handle position can mean descending to acquire or ascending with an attached ring. Independent action denoising need not represent whether the nut actually follows the hand or whether alignment precedes descent.
dependencies_preserved: Conditioning distinguishes RoundNut-8 handle from physical ring center and includes hand-handle, goal-ring and ring-handle signed vectors, not just distances.

World hand xyz, absolute handle/ring/goal heights, current and native-previous unit wxyz quaternions, aperture/change, hand/handle finite differences and their relative-motion norm retain fixed orientation, workspace, table/peg clearance and contact/slip dependencies.

Goal is the runtime peg-location field; its world position is recoverable from retained relations and world hand. No new obstacle channel, simulator collision query or success/grasp oracle is used. Only the declared absent object2 channels are dropped.

All action channels stay in the native world frame. Ring motion targets are translations anchored at a causal ring position, while hand-handle targets are same-time vectors. Gripper command and aperture are separate scalars, never rotated or treated as translation.

design.loss_and_capacity: Common action4 epsilon coefficient is exactly 1 with denominator mask.sum()*4, regardless of seven appended channels. Additional nonnegative loss is .25 times valid-normalized auxiliary geometry epsilon plus .05 times valid-normalized mode CE. required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Identity action encode/decode. Joint channels 0:4 are exactly the native world dx,dy,dz,gripper commands; native xyz scale .01 m per unit and gripper semantics are unchanged. The host jointly samples 11 channels, takes the first four for decoding, and alone clips/executes four of sixteen native actions. No generated geometric channel is converted to a waypoint or sent to a controller.
required_runtime_fields.no_future_conditioning: Mode probabilities are always predicted from raw causal geometry, including during training. No mode labels or future observations enter condition, encode/decode, or denoise. At inference auxiliary future channels start from host diffusion noise and are generated, never clamped to truth.
required_runtime_fields.source: condition uses only causal_context.raw_history [B,2,42]; denoise receives only that conditioning, the host's noisy joint sample, diffusion timestep, and causal context

design.reusable_regularity: Generate action and object/contact evolution jointly in the unchanged temporal U-Net. Append seven geometric channels: future ring displacement from the observed chunk-start ring, future handle-minus-hand vector and future aperture. Their supervised denoising encourages actions to share a representation with their physical consequences. Separately, a small observation-only mode predictor softly mixes five learned conditioning experts; it is trained with descriptive support-action mode labels but never teacher-forced. These are conditioning experts, not additional policies or denoisers. Direct metric geometry is retained beside the mixture.
design.support_fit: No deployment support-fit statistics or cached episodes. training_targets constructs arrays only for the host training dataset from this exact D5, without storing them on the candidate. All physical feature scales are fixed, with no external data/pretraining.

training_only_targets.source_fields: At chunk t: mode 0 if native action gripper<.3; else mode 2 if action z>.5; else mode 1 if observed ring z<.06 m; else mode 4 if action z<-.5; else mode 3. These indicate open approach, low closed, upward closed, raised non-descending closed, and downward closed. The .3 and .5 constants lie between observed command regimes, and .06 m separates table-near from lifted configurations; none are optimized thresholds or evaluator labels.

design.architecture: A2 MLP widths retained: grasp26->96->32, carry28->96->32, stage14->64->5. Condition width88 adds frame cosine/sine to A2's86 and makes only carry vectors frame-local. One common action4 U-Net, frozen noise/sampling schedules, optimizer, update budget and executor.
design.change_summary: One feedback-driven hybrid revision. Keep A2's stage targets/loss, learned routing, world grasp features and widths; add A3's orthonormal action/carry frame and axes. Replace the frame sigmoid with a compact smoothstep that is exactly inactive at pickup; discard A3 joint future-edge diffusion. This is newly trained code, not editing a frozen parent, selecting a checkpoint, loading parent weights or combining trained policies. q3 was A2 by the latency tie-break, not by IID or training losses. No extra rollouts, optimizer debug or performance search used.
design.coverage_gap: All initial designs fit IID and A2/A3 solve C, but extrapolated cross-sign layouts remain a gap. Development A2 succeeds in E LL/HH and fails HL/LH, while A3 succeeds in E HL/HH and fails LL/LH. Thus there is complementary support for stage-structured encoding and transport canonicalization. Only success and native_truncated categories were supplied; no stage-specific development trajectories establish the actual cause of any failure.
dependencies_preserved: The handle, ring center and goal remain distinct measured entities. The grasp encoder receives hand-to-handle, previous grasp relation, observed handle-ring offset, orientation, heights, aperture and velocities in world axes.

Carry features contain ring-goal, hand-goal, hand-handle and handle-ring edges, current orientation and hand/handle velocity, all with horizontal vectors in the causal start frame. No perfect-attachment assumption is imposed.

Ungated skips preserve world hand and previous hand xyz, world grasp edge, local ring-goal edge, world hand/ring/goal heights, aperture history and frame cosine/sine. The peg, table/gravity, fixed gripper axes and robot/workspace dependence remain visible.

Stage inference still uses only causal distance magnitudes, heights, aperture and motion, with a nonzero 0.2 floor on each relation branch. No support stage labels, elapsed time or future states enter inference. Absent object2 zeros are omitted.

design.expected_failure_signature: The hybrid hypothesis predicts retaining C and E diagonal competence while recovering some cross-sign E transports, especially the HL cell A3 solved. E LH, unsolved by all initial candidates, is the strongest falsification case for combining low-nut pickup with long positive lateral transport. If E diagonal success falls, frame/encoder interactions have damaged the retained grasp/stage behavior. If cross-sign E remains unsolved despite correct pickup, canonicalization and stage factorization are insufficient. We cannot determine those phases from the current aggregate feedback and do not claim that they were observed. Future slip/recovery and near-goal frame drift remain risks.

required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Encoded xyz=[c*ax-s*ay,s*ax+c*ay,az]; decoded xyz=[c*ux+s*uy,-s*ux+c*uy,uz]. Native 0.01 m translation scale and scalar gripper remain unchanged. All16 actions use the same causal frame even if lift will occur inside the chunk. No local action clipping or action offset, future frame or action correction. Only the public executor clips decoded native world actions and executes the common four-action prefix.
required_runtime_fields.frame_definition: At chunk start dx=goal_x-ring_x and dy=goal_y-ring_y. Let u=clamp((ring_z-rest_height-0.03)/(0.10-0.03),0,1), lift=u^2*(3-2*u), theta=lift*atan2(dx,sqrt(dy^2+0.05^2)). c=cos(theta), s=sin(theta); columns are (c,-s,0), (s,c,0), (0,0,1). This C1 smoothstep is exactly zero near table instead of A3's nonzero sigmoid tail. All carry vectors in both historical observations use the one current chunk-start frame. The world grasp branch is intentionally not rotated.
required_runtime_fields.input: Only context.raw_history [B,2,42] and context.raw_current [B,42], plus one D_N-fitted scalar rest height

design.reusable_regularity: Combine A2's causal stage-supervised grasp/carry factorization with A3's ring-to-peg horizontal action frame. Keep the grasp encoder in world axes and exactly preserve a world-aligned action frame while the ring is near its support-rest height. Rotate the carry branch, its orientation and velocity vectors, its direct goal edge, and native xyz actions into a common frame once the ring rises. This tests whether pickup regularity and long lateral transport regularity can compose without joint future-state diffusion. The heading is a coordinate transform, not a planner or a hardcoded action policy.
design.support_fit: Median initial ring z over this exact D_N only; stored/restored as rest_height_m. No development-fitted geometry/statistics, external pretraining, pretrained parent weights or ensemble. A4 is one new initialized model and one formal training slot.
design.title: Stage-routed world grasp and canonical-frame carry diffusion

training_only_targets.inference_isolation: Labels are returned to the dataset and never retained on the model. The stage head always predicts from raw observations, including in training conditioning. No teacher-forcing at inference.
training_only_targets.loss: 0.15 times NLL of causal stage probabilities, summed over the two history entries and independently normalized by 2*mask[:,0].sum(), with only empty-denominator clamping. design.change_summary: Initial standalone learned-stage candidate: soft mixture-of-encoders plus training-only current command-mode supervision and identity world action coordinates. design.coverage_gap: Correlated LL/HH support can make layout identity a surrogate for progress or lateral control. Unseen combinations and longer lateral reaches change when the robot is ready to descend and pull. A phase inferred from geometry should transfer better than a demonstration clock, while native world action modeling can retain fixed-gripper and per-world-axis control asymmetries.
dependencies_preserved: The gate sees hand/handle offsets, remaining handle-goal travel, their causal displacements, aperture and distance magnitudes, excluding absolute cabinet x or yaw as standalone stage shortcuts.

Thus robot/world, cabinet/table and fixed-orientation-gripper dependencies are retained even when the task-centric gate disagrees.
Both whole history observations are processed, including each observation's embedded previous state. No temporal state is cached and no elapsed-step heuristic is used.
Object2 is omitted only because it is declared absent. Aperture is an input, while the gripper output is still learned as a native scalar.

required_runtime_fields.architecture: 20->64->3 SiLU gate; three independent 20->96->48 SiLU expert encoders. Softmax gates their embeddings, not actions. All modules are registered in build_modules and jointly optimized with one factory DP.

design.reusable_regularity: Inspected support exhibits three distinct action regimes: elevated reach with positive z, descent with negative z and positive cabinet-y approach, then outward pull with negative cabinet-y. A small causal gate operating only on cabinet-local relational geometry softly combines three learned encoders. It is trained to recognize current demonstrator action mode, but no labels, absolute time or future ground truth enter inference. There is one common denoiser, not three policies or an external stage controller.

training_only_targets.definition: Rotate action xy to cabinet frame for labeling only: if cabinet_y < -0.2, class 2 outward; otherwise if world_z > 0, class 0 elevated approach; otherwise class 1 descent. These are action-derived labels, not claimed contact or success labels.
training_only_targets.loss: 0.05 times cross entropy on the current observation's gate logits, weighted by batch.mask[:,0] and divided by sum of those current-element masks. design.change_summary: Initial standalone continuous-outcome candidate. It introduces a shared typed relation encoder with multiplicative interaction and ten-channel joint diffusion, as distinct from a deterministic action-only representation or a supervised discrete-stage encoder. All learned parameters enter the common joint training loss. No support fitting, development feedback, extra pretraining, optimizer changes or task rollouts.
design.coverage_gap: Only correlated near-center LL/HH layouts are demonstrated. Extrapolated translation/yaw may produce hand trajectories that appear plausible while failing to move the handle, and action-only supervision does not explicitly distinguish motion of the hand from motion transmitted to the drawer. This candidate asks whether continuous, support-derived outcome structure transfers across layout changes without imposing a hard contact rule.
dependencies_preserved: Raw cabinet-local relation features bypass the learned bottleneck, and current/previous hand/handle displacements retain causal motion cues.

Absolute world hand, handle and goal positions, current/previous quaternion, cabinet yaw and aperture are retained. The cabinet-frame action representation is not treated as exact symmetry of robot reach, fixed gripper contact or world-axis clipping.
Cabinet and tabletop relationships are represented through observed world height, yaw and handle/goal geometry. No unobserved obstacle, cabinet joint, contact force or collision-free path is queried.

No future ground truth is supplied to condition, denoise or action encode/decode at inference. Joint auxiliary channels are sampled from host-owned noise alongside actions, and only decoded action4 is executed. They do not provide a planner, simulator model or extra inference controller.
Object2 absent-zero fields alone are omitted; gripper commands are learned unchanged as native scalars.

change_summary: One new revision slot based on the completed A1-A3 development feedback; A1-A3 remain immutable and all negative results remain recorded.

Retain A2's chunk-start regularized yaw mapping, world/robot dependencies, physical scales and no-auxiliary-loss architecture. Do not reuse A3's joint-diffusion/encoder package, which had lower development score; no isolated causal claim about its components is made.
Replace the sigmoid lift gate by a compact smoothstep gate so acquisition has exactly zero carry-induced yaw and destination-direction leakage below the lift band.
Add D_N-fitted binding offset and closing-event radius; split acquisition into geometric approach and closure-readiness coordinates rather than using elapsed time or hidden contact state.

Replace A2's ungated destination directions by carry-or-local-peg relevance, while retaining global height and scalar proximity and explicit local obstacle directions. Conditioning grows from 49 to 54 dimensions.
These structural changes are a single untested revision hypothesis, not a claim of improved development success. No performance-driven repeated debug or additional training is requested.
design.coverage_gap: A2 is the unique q3 winner (C=0.50, E=0.50, score=0.500), versus A1=0.375 and A3=0.275. A2 succeeds in all sampled high-nut C/E cases, including E-HL where A1 fails, but C-LH is 0/10 and E-LL and E-LH are each 0/5. All failures are reported as native truncations, with no stage-localized trajectories. The remaining low-nut/direction asymmetry is compatible with acquisition/goal entanglement, but it does not prove a grasp failure. This revision tests that hypothesis rather than claiming a diagnosed cause.
dependencies_preserved: The grasp error is site plus a D_N-fitted binding offset minus hand. Hand/site/ring geometry, body orientation and measured motion remain available independent of the destination gate.

World hand position, hand/ring/peg heights, yaw cosine/sine and rotated body axes retain robot reach, fixed gripper orientation, gravity/table and native axis dependencies. No hand or object pose is forced onto the fitted offset.

Goal directions are attenuated, not assumed irrelevant everywhere: they reappear with actual ring lift or peg proximity. Proximity uses the minimum planar peg distance to hand, handle site and ring. Full direction weight is restored within 0.10 m and ramps to zero at 0.16 m when not carrying. Peg height, hand-peg distance and ring-peg distance remain available even outside that local region.

This is explicitly a local acquisition prior, not an exact global symmetry: distant peg x/y directions are intentionally not reconstructible while the ring is unlifted and the peg is outside the locality envelope. The hypothesis is that those directions are unnecessary for safe local acquisition in this supported assembly layout. The nearby-obstacle path guards against discarding physically relevant peg geometry; it is not a collision guarantee.
After lift, ring-to-peg and hand-to-peg vectors determine transfer/alignment in the chunk-start carry frame, preserving the dependency that helped A2 on E-HL.

Both causal observations, native previous translational/aperture fields and observed ring displacement are used. Absent object2 and redundant native-previous quaternion are omitted. No episode clock, reset factors, reward, success oracle, future labels or simulator handles occur at inference.
