expected_failure_signature: If the remaining failures are mostly positive-direction transport rather than acquisition entanglement, this revision may leave C-LH and low-nut E failures unchanged. This would count against the tested local-acquisition explanation.

The two support closing events and fitted carried offset may be insufficient for fast/short approaches. Early or late closure, or a missed lift despite correct local geometry, would falsify the readiness transfer assumption.

If distant peg direction is actually necessary during acquisition, target-direction gating can make performance worse. Peg interference before lift or a drop followed by poor recovery would challenge the chosen locality envelope.
The compact lift ramp assumes visible ring lift is useful evidence of carrying; a bumped or slipping ring can still activate it incorrectly. No new failure/recovery demonstrations are supplied.
A2's saturation and fixed-gripper yaw asymmetries remain. Loss of its E-HL successes would indicate that stronger phase separation damaged a previously useful carry representation.

required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Retain A2's yaw algebra: d=goal-ring, u=carry*d_x, v=sqrt(d_y^2+0.04^2), sine=u/sqrt(u^2+v^2), cosine=v/sqrt(u^2+v^2). Local xyz=(cosine*world_x-sine*world_y, sine*world_x+cosine*world_y, world_z); inverse is the transpose. The carry weight now uses a compact smoothstep of ring height above the D_N rest reference (starts at +0.006 m, spans 0.030 m), multiplied by A2's closed-aperture sigmoid. Thus acquisition below this lift band is exactly in world axes. A single causal latest-observation frame is held for all 16 actions and both observation rows. Native xyz units remain 0.01 m; gripper is never rotated, shifted or rescaled. The host alone clips the decoded native cube and executes four actions.
required_runtime_fields.history: Earlier-row ring displacement is zero and later-row displacement is the actual two-observation difference. No future trajectory updates a frame or a stage.
required_runtime_fields.representation: 54 physical-scale features per row. Acquisition readiness is a sigmoid of fitted closing-event radius minus current planar grasp error. Five soft phase coordinates split approach, close/lift, raised low-clearance carry, high-clearance transfer, and planar alignment; they condition rather than execute the policy. Current grasp geometry, gated destination geometry, safety proximity, body axes, kinematics and physical ranges are retained.
required_runtime_fields.source: Only causal_context.raw_history [B,2,42] and raw_current [B,42], plus explicitly restored D_N support-fit scalars and one 3-vector

design.reusable_regularity: Acquisition at a handle should be primarily controlled by local grasp geometry and measured closure readiness, not by the direction of a distant insertion target. Fit a static hand-to-site binding offset and the planar error at observed first closing commands using D_N only. Expose a smooth readiness feature and separate approach from close/lift conditioning. Keep A2's regularized carry-bearing action coordinates, while suppressing destination direction before a measured lift unless the peg is locally relevant. The diffusion policy still predicts all commands; these operations are coordinate/feature choices, not an expert controller, finite-state executor or planner.

support_fit.binding_offset: Componentwise median hand_xyz minus handle_site_xyz among D_N observations whose ring z exceeds that episode's initial z by 0.06 m and whose aperture is below 0.7. This is a robust physical relation statistic, not learned weights or a control policy.
support_fit.closure_radius: Median planar fitted-grasp error at each episode's first above-midpoint closing command; the readiness smoothing width is fixed at 0.006 m.
support_fit.deployment: JSON state contains rest_ring_z_m, hand_minus_site_m, closure_radius_m and their observation/event counts. Explicit restoration precedes module construction. Defaults merely make the interface defined if no binding/closing events exist; the supplied trajectories contain both.
support_fit.fixed_constants: The 0.16-to-0.10 m peg locality envelope and compact lift ramp are new finite feature-design choices, not tuned success thresholds. Other physical scales and A2 bearing/clearance/alignment widths are retained.
support_fit.rest_height: Median initial ring-center z across the two episodes, retained from A2.
support_fit.scope: Only exact supplied D_N; binding statistics use obs[0:T] and closing-event geometry uses current obs at real action indices. No terminal observation enters these statistics.

design.title: Local acquisition readiness with carry-gated destination geometry

training_only_targets.name: support-fit closing-event geometry, not a per-window inference target
training_only_targets.source: For each exact D_N episode, take the first native gripper command above the midpoint of that episode's minimum and maximum gripper commands, and measure the contemporaneous planar error site + fitted binding offset - hand. The median of the two event radii is stored as one scalar.
training_only_targets.use: Only a static scale for a causal observation-derived readiness feature. Event indices, commanded gripper labels and episode trajectories are not stored for deployment. No future action or event label is an inference input. No auxiliary loss or joint diffusion channel is added.

design.architecture: One unchanged common DP factory invocation with condition_dim=96, diffusion action_dim=4. Retain A2 grasp MLP 26->64->32 and seating MLP 28->64->32. Replace flat 16->64->4 phase network by 13->64->1 engagement, 8->64->1 vertical and 5->64->1 alignment MLPs, SiLU hidden activations. Concatenate 32+32 branch latents, 4 phase probabilities, 16 world/contact-motion channels, 9 normalized direct relations and 3 range channels. All modules are registered only in build_modules and participate in the joint loss; common U-Net, optimizer, updates, horizons, masks and success semantics are not changed.
design.change_summary: One new A4 training slot based on q3-selected A2. Retain its two encoders, world/geometry dependencies, phase annotations, .25 gate floor and .05 auxiliary weight. Introduce hierarchical dependency-restricted phase inference and a nonsingular, world-aligned lateral range coordinate in both representation and action encoding/decoding; append explicit scales, changing condition width from 93 to 96. A3 is negative comparative feedback, not an inherited parent. Initial A4 files have no structural repairs or performance-driven repeated debug. A1-A3 remain immutable.
design.coverage_gap: Revision feedback leaves an unresolved off-diagonal extrapolation gap: A2 is the q3 winner with score .475, but both cross-sign E cells are 0/5 for every initial candidate. A2's C cells are HL 8/10 and LH 4/10. Low support action loss and reported IID success do not establish systematic recombination. The supplied failure categories say only native_truncated, so they do not localize grasp versus carry versus seating failures.
dependencies_preserved: Keep A2's hand/handle and ring/peg learned encoders, soft gates with .25 floor, nine direct relative-coordinate channels and sixteen robot/world channels. Peg information never vanishes from conditioning.

The engagement head sees hand-to-handle xyz, aperture/change, hand/handle increments, ring height and vertical lever-arm information, without any goal. The vertical head sees hand/handle/ring/goal heights, vertical hand/handle increments, aperture and hand-to-handle vertical gap; it can distinguish upward lifting from downward seating at similar heights without seeing goal_x or goal_y.

The alignment head sees planar ring-to-peg distance, handle motion projected along the observed seating direction, ring/goal height error, ring height and aperture. Its probability changes only the transport-versus-seating split, not the upstream engagement/lift probabilities.

Coarse absolute world hand xyz, current world wxyz quaternion, native hand/handle increments, goal/ring heights, previous quaternion inputs and aperture/change retain workspace, fixed-gripper orientation, gravity and contact dependence. Only declared absent object2 fields are omitted.

Separate hand-to-handle, ring-to-handle and ring-to-peg relations preserve the physical lever arm. Explicit reach/seat range channels make their normalized x coordinates metrically recoverable; world position is not deleted to impose an invalid robot symmetry.

The action unit is a positive scalar computed solely from the current physical ring/hand/handle/goal positions. It is fixed for the full sixteen-action chunk. Native y, z and gripper channels remain unchanged; only the host performs native action clipping and execution.

Both manipulated factors are along world x. Native action scale .01 m, fixed rotation, handle-site object_xyz and separate physical ring_center_xyz. Table-level initial nut_z=.02 and goal_z=.1.

design.expected_failure_signature: Falsifiable: A4 should raise the equal-cell C/E score over A2 if the linked phase/range hypotheses matter, particularly on LH and cross-sign E. Failure to improve cross-sign E would argue that these biases are insufficient, not justify a later checkpoint or extra slot. The new range unit can amplify the wrong learned x direction, underact near zero error, or poorly match clipped expert actions; a failed grasp can also change the range blend prematurely. Hierarchical phase restrictions can misinterpret contact recovery, and vertical-only progress inference can confuse initial approach with descent unless the engagement gate works. Development feedback does not yet identify any of these as observed failure causes. The bundled revision does not isolate the individual causal benefit of its two changes.

required_runtime_fields.action_frame: World-aligned, range-dependent x unit; no rotation or additive reference action. At chunk start let rg=sqrt((handle_x-hand_x)^2+.025^2)/.1 and rs=sqrt((goal_x-ring_x)^2+.025^2)/.1. Let u=clamp((ring_z-.025)/(.08-.025),0,1), w=u^2*(3-2*u), and sx=sqrt((1-w)*rg^2+w*rs^2), so sx>=.25. Encode (ax,ay,az,gripper) as (ax/sx,ay,az,gripper); decode as (sx*ux,uy,uz,ug). All sixteen positions use that same causal sx. Native xyz remains .01 m per decoded unit. Zero encoded action maps to zero native action, action direction remains learned, and the candidate never clips actions. The clamp here is only a geometric feature blend. The host clips the decoded native cube and executes four of sixteen actions.
required_runtime_fields.range_conditioning: Per-history grasp_x and seating_x are divided by rg and rs respectively before metric scaling. Append per-history rg, rs and the shared current chunk sx so the denoiser knows the action unit and the original ranges.
required_runtime_fields.source: Only causal_context.raw_history [B,2,42] and raw_current [B,42]. Learned phase estimates use raw_history; action scaling uses raw_current. No labels, masks, episode indices or elapsed-time clock at inference.

design.reusable_regularity: Two linked hypotheses revise A2: phase inference should respect conditional physical dependencies, and horizontal corrective action magnitude should be represented relative to current geometric range. Replace A2's flat phase head by engagement, vertical-progress and alignment heads. Engagement is goal-independent; vertical progress is independent of planar target position; alignment uses target distance and projected motion rather than factor signs. Retain learned world-axis DP actions but express the x coordinate in a smooth positive range-dependent unit, with associated reach/seating x features normalized by local ranges and scales explicitly retained. This is an invertible coordinate transform, not a prescribed control action, task planner or exact symmetry assumption.
design.support_fit_statistics: None. No support-fit regression, optimization, cached trajectories, external data or pretrained weights. Physical constants are explicit design choices; all training targets come from the same exact D_N. Empty deployment state is sufficient.
design.title: Hierarchical physical phase inference with range-normalized lateral action coordinates

training_only_targets.definition: Priority order: lift=1 if native az>.6 and ring_z<.18; seating=3 if ring_z>.06 and planar goal-to-ring distance<.04; transport=2 if ring_z>.1; otherwise acquisition=0. Coarse motion annotations are not physical contact truth or runtime labels.
training_only_targets.loss: Same weight .05 and NLL form as A2. Each of two historical-label losses is weighted by mask[:,0] and the sum is divided by 2*sum(mask[:,0]) with denominator floor 1. The public four-channel action epsilon objective remains weight 1 and denominator 4*mask.sum(). No auxiliary joint diffusion channels, counterfactual rollouts or future motion conditions are introduced.
training_only_targets.name: phase
training_only_targets.prediction: Let e,r,a be sigmoid outputs of engagement, vertical-progress and alignment heads. Phase probabilities are [1-e, e*(1-r), e*r*(1-a), e*r*a]. Their product structure makes the supervision conditional: acquisition NLL need not teach target alignment; lift NLL need not classify near/far target states.
training_only_targets.source: Unchanged from actual parent A2: exact D_N obs[k] and native actions[k] only.

design.change_summary: One feedback-informed A4, not an edit or ensemble of frozen parents. From A2: replace the whole-episode goal yaw with elevation/aperture-modulated yaw while keeping the .08 m anchor and exact native action inverse. Remove the learned edge/world/attention encoders. From A1: retain transparent direct metric and contact features, add A2-style local orientations and dual world/local signed errors, attenuate goal context during acquisition with a nonzero floor. Condition dimension is 51. No A3 auxiliary heads/channels, no extra losses. All structural changes are made before A4's first interface check; no performance-driven repeated debug.
design.coverage_gap: The development aggregates reveal asymmetric transfer rather than a universal benefit from either raw metric relations or learned transport-frame attention. A1 and A3 achieved C-HL 10/10 but C-LH 0/10; A2 achieved C-LH 10/10 but C-HL 2/10. All three achieved E-HH 5/5 and zero successes in the other E cells. Only truncation/success categories were supplied, not failed-rollout states, so the failed behavioral stage is unknown. A plausible representation problem is goal-dependent acquisition and coordinate/stage entanglement under unseen factor combinations.
dependencies_preserved: Current world hand xyz remains explicit at .3 m scale, preserving finite workspace and robot-base dependence. Fixed world gripper orientation and the object body's orientation are preserved by two local rotation columns for each of current and previous wxyz quaternions together with the explicit frame basis.

Distinct hand-to-handle, handle-to-ring and ring-to-goal vectors retain grasp geometry and actual hole/peg alignment. World grasp error has an ungated bypass; signed insertion error is supplied in both world and local frames with a strictly positive gate floor of .05, rather than removing the peg before acquisition.

Absolute handle, ring and goal heights retain table, gravity and peg clearance. Aperture, aperture change, hand/handle finite differences, contact proximity and elevation distinguish physical configurations without a grasp or phase oracle.

The gating factor itself is explicitly supplied, so gated goal vectors remain recoverable. No global translation or yaw symmetry of the fixed robot is assumed. Goal position is the only declared peg/obstacle-location channel, and no collision query or new obstacle information is introduced. Object2 is omitted solely because it is declared absent.

A3's joint geometry/mode objective did not improve the fixed selection score over A1 and took about 1510 s training versus about 1187 s for A1. This motivates not importing those auxiliary objectives; it does not establish their causal effect in isolation.

expected_failure_signature: If whole-episode goal/frame dependence was the source of asymmetry, this model should improve balance across the two C cells rather than merely reproduce A2's strong LH/weak HL pattern. This is a falsifiable hypothesis, not a diagnosed failure cause.

If E-low failures instead originate from out-of-support grasp reach or grip timing, attenuating goal input will not resolve them: E LL/LH may continue to truncate despite a near-world-aligned acquisition frame.

If the carrying cue rises too early or stays low under tilt/slip, the frame and goal emphasis can transition at the wrong time, causing lateral drift during lift or insufficient transport. Frames are fixed within each chunk, but can change across chunks.

A .05 goal floor and world-coordinate bypass preserve dependencies but do not guarantee immunity to coordinate shortcuts. The U-Net can still learn to amplify weak goal features. A wrong prior could reduce A2's C-LH successes without improving HL.

This is not a planner or a contact solver. It cannot infer unseen collision geometry or certify that a raised ring is securely grasped, and decoded world-cube clipping can still distort large yaw commands.
design.loss_and_capacity: Only one factory-created DP with action dimension 4; no additional learned modules. Action epsilon loss remains coefficient 1, denominator mask.sum()*4, unchanged optimizer, 20000 updates, final EMA checkpoint, history 2, horizon 16 and execute prefix 4. No altered masks, synthetic demonstrations, test-time API, planner or support retrieval. Complete-system parameter count is checked against 3x B0.

required_runtime_fields.action_frame: At chunk start d=goal_xy-ring_xy. Set v=[carry*d_x, .08+carry*max(d_y,0)] and f=v/||v||. Positive forward anchor makes the frame nonsingular; at low carry it approaches world alignment. Basis e_x=[f_y,-f_x,0], e_y=[f_x,f_y,0], e_z=world z. Encode xyz by dot products and decode by the transpose/inverse. Gripper is copied unchanged. The exact same basis transforms both history entries and all sixteen actions. No frame update uses future observations or future actions. Native xyz unit is .01 m; only the public executor clips the decoded world action cube and executes four commands.
required_runtime_fields.source: causal_context.raw_history [B,2,42] for features and raw_current [B,42] for the one fixed chunk-start action basis
required_runtime_fields.stage_cue: raised=sigmoid((ring_z-.075)/.02), closed=sigmoid((.8-aperture)/.1), carry=raised*closed. This uses current observed height/aperture, not actions, labels, time, success flags or hidden contact state. Goal feature gain=.05+.95*carry; local grasp gain=1-.6*carry, with an ungated world grasp bypass.

design.reusable_regularity: At table-level acquisition the grasp relation should dominate, whereas after observed ring elevation the peg relation should dominate. Attenuate goal features and goal-induced frame yaw until a causal elevation/aperture cue indicates carrying. Combine A1's transparent world metric features and smooth contact cues with A2's exact orthonormal action mapping, retaining both signed world and local relations. This tests stage-conditioned factor separation without learned attention, mode-label shortcuts, additional losses, policy ensembling or selection by layout cell.
design.support_fit: None. Fixed scales and cue widths are inherited from the support-motivated A1/A2 choices. The new .05 goal floor and .6 carried-grasp attenuation are one pre-training revision choice, not searched values. No parent weights, fitted episodes, or development states are embedded. The candidate is trained from scratch for the one new fixed slot.
design.title: Acquisition-decoupled dual-frame metric diffusion

design.change_summary: Initial scientific design: direct deterministic cabinet relations plus world bypass; one unchanged common action4 DP and no auxiliary heads/losses. No performance feedback used.
design.coverage_gap: The ten support episodes contain five LL and five HH cabinet-x/yaw combinations, but neither off-diagonal C cell. E combines substantially larger translations and yaw magnitudes. A world-coordinate network can fit this correlation without learning that the pull direction follows cabinet yaw.
dependencies_preserved: World hand and goal positions remain explicit, so the representation does not assume robot reachability is translation-invariant.
Unit sin/cos yaw and both observed xyzw object quaternions remain explicit: the native end-effector orientation is fixed in the world, not rotated with the cabinet.

World heights retain gravity/table dependence; cabinet-relative handle/goal relations retain drawer-front and opening geometry. There is no separate obstacle field in this task and no invented obstacle oracle.

Current and native-previous hand/handle relations and displacements, plus both gripper apertures, are included at each of the two whole observations. Only the declared absent object2 zeros are omitted.

design.reusable_regularity: Represent hand-handle alignment, remaining handle-to-goal travel, and causal hand/handle differences in the observed cabinet frame. design.change_summary: Initial independent scientific design: learned soft-stage expert conditioning and auxiliary phase classification, with native world action4 rather than a rotated action representation. No performance feedback used.

C and E require that transition to follow current hand/handle geometry instead.
dependencies_preserved: World hand/goal positions, world relative vectors and velocities, gravity-relative heights, observed cabinet yaw and current/previous object xyzw quaternions retain robot, cabinet and fixed-gripper dependencies.

Local hand-handle and handle-goal vectors are additional inputs, not replacements for world geometry. The decoder remains native world-frame identity to allow learned effects of the fixed world gripper orientation.

Current/previous apertures and hand/handle changes are available at each of two causal whole observations. The 44-dimensional direct feature bypass remains available even if the learned gate is wrong.
No separate obstacle state exists in the declared task. Handle, goal, yaw and world heights retain the available cabinet/table context; object2 is declared absent.

expected_failure_signature: If causal phase separation helps transfer, pull onset should follow near-handle state rather than the training layout sign or a fixed time. No such result has yet been measured.
Action-derived phase labels are coarse and anticipate up to four actions. A failure would be confidently predicting pull before secure engagement, or remaining in descent after the hand is aligned.

Because xyz output is world-frame rather than analytically rotated, A2 can still learn the x/yaw training correlation; large-yaw failure may show reasonable phase sequencing but a misdirected or ineffective pull.
Three-expert features may overfit the narrow support motion tube; recovery from off-support contact is not supervised.

required_runtime_fields.action_semantics: Inherited identity encode/decode for all world_dx, world_dy, world_dz and gripper channels. No clipping, offsets, rescaling, gripper override or changed executor. Native xyz scale remains 0.01 m and the fixed host executes four of sixteen actions at 80 Hz.
required_runtime_fields.conditioning: Per observation, 44 fixed-physical-scale features feed a 44-96-64 SiLU encoder, a three-logit gate and a 64-96-96 expert bank. Softmax gates mix three 32-dimensional experts. Concatenated direct features, mixture and causal logits give F=79; condition returns [B,2,79].
required_runtime_fields.source: Only causal_context.raw_history [B,2,41] from the shared deployment observation; no phase labels, episode clock or targets at inference

design.reusable_regularity: Learn a three-way soft movement-phase representation (approach/lift, descend, pull) from causal geometry and motion. Three learned 32-dimensional experts are mixed by a learned phase gate, and both the mixture and full physical features condition a single common DP. Four-step support action prefixes supply training-only phase supervision. This tests an explicit learned hybrid-stage prior rather than cabinet-equivariant output actions. There is no hard action switch and no programmed approach or pull command.
design.support_fit: None beyond the frozen host exact-D_N normalization. Targets are returned for training only, never cached on the deployment module. All learned layers are registered in build_modules and participate in the joint loss.
design.title: Causal soft-stage encoder with world-action diffusion

training_only_targets.common_loss: The host's action epsilon loss remains weight 1 with denominator mask.sum()*4. No auxiliary diffusion channels or altered action weighting.
training_only_targets.name: phase
training_only_targets.source: For each exact-D_N window (episode,t), mean native xyz actions from t through min(t+4,T)-1; rotate mean xy using normalized observation[t,39:41]. Class 2 if cabinet-local y < -0.25; otherwise class 1 if mean z < -0.05; otherwise class 0. Thresholds are fixed design hyperparameters, not fitted success rules.
training_only_targets.use: Cross entropy of the causal gate at the latest observation, multiplied by batch.mask[:,0] and divided by its valid count. Weight 0.1. No truth is substituted for a gate at training or inference. Truncated prefixes use only existing support actions.

design.change_summary: Initial independent scientific design: typed weight-shared relational features and joint action/future-displacement diffusion. Shares the basic causal yaw transform with the geometric design but adds a distinct learned relational architecture and generative auxiliary modeling objective; no stage classifier or performance feedback.
design.coverage_gap: Successful support trajectories occupy only LL/HH layouts and couple hand motion with handle motion only after engagement. Action imitation alone can exploit correlated absolute layouts or treat a pull command as evidence that the drawer actually moved. The C/E gap motivates a shared geometric representation and an additional learned motion consequence model.
dependencies_preserved: Relations retain full signed 3D direction, not only distances, and include native-previous geometry and causal changes. Typed edges distinguish robot reach from object-goal progress.

An explicit world-context bypass keeps hand and goal positions, hand/handle world displacements, yaw, current/previous object xyzw quaternions, hand/handle heights and both gripper apertures. Thus analytical yaw canonicalization does not assert that robot reachability or fixed world gripper contact is rotation-invariant.
The local current-edge bypass preserves fine alignment even if the learned compression loses it. All present declared state dependencies are retained; absent object2 zeros are omitted.
Cabinet/front and table dependencies are represented by handle-goal-yaw geometry and world heights. No extra obstacle poses, collision distances or simulator state are available or queried.

evidence_refs.detail: Exact drawer__N10__rep0 support scope with ten episodes; no other task, N, development or hidden-test data
Common observation supplies current and previous hand/handle positions, goal, yaw and quaternion; fixed world end-effector orientation and native action4
LL/HH only, five episodes each; initial handle-to-goal direction follows yaw with approximately 0.128 m travel
obs 30-33 and 58-64: hand descends while handle is stationary. obs 74-78: both hand and handle move outward; these distinguish hand motion from object progress
Actual initial robot/cabinet/goal frame establishes the three physical entities
Actual near-handle frame before appreciable opening
Actual extended-drawer frame motivates modeling handle motion as well as hand motion

expected_failure_signature: If joint consequences regularize transfer, policies with similar alignment should distinguish stationary-handle approach from actual opening rather than keying on layout sign. This is an unmeasured hypothesis.

The demonstrations contain successful coupling but little slip/recovery coverage. A3 may hallucinate handle displacement under an ineffective pull; expected physical signature is continued hand travel while the handle remains stationary.

The auxiliary diffusion variables increase denoising complexity under the same update budget and can compete with action learning. Degraded action precision or noisy near-contact switching would falsify the usefulness of this particular joint prior.

At large E yaw, fixed-gripper interaction geometry may not generalize even if the learned local motion looks plausible. No joint-prediction consistency is enforced through an external dynamics model or planner.

required_runtime_fields.action_semantics: Action4 occupies diffusion channels 0:4. Encode dimensionless native xyz by observed chunk-start yaw R_z^T and decode with R_z. Gripper is copied unchanged. One fixed frame for all 16 steps; no scaling of action magnitude, recentering, clipping or controller. The host alone clips in the native world cube and executes four actions at 80 Hz with 0.01 m xyz scale.
required_runtime_fields.conditioning: Three 12-feature edges (local current xyz, previous xyz, causal xyz change, role one-hot) share a 12-64-24 SiLU map. Their concatenation feeds a 72-48 SiLU fusion. 48 learned features + 9 current-edge coordinates + 26 world-context values yield [B,2,83]. Fixed physical scales are specified in config; common host normalization/optimizer remain untouched.
required_runtime_fields.joint_inference: Diffusion dimension 10. All ten channels start from host-owned noise and are denoised by the one common U-Net. Channels 4:10 are discarded for execution; no future observation, label, mask, target or imagined-state rollout is used as conditioning.
required_runtime_fields.source: Only causal_context.raw_history [B,2,41] and raw_current [B,41], host-owned diffusion samples/timesteps and learned weights

design.reusable_regularity: Use the same learned edge encoder for hand-to-handle, handle-to-goal and hand-to-goal relations, with explicit role tags and causal changes. Jointly denoise cabinet-frame action4 and six future displacement coordinates (hand and handle). The auxiliary trajectory is a learned random variable in the same diffusion process, not an inference oracle. It encourages the denoiser to represent both free hand approach and subsequent coupled hand/handle movement without discrete phase rules.
design.support_fit: No additional fitted statistics or persistent target caches. Empty deployment state; all encoder and common DP parameters are initialized in build_modules and optimized only by the common budget.

Both are rotated by normalized obs[t,39:41] into the single chunk-start cabinet frame and divided by 0.1 m. Pad nonexistent targets with zeros; no future frame or anchor is used.

design.action_frame_semantics: For every one of 16 native action4 rows, encode xyz as Rz(yaw_start)^T times the unitless world displacement command; decode by Rz(yaw_start). Z and gripper are unchanged. No translation of action points, rescaling, candidate clipping, changing native 0.01 m scale, or future frame use. Host alone clips the world cube and executes four actions.
design.architecture: Exactly one common DP factory call, condition_dim=33, diffusion_action_dim=4. All learned capacity belongs to the frozen common U-Net. Common mask-normalized action epsilon objective only.
change_summary: Initial executable design: analytical yaw canonicalization, metric relation and increment features, near-contact tanh features, and world-context bypass. No performance feedback used.
design.coverage_gap: The exact N=2 support has one LL and one HH episode. Cabinet x and yaw are confounded, and neither crossed cells nor yaw magnitudes of 33--37 degrees are observed. Per-coordinate support standardization would particularly magnify the almost-constant goal y and yaw cosine outside support.
dependencies_preserved: The frame is a coordinate change, not a claim of full environment rotation invariance: retain absolute world hand and goal coordinates, world vertical, yaw sine/cosine, and both handle quaternions for fixed robot orientation/workspace and cabinet contact geometry.
Current hand and handle positions, gripper aperture, and native previous hand/handle/aperture encode contact alignment and observed motion. Two whole observation histories are processed separately.

All real positional fields are reconstructible from the unbounded relation vectors and world hand/goal bypass. Current and previous quaternions are unmodified. Absent object2 fields are omitted as declared by task_materials.json.

The cabinet is the relevant visible obstacle. Handle position, cabinet yaw, and remaining drawer travel retain its task-varying geometry; no collision-free path or simulator field is supplied or inferred.

design.action_frame_semantics: Identity encode/decode of all four native action channels. Only the public executor clips native [-1,1] and executes four of sixteen actions. Yaw rotation is used for features and auxiliary targets only, never as an undisclosed action transform.
design.architecture: Shared 13->64->32 SiLU edge encoder, concatenated three edges plus 36 physical features ->128->48 latent. Condition is 48 latent + 36 physical =84 per observation. One unchanged common action4 DP. Training-only (2*84)->128->96 forecast head. All modules registered during build_modules and trained by the joint loss; no extra updates or pretraining.
change_summary: Initial design, not a performance revision: native world action diffusion with shared learned relational representation and a separately normalized training-only future-geometry loss. No checks or results from training/evaluation used.
design.coverage_gap: With only one LL and one HH trajectory, an unrestricted raw-state model can conflate cabinet side with yaw and memorize the timing of the raised approach. The support contains almost no independent layout variation or off-trajectory contact recovery.
dependencies_preserved: The 36-dimensional direct physical bypass includes world and local hand-handle and goal-handle vectors, world hand/handle increments, world hand and goal coordinates, yaw, current/previous quaternions, aperture and aperture change. Learned compression cannot erase these explicit dependencies.
The shared edge MLP has role tags, so reaching the handle is not confused with pulling it to the goal; no permutation-invariance assumption erases the hand/object/goal roles.

Absolute hand and goal, drawer relations and yaw retain the task-varying cabinet geometry and robot workspace. The fixed end-effector frame is respected by native world action encoding. There is no obstacle planner or extra geometry source.
Native previous fields and two whole histories retain observed motion. Absent object2 zeros are omitted, not treated as an obstacle.

expected_failure_signature: Forecast supervision should reduce phase ambiguity if the future relation is predictable from causal geometry. If it instead memorizes support timing, the policy will lower/pull at the wrong location when approach duration changes.

A training-only forecast can become good on support without helping actual contact. The resulting signature would be repeated commanded pulling while the observed drawer fails to move; no predicted state is treated as a runtime observation.
