design.reusable_regularity: Share a learned edge operator across hand-to-handle, handle-to-goal, and hand-to-goal relations. Each edge sees its displacement in world and cabinet coordinates, observed relative increment, distance, and a fixed role tag. A small fused latent is trained both by action diffusion and by predicting future hand/handle relations. The forecast objective asks the encoder to capture reach, descent and actual drawer response rather than merely identify a layout. Unlike analytical action canonicalization, native world axes are retained at the denoiser output to accommodate the fixed robot, gripper and native cube.
design.support_fit_statistics: None. Metric scaling is fixed in code/config, common normalization and all frozen trainer settings remain unchanged. No support cache is retained on the design.
design.title: Predictive interaction-edge encoder with native world-action diffusion

training_only_targets.inference_exclusion: The forecast head is called only in training_loss. No labels, masks, future observation, episode identity or time index enter condition, denoise, or action encode/decode. No forecast is supplied as future truth at deployment.
training_only_targets.loss: Forecast head maps both causal conditioning rows to 16x6 labels. Squared error multiplied by batch.mask[...,None], divided by mask.sum()*6 (clamped denominator for an all-zero mask), weight 0.1. Padded labels are zero and masked. Common action4 epsilon loss remains weight 1 with denominator mask.sum()*4.
training_only_targets.name: future_relations
training_only_targets.source_fields: For valid t+k<T, obs[t+k+1,0:3] minus obs[t+k+1,4:7], and obs[t+k+1,4:7] minus obs[t,4:7]. Both rotated by the causal start yaw obs[t,39:41], then divided by 0.1 m. Only the exact supplied support episodes are used.

design.architecture: Exactly one frozen common action4 DP with condition_dim=49; no extra learned modules or auxiliary loss. Fixed action epsilon objective and denominator mask.sum()*4 remain untouched.
design.change_summary: Initial independently specified cabinet-frame design. First implementation; no performance feedback or structural repair.
design.coverage_gap: D_5 has three LL and two HH episodes, no LH or HL, and only small cabinet yaw magnitudes. Cabinet x and yaw can therefore be mistaken for a single cause. Extrapolation also changes yaw to 33-37 degrees in magnitude. Standardizing nearly constant cosine or goal-y on this small support can amplify that change.
dependencies_preserved: Local hand-handle and goal-handle vectors for current and native previous states, plus goal-hand, retain approach geometry and remaining drawer displacement.
One-step hand and handle displacements retain causal movement and interaction information, including the initially repeated observation.
Current and previous absolute world hand/handle positions and world goal are retained at a lower feature gain to preserve robot reach, table height and workspace dependence.
Current and previous object xyzw quaternions and cabinet sin/cos retain fixed-world gripper versus cabinet orientation. No assertion that robot or collision geometry rotates with the cabinet.

Current and previous gripper aperture and aperture difference remain available. Object2 fields alone are omitted because this task explicitly declares that object absent. No obstacle oracle is assumed.

evidence_refs.use: Identifies exactly the five support episodes and available evidence; no other support is used.
Declares corrected handle point, yaw channel, absent object2, fixed end-effector orientation, native world displacement action semantics, and correlated versus extrapolated factor ranges.
LL=3, HH=2; initial handle-goal separation approximately 0.128 m across all five layouts; gripper action mean -1 and standard deviation zero.
Visible cabinet, handle and robot establish that the cabinet is an oriented interaction object rather than an interchangeable world marker.
The hand is above the handle during approach; retaining vertical relative and absolute geometry matters.
Visible descent toward the handle, not just a straight initial-to-goal trajectory.
The drawer is visibly displaced with the hand near its handle at the end of this demonstration.
Handle remains stationary while hand descends from z about .1255 to .1092; causal relative height and velocities are informative.
Handle moves in both world x and y during opening, supporting a yaw-aware rather than world-y-only description.

expected_failure_signature: If the cabinet-frame prior dominates real fixed-gripper orientation effects, large-yaw episodes should approach the correct local area but fail to engage or retain the handle.
If diffusion memorizes the weak world side channel despite the relative representation, failures will still track the missing x/yaw sign combinations.

Without an explicit phase bottleneck, the raised-approach/descent transition may be smeared: oscillation above the handle or a premature pull is a falsifiable failure pattern. No success measurements have been made.

required_runtime_fields.action_frame: For the entire sixteen-step chunk use Rz(yaw_at_chunk_start)^T on native world action xyz; inverse Rz on decoding. Positive local y is cabinet +y, not relabeled as opening. Gripper is identical in both directions. No shift, per-step future frame, scaling or clipping of actions; host applies .01 m/native-unit and native cube clipping after decoding.
required_runtime_fields.condition: 49 features per each of the two whole observations: 21 local relations/motions, 3 aperture features, 15 scaled world positions, 8 raw quaternion components and 2 unit yaw components. No time, phase oracle, future state or support lookup at inference.
required_runtime_fields.source: causal_context.raw_history[B,2,41] and chunk-start raw_current[B,41], all from the shared deployment observation

design.reusable_regularity: A translating drawer has an oriented local axis. Hand-handle, goal-handle, and observed motion vectors expressed in that cabinet basis can reuse geometry across cabinet position and yaw. Apply the same orthonormal basis to the translational action channels, without treating gripper as a vector. Use physical feature scales instead of fitting tiny orientation variances. This is a representation prior, not a controller or a claimed exact symmetry of the whole robot.
design.support_fit: No learned or empirical support statistics beyond the host normalizer; the representation deliberately uses raw causal fields with fixed .1 m relation, .01 m per-step motion, and .5 m world scales. The host normalization and dataset are unmodified.
design.title: Cabinet-frame kinematics with an explicit world side channel

design.action_frame_semantics: Encode unitless native xyz with Rz(yaw_start)^T; decode with Rz(yaw_start). The same start yaw applies to all 16 rows. Gripper and vertical action are unchanged; no clipping, controller gain change, action shift, integration, solver or planner. Host clips the decoded world cube and executes the fixed four-action prefix. Auxiliary channels do not enter decode_actions.
design.architecture: One common DP, condition_dim=42, diffusion_action_dim=10. Condition consists of 30 physical features plus 3 continuous chart weights and 9 chart-weighted relation coordinates. No extra denoiser or optimizer, no pretraining, no learned modules outside the common DP.
change_summary: Initial independent hypothesis: jointly diffuse local actions and future relative motion, with a smooth causal contact chart and full physical/world bypass. Shares the physically justified yaw convention with A1 but changes the modeled random variables, objective and conditioning interactions. No development feedback used.
design.coverage_gap: Two diagonally paired layouts give almost no evidence for independent translation/yaw transfer or failed-contact recovery. The demonstrations contain a rapid change from descent to pulling followed by delayed drawer movement, which an action-only marginal can imitate without representing the response of the handle.
dependencies_preserved: The 30-dimensional physical bypass carries unbounded local hand-handle and goal-handle vectors, observed local hand/handle increments, world hand and goal positions, aperture/change, yaw, and current/previous quaternions. It retains the actual alignment and observed drawer response even if a chart is inappropriate.

Yaw normalization is only a coordinate change: world position, vertical height and orientation information remain to represent fixed-gripper, robot workspace and cabinet-face dependencies. All present positional fields can be reconstructed from the physical bypass.

Chart weights are continuous functions of each causal observation's planar hand-handle separation and relative height. They do not prescribe an action, use a rollout clock, infer true contact, or replace raw geometry. The denoiser can override these soft biases using the full bypass and observed motion.
No geometry or obstacle channels beyond the common observation are added. Object2 is declared absent and omitted.

evidence_refs.detail: Only the exact N=2 current-support episodes are used for motion labels.
Drawer handle positions, yaw, fixed gripper rotation, 80 Hz native world delta controls, and confounded LL/HH training layout.
88 and 90 transitions; approximately 0.128 m initial drawer travel; no failed-contact demonstrations included.
Raised approach near the cabinet; supports a separate approach/descent representation.
Descending hand near the closed drawer.
Low hand during early drawer movement.
Near-handle interaction with opposite yaw.
Open drawer and low hand at the end of the second demonstration.

Actions 0:28 switch vertical direction near step 23; observed planar separation then is about 0.060 m (obs 21:26). Near pull onset (obs 62:70), hand is around 0.02 m above the handle; obs 72:77 show hand and drawer moving together with nonzero hand-handle offset.
Obs 63:68 show similar low-height approach near onset of pull.
Joint diffusion may append auxiliary channels after the encoded action4; all frames must be causal chunk-start frames.
Common host samples all configured diffusion channels; only first four are decoded/executed. Public action loss denominator remains mask.sum()*4.

expected_failure_signature: If command-response coupling transfers, pulling actions and actual drawer increments should stay coordinated across layouts. Joint generation may instead hallucinate drawer motion after a missed contact, yielding hand travel without observed drawer progress.

The broad soft chart thresholds may trigger low-height pulling on the wrong side of a yawed handle. Correct local pull direction combined with persistent low/side contact failure would expose the missing recovery support.

Co-denoising six extra channels can compete with action learning, especially around the rare discontinuous stage change. This would appear as worse approach/descent timing than an action-only design, rather than a claim that joint diffusion must help.
The cabinet frame does not make the fixed gripper rotation-equivariant. Extreme yaw can still fail even when motion samples are internally consistent.

required_runtime_fields.fields: Current 0:11 and native previous 18:29 hand/aperture/handle/quaternion, goal 36:39, cabinet sine/cosine yaw 39:41
required_runtime_fields.source: context.raw_history

required_runtime_fields.fields: 39:41 for the common chunk-start action basis
required_runtime_fields.source: context.raw_current

required_runtime_fields.fields: First four action channels and six jointly generated motion channels. These are latent samples, never future ground-truth observations.
required_runtime_fields.source: host-owned noisy diffusion sample

design.reusable_regularity: Model an action chunk and its hand/drawer motion together in the fixed chunk-start cabinet frame. Six extra diffusion channels describe cumulative hand and handle displacement from the observed start, so the unchanged temporal U-Net can learn a joint relation between command sequences and relative physical response. Smooth causal geometry charts expose approach, descent and near-handle pulling without a timer or an inferred future state. This is joint stochastic co-denoising, not the separate causal forecast head of A2 or the action-only likelihood of A1.
design.support_fit_statistics: No fitted or cached statistics. Physical scales are fixed; chart centers are a pre-feedback modeling choice informed by the read support geometry (planar approach around 6 cm, near-contact vertical gap around 2 cm), with broad smooth widths rather than a learned success threshold. Common normalization/training recipe is unchanged.
design.title: Causal contact-chart conditioning with joint action and relative-motion diffusion

training_only_targets.diffusion_semantics: Append after exactly preserved encoded action4; all ten channels are noised and jointly denoised by one factory DP using the frozen schedule. At deployment all ten start as host Gaussian noise; the six extra channels are discarded after common sampling.
training_only_targets.inference_exclusion: Future observations are accessed only in training_targets, never retained on the design. No label or mask is consulted by condition/denoise/decode. Inference does not clamp motion latents to ground truth, use predicted motion as an observation, or run an extra planning procedure.
training_only_targets.loss: Additional weight 0.25 times epsilon squared error on channels 4:10, multiplied by the common valid mask and independently divided by mask.sum()*6 (safe all-zero denominator). Public action epsilon loss remains weight 1, denominator mask.sum()*4, unaffected by auxiliary channel count.
training_only_targets.name: future_motion
training_only_targets.source_fields: For each valid transition t+k<T: Rz(obs[t,39:41])^T * (obs[t+k+1,0:3]-obs[t,0:3]) / 0.1 m and the same transformation of obs[t+k+1,4:7]-obs[t,4:7]. These are cumulative displacements from the chunk start, not increments rotated using future yaw. Padded labels are zero.

design.architecture: Gate MLP 9->32->3 with SiLU and softmax; three separate expert MLPs 48->64->32 with SiLU; weighted 32-dimensional mixture plus fixed-feature bypass and probabilities feed exactly one unmodified common DP(condition_dim=83, action_dim=4). All trainable modules participate in action and/or auxiliary loss. The auxiliary prediction is simply the causal gate probability, not a future observation at inference.
design.change_summary: Initial independent learned-phase design, not an A1 clone: native action frame, learned gated representation, and training-only motor-phase supervision replace geometric action canonicalization. No feedback, structural repair or training has occurred.
design.coverage_gap: Only five short successful trajectories cover correlated cabinet x/yaw. They provide distinct raised approach, descent and outward-pull behavior but little off-trajectory coverage. A monolithic condition can use cabinet location or elapsed progress as a surrogate for which interaction behavior is appropriate.
dependencies_preserved: The phase gate sees current relative planar/vertical geometry, remaining goal distance, hand vertical and drawer-axis motion, handle drawer-axis motion, two signed cabinet-frame hand-handle coordinates and aperture. History is processed separately for each of the two observations.

Each conditioning expert and the direct bypass see world-frame current/previous hand-handle, goal-handle and goal-hand relations, world hand/handle motion, aperture, absolute hand/handle/goal positions, both object quaternions, and yaw sin/cos.
World positions and orientation are not discarded by the phase invariance assumption; they can still alter actions for reachability, table/cabinet contact and fixed-gripper geometry.
Only the declared absent object2 channels are omitted; no independent obstacle fields or simulator geometry are invented.

evidence_refs.use: Current D_5 identities and support-only scope.
Native world action4, fixed gripper orientation, corrected handle observation, runtime yaw, two-observation history and LL/HH-only training.
All five gripper commands are -1; the task's meaningful motor changes are not a demonstrated open-versus-close switch. Initial handle-goal distances are approximately .128 m.
Initial approach relative to a finite cabinet and handle.
Hand above the handle during the raised approach/descent transition in a positive-yaw demonstration.
Hand near the handle before opening, motivating geometry-driven phase inference rather than layout-driven timing.
Open drawer and hand near the translated handle at the end of a different layout.
Early positive vertical commands around .6-.7 while approaching the handle.
Vertical command switches from positive .28 at step 23 to negative -.93 at step 24 while world y remains positive.
Small approach commands through step 64 give way to outward saturated-y commands at step 65.
Late outward commands persist while z becomes small positive; outward label takes priority over raise label.

expected_failure_signature: If a phase prior transfers but the native-world action model fails angular extrapolation, the raised/descent/pull order should look appropriate but the lateral pull direction or alignment should be wrong at large yaw.
If the support-only motor labels do not define recoverable states, the learned gate may confuse a missed handle with an engaged handle, producing premature pulling or repeated descent.

A soft mixture can average incompatible phase conditions near transitions; observed stalling or vertical reversals near the top of approach would falsify the proposed benefit. No performance has been measured.

required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Identity encode/decode: first four diffusion channels are native world_dx, world_dy, world_dz, gripper. Gripper is unchanged; only the public executor clips the native cube and applies .01 m per xyz unit. Cabinet axis is used only in features and training-only label construction, not to override or postprocess actions.
required_runtime_fields.condition: 48 fixed physically scaled world relational/context features plus 32 soft-mixed learned expert features and 3 causal phase probabilities = 83 per observation. Gate input has 9 geometry/motion scalars and explicitly excludes absolute cabinet x. No gate labels are read by condition or denoise.
required_runtime_fields.source: Only shared causal_context.raw_history[B,2,41]; no runtime label or elapsed-time field

design.reusable_regularity: Motor phases should be inferred from local hand-handle geometry, observed motion and remaining drawer displacement, not a clock or cabinet x. A supervised causal soft gate mixes three learned conditioning experts. Phase supervision is a training-only partition of demonstrated action directions, not an expert-state oracle, scripted action or hard phase transition. Native-world diffusion deliberately avoids imposing full rotation equivariance on the fixed-orientation robot.
design.support_fit: No empirical statistics or cached labels in deployment state. Physical scales .1 m for relations, .01 m for single-step motion, .5 m for world positions. Training labels are produced only by training_targets on the exact D_5. Host normalization is unmodified.
design.title: Geometry-gated motor-phase encoder with native-world diffusion

training_only_targets.definition: Define outward=sine*world_dx-cosine*world_dy using unit cabinet yaw. Assign pull class 2 if outward>.35, else raise class 0 if world_dz>.15, else descend/align class 1. Thresholds are fixed operational motor-direction categories chosen before checks/training, not fitted expert thresholds or measured optimal settings.
training_only_targets.loss: .05 times categorical cross-entropy of the gate probabilities. Each history label is weighted by its chunk's mask[:,0], with denominator equal to the sum of those two-observation validity weights. The common action4 epsilon loss retains weight 1 and mask.sum()*4 denominator.
training_only_targets.name: motor_phase
training_only_targets.source_fields: For the two causal history indices max(0,t-1) and t, read support native actions[index,0:3] and support obs[index,39:41]. These action labels are unavailable to the deployed gate.

design.architecture: Shared learned edge MLP 6->64->16 with SiLU, applied identically to three ordered edges for both observations; direct metric/world bypass; exactly one frozen common DP(condition_dim=94, diffusion_action_dim=10). No additional denoiser modifications. All encoder and diffusion parameters enter the joint masked loss.
design.change_summary: Third independent pre-feedback hypothesis: joint action/effect diffusion and a shared relation encoder, rather than only A1's deterministic kinematic transform or A2's supervised phase mixture. Shares the physically motivated yaw action basis with A1, but changes the generative target space and representation learning. Initial implementation with no structural repair or performance feedback.
design.coverage_gap: The five LL/HH support paths cannot independently teach all cabinet positions and orientations or recovery behaviors. Action imitation alone need not represent whether a command simply moves the hand or actually moves the drawer. The missing interaction distinction is especially consequential when yaw is extrapolated.
dependencies_preserved: Three ordered edges are handle minus hand, goal minus handle, and goal minus hand. Each carries its full three-dimensional current value and causal one-step change in the cabinet basis. An uncompressed edge bypass preserves exact metric information alongside shared learned embeddings.

Absolute world current/previous hand and handle positions, world goal, both object quaternions, unit yaw, and current/previous/difference gripper aperture remain available. The cabinet frame is not imposed as a full symmetry of fixed-gripper contact or robot reach.

Three-dimensional relative heights and world heights preserve table and cabinet dependence. The supplied drawer pose and yaw are the only cabinet geometry channels; no unobserved obstacle state or collision oracle is introduced.
The only omitted native channels are the declared absent object2. Two whole causal observations are used exactly as in the common policy.

evidence_refs.use: Exactly the five complete support trajectories define all training-only consequence labels.
Yaw-corrected handle, xyzw object pose, cabinet sin/cos, fixed native orientation, common two-observation history and four-dimensional world action semantics.
All layouts have approximately .128 m initial interaction-to-goal distance, with yaw-dependent x/y components; there are three LL and two HH episodes and no mixed-sign training cell.
Visible hand near the still-closed drawer handle, a different geometric relation from a completed pull.
The drawer has translated and the hand remains near its handle; both relations, not only hand motion, characterize the consequence.
Elevated approach motivates retaining vertical relation dynamics rather than modeling only planar drawer progress.
Hand moves for several steps while handle is stationary; handle starts moving between states 70 and 71. This supports explicitly distinguishing hand-handle change from actual goal-handle change.
Moving-handle evidence in the opposite yaw sign, with nonzero world-x and world-y displacement.
Permits joint diffusion with encoded native action4 first and separately mask-normalized auxiliary channels.
Factory supports extra diffusion channels, inference samples all channels and decodes only the first four, and future labels are isolated from causal context.

expected_failure_signature: If the small dataset teaches imagined drawer progress without robust physical engagement, rollout behavior can pull with no actual handle motion; re-observed handle-goal residual will remain large despite repeated pull attempts.
If the additional joint channels distract the frozen-capacity denoiser, action quality can degrade even in familiar layouts, particularly near the approach-to-pull transition or padded episode ends.

If canonicalization is insufficient for fixed-world gripper contact at large yaw, the model can reach a geometrically reasonable area but slide off or miss the handle. Joint consequence supervision is not a collision model or a guarantee of extrapolation. No performance results have been obtained.

required_runtime_fields.action_frame: First four diffusion channels are Rz(yaw_chunk_start)^T times native world xyz and unchanged native gripper. The same fixed chunk-start Rz decodes all sixteen actions; no use of predicted future pose to choose an action frame. No action rescaling or local clipping. Public executor clips the decoded native cube, uses the unchanged .01 m/native-unit controller and executes four actions.
required_runtime_fields.condition: 94 features per observation: 18 metric relation/change edge components, 48 learned shared-edge embedding components and 28 world/orientation/aperture components. Fixed scales; no time, support retrieval, phase oracle, future truth or inference-only auxiliary target.
required_runtime_fields.inference_auxiliary_channels: Channels 4:10 are sampled geometric hypotheses within the host's ten-channel DDIM process. There is no separate predictor rollout, optimizer, planner, score-based sample choice or oracle. Only the decoded first four action channels are executed.
required_runtime_fields.source: Only causal_context.raw_history[B,2,41] and chunk-start raw_current[B,41] from the common runtime observation

design.reusable_regularity: Hand-handle and handle-goal relations are reusable edges of the manipulation problem. Share one learned encoder over three role-ordered relation/motion edges, and jointly denoise local action4 with six future geometric-relation channels. A successful interaction sequence should jointly explain approaching the handle and decreasing drawer-goal displacement. The generated relation channels are hypotheses from the same diffusion process, never future observations or a search-based plan.
design.support_fit: No fitted statistics, retained episodes, pretrained weights or training-label cache in deployment state. Fixed .1 m relation/effect, .01 m one-step motion and .5 m absolute-world scales. All consequence targets are derived by training_targets only from this exact D_5. Common raw normalization is untouched but condition uses the identically supplied raw fields.
design.title: Joint action-and-geometric-consequence diffusion with shared relational encoding

training_only_targets.definition: Channels 0:3 are R_start^T*(handle_next-hand_next)/.1m. Channels 3:6 are R_start^T*(goal_start-handle_next)/.1m. Terminal obs[T] is a valid next state for the last real action. Slots with t+k>=T are filled with zero and receive no direct auxiliary loss. No observed future quaternion or future yaw chooses the basis.
training_only_targets.loss: Append these six targets after encoded action4 and predict their epsilon with the same common U-Net. Extra loss=.25*sum(mask[...,None]*(epsilon_aux-noise_aux)^2)/(6*sum(mask)), with safe zero-mask denominator. Action epsilon retains its independent public weight 1 and denominator 4*sum(mask), unaffected by joint channel count. No loss forces gripper to be a translational quantity.
training_only_targets.name: future_relations
training_only_targets.source_fields: For support window start t and offset k with t+k<T, read the actual support obs[t+k+1,0:3] hand and obs[t+k+1,4:7] handle. Use only obs[t,36:39] goal and obs[t,39:41] yaw for target reference and frame.

design.change_summary: One feedback-driven scientific revision of A3. (1) Move the learned hand-handle relation edge and corresponding three future-offset diffusion targets to world axes fixed relative to the gripper. (2) Retain the old cabinet-local approach as an additional 9D raw bypass, increasing per-observation condition from 141 to 150. Keep the shared encoder widths, multiplicative relation interaction, action frame, six-target auxiliary dimension/weight/scales, all world dependencies and the common DP/update recipe unchanged. This is a new training slot, not an edit or checkpoint choice for A3. A1/A2 are comparative feedback evidence, not implementation parents. No performance-driven trials of A4 or edits to submitted parents.
design.coverage_gap: A3 achieved C=1.0 and E=0.75, but all five E-LH episodes failed, while E-LL/HL/HH each succeeded 5/5. Its only non-success category was joint_violation. A1 and A2 also failed E-LH 5/5. The gap is therefore not just a missed train-cell recombination: it is an extrapolated combination of negative cabinet translation with positive large yaw. No failure trajectories were provided, so aggregate joint violations do not establish whether the originating error was reach, contact, or prolonged ineffective motion.
dependencies_preserved: Absolute world hand/handle/goal coordinates, yaw and both object quaternions are retained unchanged from A3; robot reach, table height and cabinet context are not discarded in pursuit of invariance.

Hand-handle offsets, previous offsets and relative motion appear in both world and cabinet coordinates. The learned typed contact edge uses the world version. Remaining handle-goal travel and its causal changes retain cabinet coordinates.
The current and previous aperture, individual hand and handle motion, and two whole causal observations are retained. Object2 alone is omitted because it is declared absent zeros.

Generated outcome channels are not used by an external planner or controller. Only jointly denoised action4 is decoded and executed. No future ground truth, development states, joint angles, contact force, simulator handle or extra obstacle source enters runtime.
No episode is routed by cell, yaw threshold, factor-sign rule or observed development label. The same smooth feature and target mappings apply to every layout.

evidence_refs.use: q3 score 0.875: C=1.0, E=0.75. E-LH=0/5; other E cells each 5/5. Five joint violations are the only non-success category. This identifies a residual layout dependence but does not reveal a failure trajectory or causal stage.
C=1.0, E=0.45; E-HH and LH zero successes, E-HL=4/5 and LL=5/5; eleven joint violations. Geometric canonicalization alone did not resolve extrapolation.
C=1.0, E=0.30; six joint violations and eight truncations. Current command-mode conditioning is not the strongest observed base for this revision.
Only the original exact D20 is used for all training-only outcome labels.
Explicit yaw, corrected handle observations and fixed native end-effector orientation motivate different frames for contact and articulation.
Handle stationary before pull; late hand-handle offset is nonzero with causal relative motion. Late LL offsets need not be treated as a universal cabinet-local contact constant.

HH late pull also has nonzero hand-handle offsets, with different components from the inspected LL late segment. These are not matched states and do not prove a mechanism; they support continuous rather than exact-contact supervision.
Robot approaching the cabinet from its world-fixed orientation.
Near-handle fixed-gripper geometry.
Drawer articulation and hand/handle relation during opening.
Another late opening frame shows the same nonrotating robot tool interacting with the drawer.
Compatible fixed-start frames, action4-first diffusion and causal inference separation.
Frozen update budget, common mask-normalized action loss and auxiliary target isolation.

expected_failure_signature: Primary falsifiable expectation: E-LH success improves without sacrificing the parent's successful E cells and C. If LH remains 0/5 with joint violations, separating contact and travel frames has not addressed the observed aggregate failure.

A trade-off is possible: the world contact edge may require the network to learn some yaw coupling for local actions; regressions in E-HH/HL/LL would show that the more specific frame factorization did not generalize overall.

No actual joint state is observed, so this model cannot enforce joint safety. Joint violations may remain even if contact prediction is improved, especially if the cause was world-reach extrapolation before contact.
Joint outcome generation may still hallucinate opening after lost contact. No outcome accuracy, failure timing or A4 success has yet been measured.

required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Unchanged from A3: encode xyz with R_z(chunk_start_yaw)^T, decode with the same R_z, preserve native gripper scalar. Frame remains fixed for all 16 actions. Native action units remain 0.01 m. No action clipping, damping, residual controller, stage-dependent decoding or use of predicted auxiliary channels in decode.
required_runtime_fields.architecture: A3's shared 11->64->32 SiLU typed-edge encoder and embedding product are retained. Contact edge now uses world current/previous offset and relative step delta; travel edge remains cabinet-local. Append a 9D raw cabinet-local approach bypass. Concatenate 27 raw relation dimensions, three 32D embedding/product blocks and 27 unchanged physical context dimensions. The common DP still has ten diffusion channels.
required_runtime_fields.scales: Exactly A3's physical scales: relative positions /0.1 m, observed step deltas /0.01 m, world coordinates centered at [0,0.6,0] /0.5 m. Orientation/aperture unstandardized. No new support-fit statistics or change to common normalization.
required_runtime_fields.source: causal_context.raw_history [B,2,41] and raw_current [B,41], exactly as in A3; no extra runtime fields

design.reusable_regularity: Retain A3's jointly modeled action/outcome structure and cabinet-aligned travel, but distinguish the contact relation from the drawer's articulation. Cabinet yaw rotates drawer travel; it does not rotate the robot's fixed native gripper. The hand-handle relation is therefore explicitly encoded and predicted in world axes, which are fixed relative to that gripper. Cabinet-local approach features are also retained as direct cues for cabinet-frame actions. This is a frame-factorization hypothesis, not an inferred contact state or a safety controller.
design.title: Separate fixed-gripper contact and cabinet-articulation frames in joint diffusion

training_only_targets.definition: Channels 4:7 in the full joint diffusion target are future_hand - future_handle in world axes, divided by 0.1 m. Channels 7:10 remain R_z(yaw_t)^T (future_handle - handle_t)/0.1 m. First four channels remain exactly encoded native action4. Only the contact-offset frame changes from A3; there are no additional targets. Invalid tail entries are zero-filled and auxiliary supervision is masked.
training_only_targets.loss: Unchanged 0.2 times auxiliary epsilon MSE over six outcome dimensions, numerator weighted by batch.mask and denominator mask.sum()*6 (floor 1 only for all-invalid auxiliary masks). Common action epsilon loss remains weight 1 and denominator mask.sum()*4.
training_only_targets.name: mixed_frame_outcomes
training_only_targets.runtime_isolation: At deployment ten channels start from host-owned Gaussian noise. Neither future labels nor masks are read by condition/denoise/encode/decode. No targets or caches are stored in deployment state.
training_only_targets.source: Exact current D_N obs[t+k+1,0:3], obs[t+k+1,4:7], obs[t,4:7], obs[t,39:41] for valid k only

design.architecture: condition[B,2,44], one unchanged common action4 U-Net, no added learned modules, no extra loss; public masked action epsilon loss weight 1 and denominator mask.sum()*4.

change_summary.change: New deterministic static-frame design. No parent, pretraining, performance feedback, learned action residual, auxiliary labels or optimizer changes.

design.coverage_gap: The exact 20-episode support contains ten LL and ten HH layouts, not the LH/HL cross-combinations or cabinet yaws of magnitude 33-37 degrees. Raw absolute handle/goal coordinates can encode the door_x/yaw correlation. Narrow-support standardization of cosine yaw would also magnify extrapolation. This design tests a deterministic geometry representation rather than an additional learned bottleneck.
dependencies_preserved: Absolute world hand, handle and goal positions remain explicit (meters divided by 0.5), preserving reach, table/world and robot workspace dependence rather than asserting full task equivariance.
Cabinet sine/cosine yaw remains explicit, preserving its relation to fixed world-oriented fingers, world action saturation and the robot.

Current and previous object quaternions xyzw are represented by two rotation-matrix columns in cabinet coordinates; this is sign-invariant and preserves the physical door orientation relative to its fixed cabinet.
Current/previous aperture and hand/handle displacements preserve contact and motion dependence. Only declared absent object2 zero channels are omitted.

Native action4 order and gripper semantics are unchanged. A single chunk-start Rz(yaw) is used for all sixteen action vectors. Encode is Rz(yaw)^T on xyz; decode is its inverse, no translation, scale change or candidate clipping. Gripper is never rotated. The host alone clips in the native world cube and executes four actions.

evidence_refs.detail: door__N20__rep0, exactly the listed twenty support episodes and no development states.
State41 schema, fixed native end-effector orientation, handle geom center, observed cabinet sine/cosine, LL/HH training and C/E gaps.
cell_counts HH=10, LL=10; initial interaction-to-goal distance is approximately 0.56054 m in the displayed demo_00 through demo_03 summaries despite differing world directions.
Robot, cabinet and handle sit in a shared world/table scene; no image-derived runtime channel is introduced.
Elevated hand near the closed-door handle supports retaining vertical contact error.
Door has rotated during pulling, motivating retention of dynamic object orientation separately from cabinet yaw.
Inspected obs rows 0-2, 35-40, 60-64 and actions 44-51: fixed initial handle followed by curved motion, descending approach, and changing action direction.
Frozen condition/action hooks and common mask/loss/control semantics.

expected_failure_signature: If geometry canonicalization is insufficient, E failures should concentrate at contact or world reach limits despite an approximately correct co-rotated approach.

The fixed finger orientation and axis-aligned native saturation break exact yaw equivariance. At large yaw the retained world context may still require unsupported interactions, causing glancing contact or loss of the handle.
No explicit stage supervision is used; a failure mode is premature pulling during descent or continued approach after contact. These are hypotheses, not observed evaluations.

required_runtime_fields.source: causal_context.raw_history[B,2,41] and raw_current[B,41], same public observations as B0

design.reusable_regularity: Approach/contact errors and the opening displacement should largely co-rotate with the cabinet. Rotate relative positions, pose axes, one-step displacements and action translations by the observed cabinet yaw. Use fixed physical scales rather than support z-scores for geometry and trigonometric channels. Supply both whole causal observations; native embedded previous state supplies one further displacement estimate. The U-Net alone learns the action distribution and stages.
design.support_fit: None. All feature scales are preregistered physical units, not statistics from another dataset. Common host normalization remains untouched but this representation uses the permitted raw causal context.
design.title: Cabinet-canonical diffusion with explicit world-context retention

design.architecture: 50 geometric features per observation, three separate 50->64->32 SiLU experts, invariant-only 36->32->3 gate, weighted embedding32, logits3. Concatenate to condition_dim85. Exactly one unchanged common action4 U-Net; all trainable modules participate in the common joint optimizer loss.

change_summary.change: New pre-feedback moving-chart and soft-contact-expert model with D_N-only low-dimensional support fitting and a masked stage auxiliary. Independently chosen initial candidate, not a repair or checkpoint of A1.

design.coverage_gap: LL/HH support entangles translation and cabinet yaw, and a single approach/pull representation may entangle distance-to-handle with progress around the door's curved path. C recombines the layout factors; E rotates the cabinet much farther than support. This candidate tests a moving articulation chart and causal stage specialization, not just static cabinet canonicalization.
dependencies_preserved: All actions are learned by the one common U-Net. No analytic tangent controller, rollout, planner, dynamics integration, desired path, reward or simulator joint value is used.

Fitted center/radius/rest direction are low-dimensional observed-support statistics, not runtime oracles. Circle residual, observed goal error and true handle pose remain inputs so the policy is not forced to trust an exact circular mechanism.

Explicit world hand, handle, goal positions and cabinet yaw retain fixed robot workspace, table/world and fixed-finger-orientation dependence. Cabinet x-axis and both current/previous object orientations in the moving chart retain door-versus-cabinet geometry and obstructions.

Aperture, its change, current/previous hand-to-handle error and hand/handle displacement retain approach/contact/motion dependence. All raw nonzero physical channels are represented; absent object2 zeros are omitted.

Frame x=(radial_y,-radial_x,0), frame y=(radial_x,radial_y,0), frame z=world up is orthonormal. Encode action xyz by its transpose and decode by its inverse using exactly the same chunk-start raw_current and fitted statistics for all 16 actions. No moving future frames, scale change, clipping or gripper transformation. Native action4 remains first and host clipping/execution semantics are unchanged.

evidence_refs.detail: All fitted statistics and coarse stage labels use only the twenty complete listed episodes.
Door object point is handle geom center, quaternions xyzw, cabinet sin/cos is common runtime data, no joint-angle or contact oracle is provided.

LL/HH counts 10/10; displayed initial handle-goal distances are constant while directions vary across the layout factors. This motivates trying a shared cabinet-relative geometric chart, not claiming an evaluated fit.

obs 35-40 show hand descending from z about 0.249 to 0.203 while handle is approximately fixed at z 0.150; obs 60-64 show the handle moving in both horizontal coordinates with changing quaternion. actions 44-51 include a transition into strong pulling.
obs 40-42 show a higher descending hand, nearly fixed handle, and different positive cabinet yaw. Stages should depend on geometry, not elapsed step.
Hand near closed cabinet/handle supports an acquisition phase distinct from opening.
Partially rotated door and hand near handle support articulation-relative representation.
Late opening pose shows a large panel rotation, not a free object translation.
Another listed support demonstration shows the late open-door geometry.
obs 113-114 maintain handle z near 0.150 and hand near handle, with still-changing horizontal position and orientation.
Support-fit state restoration and separate training-only target/loss hooks.

expected_failure_signature: If the fitted circle is not stable outside support, approach can be reasonable but the predicted pull will have incorrect radial/tangential components. Errors should grow with yaw or with radius residual rather than just translation.
The coarse moving-door label is not a true contact label. A hand that slips after opening begins could remain assigned to an opening expert, causing repeated tangential motion without recapture.

Soft stage specialization may learn an overly sharp acquisition transition; expected symptoms are premature pull or prolonged hovering near the handle. Fixed finger orientation at large yaw can also defeat a correct geometric chart.
These are preregistered hypotheses; no development success, learned fit quality or rollout results have been observed.

required_runtime_fields.source: The shared raw_history[B,2,41] and raw_current[B,41] only

design.reusable_regularity: The observed handle path is consistent with planar articulation about a fixed center relative to cabinet and goal. Fit one pooled circle to goal-relative handle positions after undoing observed cabinet yaw, using only current D_N obs[0:T]. At runtime reconstruct this empirical chart from goal and cabinet yaw, then define horizontal axes as clockwise tangent and outward radial at the current observed handle. This makes opening motion simpler in action coordinates. A learned three-way soft gate emphasizes approach, acquisition and moving-door experts, with coarse support-only stage supervision. The gate is a causal feature map, not an action controller or a hard state machine.
design.support_fit: One float64 least-squares algebraic circle fit to all D_N obs[:T] canonical handle-minus-goal xy points: [2x,2y,1] beta=x*x+y*y. Radius and mean normalized initial radial direction are derived from these same episodes. Store only center, radius, rest direction, count and radial RMSE as JSON; rebuild registered float32 geometry buffers after loading. No optimizer updates, external geometry constants, action regressors or additional data.
design.title: Support-fitted articulation chart with softly supervised contact experts

training_only_targets.inference: Labels never enter condition or denoise. The softmax gate is predicted from the first 36 invariant/current-motion/chart features, not absolute world layout, episode clock or a label cache.
training_only_targets.loss: 0.05 times cross entropy of the causal gate's last-history logits; weighted by mask[:,0] and divided by mask[:,0].sum().clamp_min(1). This window-level auxiliary is separate from the unchanged action epsilon loss with denominator mask.sum()*4.
training_only_targets.name: contact_stage
training_only_targets.source: Only support obs[t] and that support episode's obs[0]. Class 2 if handle has moved more than 0.015 m from its initial observed position; otherwise class 0 if planar hand-handle error exceeds 0.06 m or vertical error exceeds 0.12 m; otherwise class 1. Thresholds are preregistered coarse geometric labels, not measured contact or success.

design.architecture: Typed node input26 -> shared 64 ->24 SiLU encoder. Six directed messages share a (2*24+7)->64->24 encoder; each node averages its two messages and uses a shared 48->64->24 residual update. Three updated nodes concatenate with a 13-dimensional causal bypass to condition_dim85 per observation. One common U-Net has diffusion_action_dim10; all encoder and denoiser parameters participate in the joint loss. No separate stage head or support-fitted articulation model.

change_summary.change: New pre-feedback relational joint-diffusion model. Distinct from static-frame action canonicalization and moving-chart stage experts; no parent checkpoint, external pretraining, additional demonstrations or performance-driven edits.

design.coverage_gap: The 20 demonstrations cover correlated LL/HH layouts only. A flat state encoder may memorize an absolute hand/handle/goal configuration rather than transferable relations, and action-only imitation need not represent whether an action chunk acquires the handle or advances the door. This design tests shared relational computation and joint geometric outcome modeling, while deliberately retaining native world action coordinates.
dependencies_preserved: Every node includes its world position and cabinet-relative position, and messages include both world and cabinet-relative differences and distance. Thus robot workspace/world position is not removed by invariance.

The handle node includes current object orientation as two sign-invariant rotation columns and their change from the native previous quaternion. Cabinet and world-reference axes encode fixed-finger/world versus cabinet alignment. The hand axes are explicit world-reference axes, not a fabricated observed gripper quaternion.

Hand and handle one-step displacements, current aperture and aperture change retain motion/contact dependence. Direct bypass includes current/previous aperture and critical current contact/goal errors. Two whole causal observations are used, with their embedded previous fields.

Observed cabinet yaw, goal, panel orientation and relative hand position retain the provided obstacle/cabinet dependencies. The absent object2 zero channels are not treated as real entities. No unobserved obstacle channels are added.

encode_actions and decode_actions are inherited identity mappings: [world_dx,world_dy,world_dz,gripper], native 0.01 m xyz scale, no gripper remapping and no candidate clipping. The first four joint channels are exactly encoded native action4. Only the host clips and executes the fixed four-of-sixteen prefix.

evidence_refs.detail: Current D_N consists of exactly the twenty named door episodes; no development or other-task data.
Public state41 has hand, handle pose, previous counterparts, goal and cabinet yaw; fixed native world action4 and no second object. These determine the graph entities and frames.
10 LL and 10 HH demonstrations; raw gripper action mean 1 and std 0. This design nonetheless keeps gripper as a learned fourth action channel under the unchanged public loss, not an override.
Hand begins separated from handle; table, robot and cabinet remain relevant world geometry.
Near-handle elevated pose motivates a future contact-relation target, not only goal progress.
Hand and handle remain close while the door rotates: contact and object-goal progress are separate relations.
Late door configuration reinforces the need to encode physical panel orientation, not just a point target.
Inspected obs 0-2, 35-40, 60-64 and actions 44-51 show separation, descent, then coupled hand/handle motion; this motivates next-state relational labels.
obs 113-114 have close but nonzero hand-handle offsets while the handle approaches the goal. Future labels should retain full vectors rather than fabricated contact/success bits.
Joint diffusion first-four preservation, noise-target hook, per-action mask loss, training-only target isolation and inference sampling of all channels.

expected_failure_signature: Unlike the two frame-mapped candidates, this model must learn how world action direction varies with cabinet yaw. It may transfer relation recognition to C yet show systematically unrotated or under-rotated motion at extreme E yaws.

If joint geometric generation is inaccurate, apparently plausible future hand-handle proximity can accompany physically ineffective actions, causing glancing contact or repeated short pulls that fail to move the handle.

The graph's shared bottleneck may lose precise acquisition offsets or the auxiliary may compete with action denoising within the fixed update budget. This would appear as broad action/contact imprecision rather than a single circle-fit failure.
No failure rates or success rates have been measured in this design session. These are falsifiable expectations, not evaluation feedback.

required_runtime_fields.source: Only shared causal_context.raw_history[B,2,41]; raw_current is supplied by the host but action encode/decode need no context

design.reusable_regularity: Represent hand, handle and goal as three typed nodes. A shared node encoder and shared directed pairwise message encoder process both cabinet-relative and world geometry, followed by one shared residual node update. The same relation computation is reused across entities rather than learning unrelated per-coordinate interactions. Jointly diffuse the native action4 and six future hand-handle/goal-handle relative coordinates. Predicted future geometry can encourage coherent approach, sustained contact and opening progress through the ordinary denoiser, without a separate controller or a runtime ground-truth target.
design.support_fit: None. Feature/target scales are fixed physical units. Training labels are computed solely from the exact D_N and are not retained in deployment state. Common normalization/optimizer/split/budget remain frozen.
design.title: Relational hand-handle-goal encoder with joint future-geometry diffusion

training_only_targets.inference: The host initializes and denoises all ten channels using its fixed diffusion generator. Future geometry is generated jointly, never looked up or fed as clean conditioning. The executor discards the six auxiliary channels and uses only the native action4 prefix. No candidate sampling loop, planner, reranking or extra inference state is used.
training_only_targets.loss: Additional nonnegative 0.2 * sum(mask * (epsilon_geometry-noise_geometry)^2)/(mask.sum()*6).clamp_min(1). The host's first-four epsilon action loss stays weight 1 with denominator mask.sum()*4; it is neither diluted by six auxiliary channels nor rescaled.
training_only_targets.name: future_geometry
training_only_targets.source: For chunk start t and each valid action t+k, use support obs[t+k+1]. First three labels are Rz(yaw_t)^T(hand_next-handle_next)/0.1; last three are Rz(yaw_t)^T(goal_t-handle_next)/0.5. Goal and rotation are held at the causal chunk start, while next-state positions are training-only labels. Terminal obs[T] is valid for action T-1. Unavailable padded positions are zero and excluded by the same action-valid mask.

design.change_summary: Revision from actual parent A3 after q3 selection. Remove the redundant third relation; replace three 24-d tokens plus a 48-d fusion with two shared 16-d tokens and no fusion, reducing condition_dim 83 to 64. Replace 3D future handle displacement by its observed outward-axis scalar, reducing diffusion_action_dim 10 to 8. Retain 3D hand targets, cabinet action mapping, world dependencies, physical scales and joint-loss aggregate weight. This is one bundled compression hypothesis, not an isolated causal ablation of each change. A1-A3 remain immutable; no new checkpoint choice or performance-driven debug is performed.
design.coverage_gap: A3 has no observed development failures: C=20/20 and E=20/20 under the frozen score. This does not establish universal transfer or identify the causal source of its gain over A1 (E=11/20) and A2 (E=5/20). A4 tests whether the successful relational/joint prior can retain C/E coverage with less geometric and auxiliary redundancy, rather than claiming to repair an observed A3 failure.
dependencies_preserved: Full signed 3D hand-handle and handle-goal geometry, native-previous geometry and changes remain in the encoder. The omitted hand-goal edge is algebraically reconstructible, not an omitted physical entity.

The same 26-dimensional world bypass as A3 retains hand and goal world coordinates, world hand/handle displacements, both object xyzw quaternions, yaw, both apertures and heights. The current-edge bypass keeps all handle position components; scalar auxiliary projection does not remove transverse or vertical runtime handle information.

Fixed world gripper orientation, robot reachability, gravity/table height and cabinet-front layout remain available. The cabinet frame is only a compatible representation, not a claim of full robot rotation symmetry.
No obstacle oracle, simulator internals, planner, new demonstration, synthetic trajectory, action override or rule-based success detector is used. Absent object2 zeros alone are excluded.

evidence_refs.detail: Same exact ten demonstration identities for drawer__N10__rep0; no new support for the revision
Runtime yaw-corrected handle and sin/cos yaw; full present state schema; fixed world end-effector orientation
Initial handle-goal vector is aligned with (sin(yaw),-cos(yaw),0) in inspected LL and HH entries; LL/HH support only
obs 74-78: negative-x/negative-y handle movement consistent with outward axis and constant handle z=0.09 m; earlier 58-64 stationary handle despite hand descent
obs 74-78: positive-x/negative-y handle motion with sin/cos=(0.15293577,0.98823613), negligible cabinet-transverse displacement and constant z=0.09 m
Inspected actual near-handle pre-opening frame
Inspected actual extended-drawer frame supports distinguishing hand motion from drawer-axis progress

Frozen scores A1=0.775, A2=0.625, A3=1.0. A3 succeeds in every C/E cell; A1 E failures are concentrated in off-diagonal cells. These are aggregate outcomes, not inspected rollout failure states. A3 is selected by the prescribed rule.
evidence_refs.source: Revision-phase development_feedback message and q3 record_selection

expected_failure_signature: The compression hypothesis predicts retention of A3-like C/E success with fewer complete-system parameters and possibly lower fixed-method latency. No A4 performance or latency has been measured at design time, and the latency prediction is uncertain because the frozen U-Net dominates cost.
If the redundant third edge or learned fusion in A3 helps nonlinear contact representation, A4 may lose E off-diagonal robustness despite retaining the information algebraically.

Dropping transverse/vertical handle auxiliary channels may remove useful regularization. Failure could show adequate reaching but ineffective pulling, or renewed off-support joint violations; aggregate feedback cannot establish such mechanisms without rollout evidence.

Only successful support motion is available. As in A3, predicted axial movement may be optimistic when the fixed-orientation gripper slips. The revision does not assume its scalar imagined progress is physical truth.

required_runtime_fields.action_semantics: Retain A3 cabinet action4 at diffusion channels 0:4. Encode normalized native xyz by chunk-start R_z^T; decode with R_z using the same normalized observed sin/cos for all 16 steps. Gripper is untouched. No clipping or rescaling: host retains native world cube clipping, 0.01 m xyz scale, fixed end-effector orientation, 80 Hz and four-action execution.
required_runtime_fields.conditioning: Two typed 11-feature edges (3 current local coordinates, 3 previous, 3 causal changes, 2 role bits) share an 11-64-16 SiLU encoder. Concatenate the two tokens (32), six current-edge coordinates and A3's 26 world features: [B,2,64]. No separate learned fusion. Same physical scales as A3, no new support statistics.
required_runtime_fields.joint_inference: The one common factory U-Net denoises eight channels from host-owned noise. Auxiliary channels 4:8 are sampled, never supplied as future truth, and are discarded for execution. No planning, latent rollout feedback or substitution into causal conditioning.
required_runtime_fields.source: Only shared causal_context.raw_history [B,2,41], raw_current [B,41], learned weights and host-owned diffusion variables

design.reusable_regularity: The three entities form a chain: hand-to-goal equals hand-to-handle plus handle-to-goal, including their causal differences. Encode only the two independent typed edges. Support handle motion follows the observed drawer outward axis (sin(yaw),-cos(yaw),0), so model its future scalar progress jointly with full 3D hand displacement and cabinet action4. This keeps joint movement consequences while eliminating two nearly constant handle-displacement targets and the redundant edge/fusion representation.
design.support_fit: No additional fit statistics, weight reuse or cached labels. Empty deployment state. New seeded initialization and exactly one new fixed-budget training slot; all layers are registered in build_modules.
design.title: Compact two-edge joint diffusion with scalar drawer progress

training_only_targets.name: future_motion
training_only_targets.source: For window (episode,t) and valid j, three hand coordinates are R_z(t)^T*(obs[t+j+1,0:3]-obs[t,0:3])/0.1. The fourth is dot((sin(yaw_t),-cos(yaw_t),0), obs[t+j+1,4:7]-obs[t,4:7])/0.1. Frames and anchors use only obs[t]. Unavailable suffixes are zero padded.
training_only_targets.use: Append after encoded action4. Apply a separate auxiliary epsilon MSE with mask[...,None], denominator mask.sum()*4 and aggregate weight 0.2. The dimensional reduction intentionally changes per-auxiliary-coordinate weighting relative to A3's six-channel mean, but the public action loss remains completely unchanged at weight 1 and denominator mask.sum()*4.

design.architecture: Exactly one unmodified common conditional U-Net DP with condition_dim increased from 94 to 160 and diffusion_action_dim unchanged at 10. The single shared edge encoder remains 6->64->16 with SiLU. Its world-chart invocation reuses weights rather than creating a second encoder. All learned parameters enter the joint loss. Optimizer, seeds, update budget, DDIM schedule, control and splits are frozen.
design.change_summary: One feedback-driven revision of the q3 winner: add an explicit world-aligned relation/motion chart with raw and weight-shared learned features; condition_dim 94->160. Keep cabinet action frame, shared encoder architecture, joint ten-channel target, all physical scales and auxiliary weight unchanged. This tests a world-contact representation hypothesis, not a causal attribution of A3's advantage over the other non-ablated initial designs. New seeded training slot, not a new checkpoint or edit of A3. First implementation, with no interface repair or A4 performance feedback.
design.coverage_gap: Pre-feedback designs all achieved C=1.0, but their E rates differ: A1=.25, A2=.40, A3=.75. A3, the q3 winner, succeeds in all five E-HH, E-HL and E-LL episodes yet fails all five E-LH episodes. Its .875 development score is not evidence of full generalization. The remaining negative-cabinet-x/positive-yaw combination is a reason to revisit robot/world contact dependence, not to add a cell-specific controller.
dependencies_preserved: Retains every A3 runtime dependency: cabinet-frame hand-handle, goal-handle and goal-hand vectors and their one-step changes; direct edge bypass and shared embeddings; world current/previous hand/handle positions, goal, both quaternions, yaw and aperture history.

Adds the same three role-ordered relations and motions in the native world basis at .1 m relation and .01 m motion scales. World orientation is a genuine dependency because end-effector rotation is fixed; the two charts are not forced to produce identical learned responses.
Absolute world anchors and heights remain available for robot reach and table/cabinet dependence. The revision does not erase robot context to obtain a false whole-system symmetry.
No new raw information, obstacle oracle, joint state, planner, future inference truth or support retrieval is introduced. Only the declared absent object2 fields are omitted, as in A3.

evidence_refs.use: The exact five support episodes remain the sole data source for training targets. No additional demonstrations are added after feedback.
States fixed native end-effector orientation but varied cabinet yaw, plus world xyz actions, yaw-corrected handle, current/previous pose fields and matched raw observation access.
Three LL and two HH demonstrations cannot independently separate cabinet x and yaw, while the goal-handle axis rotates and initial distance is approximately .128 m.
Robot and cabinet occupy a common finite workspace; rotating the cabinet does not rotate the entire robot or gripper.
Hand-handle alignment is a local contact relation rather than just an absolute cabinet position.
End-of-demonstration relation of the world-oriented fingers and translated drawer handle.
Hand motion precedes actual handle translation, motivating preservation of both relation and motion edges.
Another yaw sign has hand and handle moving in world x and y; explicit dual charts are computed only from these same causal fields.

A1 score=.625, A2=.700, A3=.875 under equal-cell C/E weights. A3 E rates: HH=1, HL=1, LH=0, LL=1 with five episodes per cell. A3 aggregate failures are three joint violations and two native truncations. No development trajectories or frames were supplied, so these categories do not identify the contact mechanism.

evidence_refs.source: submitted A3 implementation in this session
evidence_refs.use: Actual parent: shared local edge encoder, joint ten-channel diffusion, action rotation, target definitions and loss normalization are retained; only the conditioning representation is extended.
One common denoiser, causal context isolation, independent native action4 epsilon denominator and permitted joint channels remain unchanged.

expected_failure_signature: The specific revision hypothesis predicts an E-LH gain without losing A3's E-HH/HL/LL or C successes. These are predictions for the one new slot, not measured A4 results.

If E-LH remains at zero, merely exposing world-aligned relative geometry was insufficient; a physical engagement or recovery limitation is still possible but cannot be diagnosed from the current aggregate feedback.

Duplicating coordinate charts could encourage shortcut learning of correlated world geometry. A drop in the previously successful E cells or C is an explicit falsification/risk, not a reason to repair after training.

Joint violations may persist because hand-position observations do not contain actual joint margins. This design is not a safety shield, simulator model or altered success rule. Additional condition channels may also increase fixed-method latency and parameter count.

required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Unchanged from A3: native action xyz is rotated by Rz(yaw_at_chunk_start)^T and decoded with its inverse for the entire sixteen-step chunk. Gripper is unchanged. No learned offset, rescaling, local cube clamp, phase-based action override or future frame. Host alone clips native actions, applies .01 m/native-unit control and executes four actions.
required_runtime_fields.condition: 160 features per each of two whole observations: A3's 18 local metric edge components, 48 local shared embeddings, 28 world/pose/aperture side components, plus 18 world metric edges and 48 world shared embeddings. Each edge is its relative vector followed by observed change. The same 6->64->16 encoder processes all six ordered edge/chart combinations.
required_runtime_fields.inference_auxiliary_channels: Six relation channels are generated jointly with action4 by host-owned DDIM noise/sampling. They are not ground-truth conditioning, do not choose a basis, and are never searched or executed as a plan.
required_runtime_fields.source: Shared causal_context.raw_history[B,2,41] and chunk-start raw_current[B,41], exactly as A3

design.reusable_regularity: Cabinet-relative geometry is useful for drawer translation, while fixed-orientation gripper interaction is naturally expressed in world-aligned relative coordinates. Supply both charts explicitly and reuse the same small relation encoder across both. This lets the common denoiser combine cabinet-axis action regularity with world-aligned approach/contact relations without first learning inverse rotation or subtracting weak absolute-position features from only five correlated layouts.
design.support_fit: No empirical support-fit state, retained training cache or pretrained weights. All fixed scales and the .25 auxiliary weight are exactly those of A3. Future labels exist only in the host training dataset. The host raw normalizer is unmodified; conditioning uses the same raw fields available to all methods.
design.title: Dual-frame relational charts for joint action-and-consequence diffusion

training_only_targets.definition: Unchanged A3 targets: first auxiliary xyz is R_start^T*(handle_next-hand_next)/.1 m, second is R_start^T*(goal_start-handle_next)/.1 m. Terminal next observation for the final real action is valid; invalid padded steps have zero targets and no direct auxiliary loss.
training_only_targets.loss: Unchanged A3 joint target order: encoded native action4 then six relation channels. Public action epsilon weight stays 1 with mask.sum()*4 denominator. Additional nonnegative relation epsilon loss weight .25 with its own mask.sum()*6 denominator and zero-mask guard. No motor-phase loss, extra target channel or future inference observation is added.
training_only_targets.name: future_relations
training_only_targets.source_fields: Exact D_5 obs[t+k+1,0:3] and [4:7] for each valid transition t+k<T; goal obs[t,36:39] and yaw obs[t,39:41] anchor the whole window.

action_frame_semantics.compatibility: An invertible causal affine reparameterization with orthonormal linear part; zero encoded horizontal residual corresponds to proportional reaching, not to a zero native action. b and R are evaluated once from the same start observation for every row. No future observation, predicted future frame, integration of actions, extra solver, learned gain at test time, or policy switching is involved.
action_frame_semantics.definition: Let R=Rz(yaw_start), r=R^T*(hand_start-handle_start) in metres, and b=(4*r_x,4*r_y,0) in unitless command units. For every k=0..15, encode u_xyz[k]=R^T*a_world_xyz[k]+b, u_gripper[k]=a_gripper[k]. Decode a_world_xyz[k]=R*(u_xyz[k]-b), a_gripper[k]=u_gripper[k].
action_frame_semantics.native_control: The coefficient 4 has units command per metre and only centers encoded actions. It does not replace native_xyz_scale_m=0.01, change control frequency, change xyz actuator mapping, alter vertical/gripper semantics, or change the native clipping cube. Encoded values may lie outside [-1,1]; the common unclipped diffusion schedule is preserved. Host alone clips the decoded world actions and executes four of sixteen.

design.architecture: Same as A1: condition_dim=33, diffusion_action_dim=4, exactly one unchanged common U-Net and no additional learned modules. Common masked action epsilon loss alone, weight 1 and denominator mask.sum()*4. Same normalization, 20,000-update optimizer budget and final EMA checkpoint rules.
change_summary: Single feedback-driven revision of q3 parent A1; A1-A3 are immutable.

Only substantive implementation change: add a horizontal hand-handle-error affine shift to cabinet-frame action encoding and subtract the identical causal-start shift before world decoding. Conditioning, architecture, vertical/gripper encoding and loss are retained.

Do not carry forward A2's learned edge/forecast modules or A3's chart/joint latent objective because neither improved the fixed overall development score. These are feedback comparisons, not claims isolating their causal effects.
No ensemble, per-cell routing, new demonstrations, extra optimizer runs, checkpoint search or performance-driven repair. This is a fresh A4 training slot with no inherited weights.
design.coverage_gap: The initial candidates all achieve dev_C=1.0 but extrapolation remains cell-dependent. A1, selected for q3, has dev_E=0.60, with E-LL 0/5, E-HH 3/5, E-HL 4/5 and E-LH 5/5. A3 has 0.55 and A2 0.25, so neither joint motion diffusion nor the learned world-action encoder provides an overall improvement. Same-sign extreme x/yaw layouts can place the handle much farther laterally from the fixed initial hand than the diagonal support does. The available feedback does not reveal failure-step states, so long-offset reach extrapolation is a hypothesis rather than an observed causal diagnosis.
dependencies_preserved: A1's 33 features are unchanged: metric local hand-handle separation and goal-handle displacement, observed hand/handle increments, aperture/change, world hand and goal, yaw sine/cosine, current/previous quaternions, and smooth near-contact features. All necessary robot/world/cabinet dependencies and two whole observations remain.

The residual shift depends on actual current hand and handle positions, not only a task label or yaw. Actual drawer movement and hand separation therefore continue to affect both conditioning and the invertible representation.
Vertical actions are not residualized because the evidence has a raise-then-descend stage change. Gripper remains a separate native scalar; neither channel is clamped or replaced by a fixed command.

The horizontal attraction is a representation offset, not the final policy: all four residual channels are still generated by the common DP. No action is overridden, selected by cell, clipped by candidate code, or produced by a second policy. The full inverse mapping exactly reproduces every encoded native action.
World position, gravity/height and handle orientation remain explicit because the native gripper/robot and table are not rotated with the cabinet. Absent object2 remains omitted as in A1.

evidence_refs.detail: Same two complete support episodes; no new demonstration, development trajectory or external data was used.
Shared causal hand/handle/goal/yaw channels, unitless native world xyz delta commands at 0.01 m scale, fixed end-effector orientation, and separate gripper command.

Diagonal LL/HH support with small x/yaw factors and substantially larger evaluation factors; two almost equal initial handle-goal lengths, so extrapolated reach rather than a new drawer travel law is a plausible coverage gap.

Paired read rows: t=0 hand-handle world xy error is approximately (0.057227,-0.129866), with a_xy=(-0.228907,0.519464); t=23 has error approximately (0.018560,-0.056636), with a_xy=(-0.074240,0.226546); t=62 has error approximately (0.003663,-0.007829), with a_xy=(-0.014652,0.031316). These support the chosen common gain of four command-units per metre. Pull actions from t=65 differ, so residual outputs must remain learned and unconstrained.
Raised approach makes a blanket vertical proportional residual less well motivated than a horizontal-only one.
Descent near the handle; keep the successful A1 vertical conditioning and encoding intact.
Low contact/pull phase requires learned residual commands, not a replacement reach-only controller.
Open drawer at the end of the second support, with hand and handle retaining an offset.

A1 score 0.800, A3 0.775, A2 0.625 under equal C/E weighting. A1 is q3. All have C=1.0. A1's 50-episode aggregate failures are 3 joint violations and 5 truncations; these categories are not localized to a particular cell or phase in the provided feedback.
Only causal chunk-start context may enter action mappings; no candidate clipping; common action epsilon objective and execution semantics remain fixed.

expected_failure_signature: Primary prediction: retaining A1's conditions while centering horizontal reach commands should improve long-offset extreme layouts, especially its failed E-LL cell, without sacrificing crossed-cell success. A lower or unchanged E score would not support this residual-extrapolation hypothesis.

If A1's extreme failures are predominantly fixed-gripper contact geometry rather than reaching, this change can bring the hand to the handle yet still truncate with little observed drawer progress. No failure-step state was available to rule that out.
The causal-start bias is fixed for all sixteen actions. At distances requiring rapid hand movement its approximate finite-horizon residual can overshoot during the four-action executed prefix.

During a missed pull, the horizontal reach-error shift may oppose the learned pull residual or return the hand toward the stationary handle. That can prevent runaway motion but also stall or yield repeated re-approach; reduced joint violations are not assumed.
An action residual near zero during support approach is easier to transfer only if the unchanged conditioning does not still learn an off-support shortcut from world/yaw fields.
