design.reusable_regularity: Preserve A1's complete conditioning and single action4 U-Net, but move a simple horizontal hand-to-handle error dependency from what the network must extrapolate into an invertible action representation. In the paired support rows during approach/descent, native a_xy is approximately 4*(handle_xy-hand_xy). Encode local horizontal actions after adding 4 times the local hand-minus-handle error at the chunk start. The denoiser then learns residual commands, including pulling and finite-horizon deviations, while the inverse representation reinstates the known linear error dependence at long reach distances. This is a continuous, cell-independent affine mapping, not a staged controller, planner or mixture of previously trained candidates.
design.support_fit_statistics: No runtime fit or cached support statistics. The new fixed coefficient 4.0 is an explicit representation hyperparameter grounded in read action/observation pairs from this exact D_N, not a gain obtained from extra data or performance search. No learned modules are initialized outside build_modules and no old weights are imported.
design.title: Horizontal reach-error residual diffusion in the cabinet frame

design.change_summary: Initial scientific design: deterministic metric cabinet-frame relations and orthogonal action mapping, with explicit world dependencies. No predecessor, no measured feedback and no pretraining.
design.coverage_gap: The exact ten demonstrations contain five LL and five HH layouts, but no LH or HL layouts. Extrapolation also requires yaw magnitudes of 33-37 degrees rather than 5-10. Raw coordinate normalization risks entangling cabinet translation, orientation, reach phase and opening progress.
dependencies_preserved: World hand and goal xyz remain explicit, together with cabinet sin/cos yaw, so the world positions of the handle and prior hand/handle are recoverable from the relative features and motion differences.
Current and previous gripper aperture are retained. Fixed end-effector orientation is not rotated; cabinet yaw and world coordinates preserve its relation to the cabinet and workspace.

Two quaternion rotation columns encode full current orientation up to the irrelevant quaternion sign; their previous-to-current differences retain causal angular motion. Cabinet pose, goal-relative handle location and orientation continue to describe the door obstacle and its evolving sweep.
Only declared absent object2 zero channels are omitted. Both whole observations are independently represented. Native history reset repetition remains valid.

evidence_refs.fact: Current evidence is door__N10__rep0, exactly ten complete support episodes and sixteen real frames.
Observed cabinet sin/cos yaw, handle geom center, xyzw quaternions, fixed native end-effector orientation and world action4 semantics; train LL/HH and C/E gaps.

Five LL and five HH; examples demo_00 and demo_01 have distinct world reach and goal directions but the same 0.56054 m initial handle-to-goal distance. Gripper action is constant +1 in support but is still learned, not clamped.
Initial hand offset from closed cabinet and handle.
Hand near handle on a partly swung door; cabinet remains a physical obstacle.
Hand is approaching the handle from above on the other training layout.
Late opening configuration, not just translation toward a free-space point.

Hand first rises and descends while the handle is nearly stationary, followed by handle motion and changing orientation. Motivates relative height, separate hand/object differences and geometry-based rather than elapsed-time conditioning.
Single common DP, 2x37 conditioning, causal chunk-start reversible action mapping and unmodified public action epsilon loss.

expected_failure_signature: At large yaw the fixed-orientation fingers may require non-equivariant contact offsets not covered in support: a plausible approach followed by failure to engage or sustained handle slip would falsify sufficiency of the static canonical representation.

The static frame does not explicitly straighten the rotating handle trajectory. Wrong pull direction or early stopping after initial door motion would indicate unresolved articulation/stage ambiguity.
World side channels could still be used as spurious layout proxies; a strong LH versus HL asymmetry would be evidence of that limitation. These are predictions, not measured outcomes.

required_runtime_fields.action_frame: For all 16 steps, xyz_encoded=Rz(yaw_at_chunk_start)^T xyz_native. Decode with Rz(yaw_at_chunk_start). Native dimensionless xyz still scales by 0.01 m per control; no centering, scaling or rotation of gripper. No candidate clipping; host clips world action cube and executes four steps.
required_runtime_fields.source: causal_context.raw_history [B,2,41] and raw_current [B,41] only

design.reusable_regularity: Express hand-minus-handle, handle-minus-goal, hand and handle finite differences, and sign-invariant handle orientation columns in the observed static cabinet yaw frame. Rotate the action translation into the same frame. This makes rigidly transformed local manipulation relations easier to reuse without assuming global robot equivariance. Metric feature scales, rather than small support yaw/height variances, prevent artificial amplification outside support. The 37-dimensional deterministic representation is the only addition to the frozen DP; no learned encoder or auxiliary objective is used.
design.support_fit: None. Physical scales in config are design constants; no statistics from other demonstrations, evaluation states or future deployment observations.
design.title: Cabinet-canonical relations with a world-anchor side channel

design.change_summary: Initial independent design: data-fitted articulated frame and causally gated learned stage encoding, in contrast to a static cabinet-coordinate representation. Uses only the common action epsilon objective; no auxiliary loss or postprocessing controller. No performance feedback has been used.
design.coverage_gap: Only LL/HH are demonstrated. The missing combinations and large yaw extrapolations require transferring both contact acquisition and a rotating constrained pull. The hand-to-handle vector is insufficient to distinguish being above a stationary handle from pulling an already moving handle.
dependencies_preserved: The fitted center is not an oracle or a runtime hinge field: it is a constant relation estimated only from observed support handle/goal positions and cabinet yaw. Runtime handle, goal and cabinet yaw determine each current frame.

World hand and goal coordinates, cabinet yaw and moving-frame world direction remain explicit. Robot workspace constraints and fixed end-effector orientation can therefore break nominal rotational symmetry.

Current and previous aperture, sign-invariant orientation columns, hand motion and handle motion are retained. Door orientation, residual radius, opening progress and goal relation preserve the moving obstacle/contact dependencies.

Stages are soft, nonexclusive and recomputed from each causal observation. They neither depend on elapsed time nor disable the direct geometry path. Both whole observations are independently represented. Only absent object2 zero fields are removed.

evidence_refs.fact: Exactly ten current support episodes; no dev or test states.

Handle geom center, xyzw orientation, goal xyz and static cabinet sin/cos yaw are observed; cabinet translation/yaw are the factors. Native xyz actions are world deltas and end-effector rotation is fixed.
Five LL/five HH. Demo_00 and demo_01 have the same initial handle-goal distance despite different world directions; support gripper action +1 is not used as a hard-coded output.

Handle height remains approximately 0.150036 while xy and quaternion change through opening; hand descends from above a nearly stationary handle, and pull action begins around 45. Late handle y first decreases then increases, consistent with a curved rather than straight trajectory.
Different world handle/goal positions and cabinet yaw in HH; motivates fitting geometry only after removing the observed rigid transform.
Closed cabinet and initially offset hand.
Partly rotated door with hand at the handle.
Above-handle acquisition geometry differs from late pulling.
Large visible door swing motivates an articulated frame.
Support fitting and JSON restoration precede build_modules; action frames must be reversible and frozen at chunk start.

expected_failure_signature: A noncircular handle path or a changed hinge-goal relation would give large radius residual and wrong tangent actions; approach may work while the pull pushes radially or slips.

At large yaw the fixed fingers may need contact geometry not captured by a soft proximity stage. Oscillation between descent and contact, or pulling before engagement, would falsify the adequacy of these stage variables.

A circle-canonical representation can extrapolate mechanics without extrapolating robot reachability; errors concentrated at workspace-extreme layouts would expose this limitation despite retained world channels.
The frame is fixed for sixteen predicted steps, not recomputed with future truth. Rapid rotation within the four executed steps may induce late-pull lag. These signatures are unmeasured predictions.

required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Infer center_world=goal+Rz(cabinet_yaw)*center_local. Frame x is the observed horizontal handle-minus-center unit vector, y is its counterclockwise tangent, z is world up. Encode xyz by frame transpose; decode by frame. The frame is from raw_current at chunk start for all sixteen actions. Gripper stays native, xyz retains native 0.01 m scale; only the executor clips world action4 and executes four steps. Degenerate radius uses cabinet x rather than any future observation.
required_runtime_fields.source: Only causal_context.raw_history and raw_current plus restored support geometry constants

design.reusable_regularity: A hinged handle traces a planar circle. Fit its center in cabinet-canonical, goal-relative coordinates from the exact support. At runtime compute the observed handle radius direction and its orthogonal tangent; predict translation in that moving frame, held fixed over the chunk. Represent radial residual and opening sin/cos, full relative geometry, causal motion and orientation. Three small learned encoders are smoothly weighted by planar hand alignment and relative height (approach, descent, contact/pull). This is a learned conditional prior, not a scripted action controller or planner. The unmodified DP receives 42 direct features, three soft stage weights and a 32-dimensional mixed learned encoding.

support_fit.algorithm: For p=Rz(yaw)^T(handle-goal), least-squares fit [2*p_x,2*p_y,1] dot [c_x,c_y,k]=p_x^2+p_y^2 over all support rows. Radius=sqrt(k+c_x^2+c_y^2); z center is mean p_z. Closed direction is mean normalized initial p_xy-center. Store these JSON constants, observation count and radial RMS residual, then register geometry buffers in build_modules. No action labels, expert source, success rules, rewards or simulator internals are needed.
support_fit.normalization: Fixed physical feature scales, not support standard deviations; no future truth used to update deployed geometry.
support_fit.scope: Only this D_N obs[0:T] and initial obs[0]

design.title: Support-fitted radial/tangent frame with soft causal manipulation stages

design.change_summary: Initial independent scientific design: learned role-shared relational message passing and joint state-action diffusion with identity native action frame. No fitted hinge, explicit stage gates or pretraining. No measured performance feedback has been used.
design.coverage_gap: Ten diagonal-cell demonstrations do not independently cover cabinet translation and yaw, nor recovery from missed contact. An action-only learner can memorize a reach/descend/pull script without representing when the handle actually follows the hand. A fitted hinge and fixed stage thresholds are additional assumptions that this candidate deliberately avoids.
dependencies_preserved: Native world action coordinates are unchanged. The gripper is always the fourth native scalar, and fixed end-effector orientation is not treated as a rotatable translation.

Explicit world hand, handle and goal positions and cabinet yaw are present both through graph node attributes and a direct bypass. Cabinet-relative relations do not erase reachability, world cube saturation or fixed-finger alignment dependencies.

Current and previous gripper aperture, hand/handle finite differences and full handle orientation up to quaternion sign preserve causal contact and door motion information. Only the declared absent object2 zeros are omitted.

Door/cabinet dependencies are represented by observed handle pose, goal and cabinet yaw rather than hidden body poses or collision geometry. The design assumes this shared observation is sufficient; it obtains no simulator internals.

Message passing is per observation and both complete observations are returned to the common two-step conditioner. No future label, stage target, timestep-in-episode or valid mask enters condition or denoise.

evidence_refs.fact: The same ten complete current support episodes supply all supervision; there is no evaluation data in the bundle.
Native action4/world control, fixed orientation, handle geom center, current/previous state and observed cabinet yaw; factor coverage is only LL and HH.
Five demonstrations per training cell, saturated translation actions and constant +1 demonstrated gripper. The output gripper is nevertheless learned with the unmodified common action loss.

Early hand motion while the handle is static, then handle motion during pulling. Separate future hand and handle displacements can supervise this change in coupling without providing a phase label at deployment.
Different world positions and cabinet yaw produce another initial spatial relation under otherwise shared task semantics.
Initial separated hand and handle.
Above-handle descent geometry.
Hand remains by a handle on the opened door.
Another demonstration shows hand/handle interaction during visible door swing.
Another demonstration shows approach from above rather than straight displacement to the final goal.
Joint diffusion is allowed when encoded native action4 occupies the first four channels; future supervision is restricted to training_targets/diffusion_targets/training_loss.
The host fixes action epsilon weight 1 and mask.sum()*4 normalization, and inference initializes all joint channels from the host generator without labels.

expected_failure_signature: World actions require learning rather than enforcing the yaw dependence. Good C performance but failed contact/pull at extreme yaw would show that dual-frame features and relational weight sharing did not suffice for rotational extrapolation.

Auxiliary future motion can learn an optimistic handle trajectory from successful demonstrations. Repeated pulling with a stationary handle after missed contact would falsify the intended coupling benefit.

The larger joint denoising problem may hurt action fidelity under the fixed budget. Across-cell degradation rather than only OOD errors would indicate auxiliary competition/underfitting, not evidence that the task is nonrelational.

A three-node graph has no explicit moving obstacle mesh. Collision during descent despite accurate coarse hand/goal geometry would expose insufficient contact detail. All these outcomes are predicted, not measured.

required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Identity native world xyz and gripper for encode/decode. Output first four joint channels only; no candidate clipping, action offsets, scaling, rollout, planning or auxiliary-based execution correction. The executor clips world action cube, applies native 0.01 m xyz scale and executes four of sixteen actions.
required_runtime_fields.inference_auxiliary: Six latent future displacement channels are jointly generated from diffusion noise. They never contain ground-truth future states at inference and are discarded by the executor.
required_runtime_fields.source: causal_context.raw_history [B,2,41]; inherited identity action mappings require no additional context

design.reusable_regularity: Use hand, handle and goal as three role-labelled nodes with shared pairwise message functions. Nodes contain world positions, cabinet-canonical goal-relative positions, causal motion, gripper attributes and sign-invariant handle orientation/history. Directed edges carry both world and cabinet-relative position differences, relative motion and distance. Two shared residual message rounds form a 64-dimensional learned relational encoding, alongside 40 direct causal features. Jointly diffuse native world action4 followed by six cabinet-frame future hand/handle displacement channels. Predicting both moving entities should encourage distinguishing free hand movement from coupled pulling, without a hard-coded stage machine. The auxiliary channels are generated with the action by the common U-Net; they are never interpreted by a planner or a controller.
design.support_fit: No fitted statistics or external weights. Fixed metric scales; future arrays exist only in the host training dataset. Deployment state is the inherited empty JSON object plus normal registered learned weights and role/adjacency buffers.
design.title: Role-structured relational graph with joint hand/handle motion diffusion

training_only_targets.causality: The label array is returned from training_targets, not cached on the design. No support labels, masks or future frames are accepted by condition/denoise/identity decode. All modules are registered in build_modules and optimized only by the common joint loss.
training_only_targets.loss: Append six clean targets after action4, use the frozen joint diffusion noise process, and add 0.2 * sum(mask * squared_auxiliary_epsilon_error)/(6*mask.sum()). Denominator is clamped to at least one only for an all-invalid batch. The host's action4 epsilon loss remains unchanged, separately normalized and weight one.
training_only_targets.name: future_displacements
training_only_targets.padding: Unavailable tail entries are zero placeholders; auxiliary loss uses the same per-action valid mask, with its own six-channel denominator. The final obs[T] is used only as the valid outcome of action T-1.
training_only_targets.source: Exact D_N obs[t+k+1,0:3] minus obs[t,0:3] and obs[t+k+1,4:7] minus obs[t,4:7], for k=0..15 with valid native actions. Both differences are rotated by observed cabinet yaw at chunk start t and divided by 0.1 m.

design.change_summary: Initial scientific design: deterministic cabinet chart, sign-invariant attitude, direct geometric conditioning, orthogonal action mapping; factory U-Net and action epsilon loss are unchanged. No performance feedback used.
design.coverage_gap: D_5 has 3 LL and 2 HH episodes and no crossed position/yaw cells; yaw extrapolation is roughly +/-35 degrees rather than the observed -6.17 to +7.63 degrees. A raw-state policy can associate cabinet translation, yaw and phase. Near-constant yaw cosine also has a very small support standard deviation.
dependencies_preserved: World hand, handle and goal positions, their previous positions, and cabinet sin/cos remain explicit. This is not full SE(2) invariance: fixed robot orientation, world action cube, table height and reachability can still matter.

Current and native-previous hand/handle relative vectors, full physical handle attitude, gripper apertures and causal finite differences are retained. The two whole input observations are encoded separately.

Cabinet placement and yaw plus handle pose retain the available cabinet/panel obstacle dependence. No unobserved collision geometry or hidden hinge state is queried. Object2 channels are omitted only because the schema declares them absent zeros.

Raw41 slices, xyzw handle quaternion, observed yaw39:41, world displacement control and correlated layout distribution.
3 LL/2 HH; 542 transitions; yaw cosine std about 0.00170; hand-to-interaction distances about 0.21-0.31m.

expected_failure_signature: If gripper/panel contact is not yaw-equivariant, initial approach may improve yet the hand can slip or collide during pulling, especially at the two yaw extremes.
The world escape path may still memorize the correlated training layouts: a persistent C gap despite canonical relative features falsifies the intended decorrelation benefit.
Without explicit phase supervision, lowering may occur too early or pulling may begin before contact. This should appear as a stationary handle with a moving hand rather than steady opening.

required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Encode action xyz as Rz(cabinet_yaw_at_chunk_start)^T times native xyz. Decode with Rz, retaining native 0.01m control units. All 16 steps use the same causal frame. Gripper is unchanged. No local clipping or rescaling; executor alone clips the decoded world cube and executes four steps.
required_runtime_fields.normalization: Use raw values with contact scale 0.1m, span/world scale 0.5m, one-step motion scale 0.01m, unit attitude/yaw/aperture and 0.1 aperture-difference scale; common normalized history is deliberately replaced.
required_runtime_fields.source: causal_context.raw_history [B,2,41] and raw_current [B,41]; no additional runtime fields

design.reusable_regularity: Hand-to-handle corrections and the handle-to-goal displacement can be described in the observed cabinet yaw frame. Use a direct, nonlearned 53-dimensional chart per observation and express translation actions in that same yaw frame. No fitted action rule or waypoint is added. Two rotation-matrix columns replace xyzw quaternions, removing antipodal ambiguity without losing physical attitude. Fixed metric scales avoid amplification of nearly constant support coordinates.
design.support_fit: None. Metric scales are representation choices, not estimates from other data.
design.title: Cabinet-chart diffusion with an explicit world-context escape path

design.architecture: Exactly one unchanged factory DP at condition_dim=46, diffusion_action_dim=4; no extra learned modules or auxiliary losses. Fixed public action epsilon loss and mask denominator mask.sum()*4.
change_summary: Initial scientific design: deterministic cabinet-frame representation and reversible cabinet-frame action rotation, with explicit world bypass. No performance feedback used.
design.coverage_gap: D_N contains only two episodes, one LL at door_x 0.03763 m and yaw -6.17 degrees, one HH at 0.06858 m and 7.63 degrees. The crossed translation/yaw combinations and roughly +/-35 degree yaw are absent. Empirically standardizing the near-constant cosine channel (support std approximately 0.00153) would greatly magnify extrapolated yaw.
dependencies_preserved: World hand and goal positions, world hand-handle and goal-handle vectors, and cabinet sin/cos remain explicit: fixed robot orientation, workspace anisotropy, and cabinet obstacle orientation are not assumed invariant.
Current and native-previous hand/handle positions determine local motion and contact-relative history; both whole causal observations are used.

Handle quaternion orientation is retained by two independent rotation columns, both current and native previous. Goal and handle heights and gripper aperture are retained. The declared absent object2 zero slots are omitted, not substituted by privileged geometry.

evidence_refs.use: Exact two-episode support scope and no development evidence.
World delta action semantics, xyzw handle quaternion, observed cabinet yaw, missing object2, LL/HH coverage.
Layout values, cosine standard deviation, 220 transitions, handle-to-goal distance 0.56054 m in both layouts; motivates bounded physical feature units.
Cabinet face, handle, fixed robot/world geometry at approach.
Approach above the handle rather than a straight goal-directed reach.
Contact and partial opening; relative contact geometry matters.
Large articulated opening and retained fixed cabinet obstacle.
Handle stationary during above-handle approach, then movement with changing quaternion; native history supplies causal increments.
Similar near-handle interaction in the HH demonstration.

expected_failure_signature: If canonical geometry is insufficient to disentangle phase from only two demonstrations, the hand should arrive above the handle but descend or start pulling prematurely.
At large yaw, success can still fall because the gripper orientation and native clipping cube are world-fixed; the bypass retains this dependency but its learned correction has little support.
A cabinet-frame command does not directly encode the evolving hinge tangent, so later opening may drift from the handle even if approach generalizes.

required_runtime_fields.action_frame: For all 16 actions, encode xyz as Rz(cabinet_yaw_at_chunk_start)^T times native world xyz; decode with Rz in the same fixed chunk-start frame. No translation, gain, local clipping or gripper rotation. Native xyz unit remains 0.01 m per unit and gripper remains action[3]. Only the host clips the decoded native cube and executes four actions.
required_runtime_fields.conditioning: 46 deterministic features per whole observation; history two. No runtime hidden state, planner or external call.
required_runtime_fields.source: Only causal_context.raw_history [B,2,41] and raw_current [B,41], supplied from shared deployment observations; common normalized history is accepted but raw-derived metric geometry is used instead.

design.reusable_regularity: Relative hand-handle and handle-goal displacements and translation commands rotate together with a cabinet. Expressing these relations in the observed cabinet frame removes a needless requirement to learn coordinate rotation from two layouts. Use fixed metric scales, not empirical yaw standardization. Quaternion first and third rotation columns are sign-invariant and retain the full handle orientation. This design leaves stage discovery entirely to the common U-Net; it imposes neither a fitted hinge nor predicted future-state diffusion.
design.support_fit: None. All scales are declared physical representation hyperparameters; no statistics outside this D_N or additional normalization fitting.
design.title: Cabinet-aligned contact geometry with a world-context bypass

design.change_summary: Initial independent design: support-estimated kinematic circle, moving radial/tangent action chart, and learned soft geometric regime experts. Unlike a fixed cabinet-frame chart this factors opening progress through a hinge estimate. No performance feedback or action planner; common DP and action epsilon loss unchanged.
design.coverage_gap: Only five demonstrations of a curved handle path are available, with cabinet position and yaw correlated. The same opening angle occurs at different world coordinates, and unseen yaw values should change the tangent direction without changing the underlying hinge constraint. Support also has a visible approach/lower/pull progression that should not be represented by an episode clock.
dependencies_preserved: World hand, handle, goal and previous hand positions are explicit, and handle motion retains previous handle position. Fixed gripper/world orientation and reachability are not quotiented out.

Cabinet yaw, cabinet-relative radial direction, signed goal angular relation, current and previous full 6D handle attitudes, current/previous gripper aperture and radial fit residuals remain available. Deviations from the fitted circle are not projected away.

Observed goal and yaw anchor the fitted cabinet pivot; handle pose retains panel orientation and location. No obstacle planner, environment state or runtime hinge oracle is accessed. Absent object2 zeros are omitted.

evidence_refs.detail: Statistics limited to the five identified complete support episodes.
Goal, handle pose and cabinet yaw are shared runtime fields; action is world translation with fixed gripper orientation.

3 LL/2 HH; handle z is fixed in support; initial handle-to-goal distance is the same about 0.56054m in all five episodes. This motivates testing a shared de-yawed geometry, not claiming its correctness outside support.
Closed panel and spatially separate robot before approach.
Hand above handle before the opening motion.
Panel rotates while the hand follows the handle.
Partially opened panel and contact in the second layout.
Large late opening angle rather than a pure translation.
Obs rows 0:4,33:38,50:56,73:76 show stationary handle during approach followed by planar curved motion with changing quaternion; actions50:56 show pulling.
fit_support statistics and deployment restoration; chunk-start-only action mapping.

expected_failure_signature: If the goal-to-pivot offset is not rigid across reset yaw/translation, extrapolated frame directions will be wrong even when the predicted radial/tangent actions match support; handle-relative radial errors or stalled/slipping pulls should appear.
Near the pivot the polar chart is ill-conditioned. A deterministic cabinet-axis fallback ensures finite values but does not solve that representational failure.
If soft experts learn a clock proxy or collapse to one expert, transitions from lowering to pulling may be premature or delayed on unfamiliar initial reach distances.
An accurate local hinge model cannot remove fixed-gripper contact anisotropy, world-cube clipping, table or arm reach limitations. E failures can remain after successful C decorrelation.

required_runtime_fields.action_frame: At chunk start, reconstruct pivot XY as goal XY plus Rz(yaw) times the fitted center. Unit radial points from pivot to observed handle; tangent is positive CCW, z is world z. Encode xyz with the transpose of this orthogonal basis, decode with its inverse, in unchanged native 0.01m units. The basis is frozen for all sixteen actions, not updated with future truth. Gripper remains identical, and only the common executor clips in world coordinates.
required_runtime_fields.normalization: Fixed physical scales: contact 0.1m, world/span 0.5m, per-step motion 0.01m, circle residual 0.05m; unit angular, aperture and attitude features. No narrow support-variance scaling.
required_runtime_fields.source: raw_history [B,2,41] and raw_current [B,41] only, plus frozen support circle statistics

design.reusable_regularity: Fit a shared planar circle to observed handle-minus-goal positions after de-yawing each observation. Its center is a support-estimated pivot offset, not a simulator field. Express control and hand/handle errors in radial, positive-CCW tangent and vertical axes at the current handle. A 54D geometry chart, a learned softmax mixture of three 32D experts, and the three gate probabilities give 89D conditioning per observation. The experts can specialize in approach, lowering and opening, but no semantic assignment or hard switch is imposed. They learn only through the common diffusion loss.

support_fit.deployment: Restore JSON before build_modules; register the fitted center as a buffer. Retain no observations, actions, windows, paths or future labels.
support_fit.procedure: Concatenate cabinet-frame XY handle-minus-goal points p, solve [2px,2py,1] times [cx,cy,k] = px^2+py^2 by numpy least squares. Store center, mean radius, radial RMS and row count as JSON. RMS is an auditable support statistic, not an evaluation score. No numerical fit quality is claimed before host fitting.
support_fit.sources: Every current D_5 obs[0:T], excluding final obs[T], using only handle4:7, goal36:39 and yaw39:41; no action fitting and no extra episodes.

design.title: Support-fitted hinge chart with causal soft regime experts

design.architecture: Three 37->64->24 SiLU MLPs, mixed by deterministic positive soft phase gates; one unchanged common factory DP, condition_dim=80 and action_dim=4. All encoder parameters are trained only through the common epsilon action loss, weight 1 and denominator mask.sum()*4. No auxiliary loss. Complete system is subject to the public 3x B0 cap.
change_summary: Initial independent scientific design: support-fitted articulation model, moving polar action coordinates, and softly stage-specialized learned representation. Unlike cabinet-only A1, this imposes a circle prior and explicit phase structure. No performance feedback or post-training edits.
design.coverage_gap: Only two cabinet layouts are supported, and their translation and yaw are correlated. The images and observations contain a substantial within-episode change in door orientation, but almost no independent across-layout variation. A Cartesian trajectory learner may confound opening angle, interaction stage and cabinet pose.
dependencies_preserved: The fitted center is a representation estimate from support observations, never a simulator hinge channel. Runtime center is goal + R(cabinet_yaw) * fitted_offset; goal, cabinet translation and rotation remain coupled correctly.

The radial frame is not treated as a complete symmetry: world hand and goal coordinates, cabinet and radial world orientations, cabinet-relative contact and handle-goal vectors all bypass the phase experts into DP.

Current and native-previous hand and handle positions, apertures, and both full quaternion orientations as first/third rotation columns are represented. Both whole causal observations are used. World z is not rotated away.

The fixed cabinet obstacle is represented by goal anchoring, cabinet yaw and contact/cabinet relations; there is no collision-free planner. The gripper's world-fixed orientation and native clipping cube remain relevant through the bypass and native execution.

evidence_refs.use: Exact two complete demonstrations; support fitting restricted to them.
Articulated door task, handle center and xyzw orientation, observed cabinet yaw, goal field, native action semantics and LL/HH split.

Handle height is constant in these episodes and initial handle-goal length is identical despite translation/yaw change; supports testing a planar rigid-geometry prior rather than memorized world trajectories.
Above-handle alignment stage.
Door begins rotating while the hand stays at the handle.
Large final opening about a cabinet-fixed hinge; motivates a moving radial frame.
Similar low interaction configuration in the other layout, at a different demonstration time.
Corresponding open-door geometry in HH.
Stationary handle during approach, then changing planar position and quaternion; action transition around the low hand configuration motivates soft geometric stages.
Hand-height/contact relations are observable without episode time or stage labels.

expected_failure_signature: If a goal-anchored common circle offset is not stable across extrapolated resets, the polar frame should be systematically misaligned even while the observed hand-handle error is small; late opening should drift or stall.

Phase gates use metric heuristic widths, not observed contact force. Premature low-height activation can cause pulling before a secure hook, while strong opening evidence can keep the opening expert active after contact is lost.
At large yaw the fixed gripper and anisotropic world action cube can violate approximate radial/tangential regularity; the world bypass may not learn enough correction from N=2.
A fixed chunk-start radial frame lags a rapidly turning door later in the 16-step prediction; frequent four-step replanning reduces but does not remove this error.

required_runtime_fields.action_frame: At chunk start compute estimated center from goal and cabinet yaw; ex is the normalized horizontal center-to-observed-handle vector, ey is its counterclockwise tangent and ez is world vertical. Encode xyz by the transpose of this orthonormal basis and decode by the same frozen basis for every horizon index. Degenerate radial norm uses cabinet axes. Gripper is unchanged. No action gain, planner, native clipping or future-frame update is introduced; host clips after decode and executes four of sixteen.
required_runtime_fields.conditioning: 37 intrinsic features, 16 world/cabinet bypass features, three soft phase weights and a 24-dimensional weighted learned phase embedding, totaling 80 per observation. No elapsed-time counter or persistent rollout stage state.
required_runtime_fields.source: Only causal_context.raw_history [B,2,41] and raw_current [B,41], plus the serialized D_N-fitted geometric constants; normalized input history is accepted but metric raw geometry is used.

design.reusable_regularity: A rigid revolute door constrains its handle to an approximately planar circle. Fit the circle in goal-relative cabinet coordinates from this exact D_N, then express hand-handle errors, motion and native action translation in instantaneous radial/tangential coordinates. Opening angle becomes an observed geometric quantity rather than elapsed demonstration time. Three learned feature experts are smoothly mixed from causal alignment, height and departure from the closed radial direction, distinguishing approach, descent and opening without selecting a hard action program.

support_fit.algorithm: Transform handle-goal xy by observed cabinet yaw inverse. Per episode solve least squares [2*x,2*y,1] beta = x*x+y*y; center=(beta0,beta1), radius=sqrt(beta2+center dot center). Equal-average per-episode centers and radii. Fit closed radial direction from each episode's first observed handle, normalize the averaged direction. Center z is the goal plane, not an inferred hinge height.
support_fit.deployment: JSON stores only center offset, radius, closed radial unit vector, support counts and fit scope. build_modules registers corresponding float32 buffers; fresh load restores before module construction. No trajectories or action table are stored.
support_fit.source: Each exact D_N episode obs[0:T], not terminal obs[T]; native actions are not used to fit geometry.

design.title: Support-fitted articulation coordinates with soft causal approach/descent/opening experts

design.architecture: Three 19D typed nodes -> shared48D encoder; two rounds of 106->96->48 edge messages and 96->96->48 residual node updates with LayerNorm; ordered144->96->64 readout; concatenate43D skip for107D per-observation conditioning. One common U-Net with diffusion_action_dim10. All learned modules are created only in build_modules and participate in joint loss.
design.change_summary: Initial independent scientific design: learned typed message passing plus training-only joint future-motion denoising, retaining native world actions. Contrasts with explicit cabinet/hinge action charts without inheriting them. No development feedback used; common optimizer, update budget, U-Net architecture rule and action loss unchanged.
design.coverage_gap: Five successful support trajectories provide many coupled hand/handle motion observations but little independent position/yaw coverage. A single flattened-state regressor may learn the correlated layouts rather than the changing hand-to-handle and handle-to-goal relationships. The stationary handle during approach and moving handle during pulling supply useful training-only physical supervision without external labels.
dependencies_preserved: The direct skip retains current/native-previous hand and handle world positions, goal world position, yaw, both gripper apertures and full sign-invariant 6D current/previous handle attitudes. The graph does not replace all information by a translation-invariant average.

Typed nodes and ordered node readout preserve the difference between robot, movable handle and goal. Directed pair features retain motion and displacement signs. Hand and goal attitude slots are zero placeholders, not invented measurements; type codes identify their roles.

World positions, world edge vectors and native world actions retain fixed robot/gripper, gravity/table height, reachability and cube-saturation dependencies. Cabinet yaw and full handle pose retain all declared panel/cabinet information. Object2 is omitted because it is declared absent.

evidence_refs.detail: Exactly the five current D_5 episodes, no other task/N evidence.
Raw41 fields, causal two-observation history, native world action cube and fixed EE orientation.

542 transitions; initial hand-to-handle distances vary about 0.21-0.31m; all gripper actions equal 1 but physical aperture and hand motion vary. Gripper remains a learned native action channel rather than a hardcoded output.
Hand, handle/cabinet and goal have distinct spatial roles.
Hand moves toward/above the stationary handle.
Hand and handle move together during opening.
Different layout with hand-panel interaction during pull.
Later opening configuration supports using future handle displacement as a training-only target.
Obs0:4 and33:38 have a stationary handle with moving hand; obs50:56 and73:76 have coupled but unequal hand/handle displacement. This motivates separate auxiliary motion channels.
Joint diffusion retains action4 first; extra supervision may use support future states but never inference conditioning.
Host action loss uses mask.sum()*4; auxiliary losses are separate; deployment denoises joint channels then decodes only action4.

expected_failure_signature: World action coordinates require learned direction composition. If the relational encoder cannot extrapolate the yaw dependence, C may improve while E shows systematically wrong pull directions or excessive world-cube saturation.
Generated future motion is not a dynamics oracle. The denoiser may hallucinate moving handles while actual contact fails, causing confident repeated pulls at a stationary handle.

Extra channels and message passing may overfit five trajectories or spend capacity modeling motion rather than action. Worse C and E despite coherent support motion would falsify the intended auxiliary benefit.
The world-context skip can reintroduce position/yaw confounding. Persistent crossed-cell asymmetry is a predicted warning sign rather than evidence for an invariant graph policy.

required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Identity encode/decode for native [world_dx,world_dy,world_dz,gripper], including 0.01m xyz units. Auxiliary motion is cabinet-frame, but action4 is not rotated, normalized or overwritten. Only the public executor clips decoded world actions and executes four of sixteen.
required_runtime_fields.normalization: Fixed world/goal-relative position scale0.5m, edge scale0.25m, contact skip0.1m, causal step motion0.01m and unit attitude/aperture/yaw. No fitted mean/std, no clipped observations.
required_runtime_fields.source: Only raw_history [B,2,41] and raw_current [B,41] from the common causal context; neither labels nor masks enter condition or denoise.

design.reusable_regularity: Represent hand, handle and goal as typed nodes. Two rounds of shared directed-edge message passing use both world and cabinet-relative displacements, distance and relative causal motion. A learned 64D relational readout augments a 43D geometric/world skip. Jointly diffuse native world action4 followed by six future cumulative hand/handle displacement channels in the chunk-start cabinet frame. Sharing the denoiser across action and observed effects encourages coherent contact/motion representations. There is no fitted circle, hard stage rule, auxiliary planner or forced action rotation.
design.support_fit: None. training_targets produces a returned training-only tensor dictionary; no labels or raw trajectories are retained on the design. Default empty deployment state is sufficient.
design.title: Typed relational encoder with joint action and hand/handle-motion diffusion

training_only_targets.inference: No future truth, target cache or mask at runtime. Host initializes all ten diffusion channels from its generator and denoises jointly; auxiliary sampled channels are discarded, never used as a planner or supplied externally.
training_only_targets.loss: Append after unmodified encoded native action4. Auxiliary epsilon squared error on channels4:10, multiplied by mask[...,None], summed and divided by max(mask.sum()*6,1), weight0.25. Host native action epsilon weight1 and denominator mask.sum()*4 remain untouched.
training_only_targets.name: future_displacement
training_only_targets.padding: Edge-repeat obs[T] only for padded indices. Common valid-action mask determines all valid auxiliary elements; obs[T] is a legitimate next-state target for the final valid action.
training_only_targets.source: For support window (episode,t) and k=0..15, take obs[min(t+k+1,T),0:3]-obs[t,0:3] and obs[min(t+k+1,T),4:7]-obs[t,4:7]. Rotate both differences using observed yaw39:41 at t only and divide by0.1m.

design.architecture: Three typed nodes with 26 input features, shared 26->64->24 node encoder. All nine directed edges use 13 geometric features plus sender/receiver embeddings, a shared 61->64->24 message MLP, learned scalar softmax attention over senders, and shared 48->64->24 residual node update. Flatten three 24-dimensional nodes plus 28 explicit features to condition_dim=100 per observation. Exactly one unchanged common DP at diffusion_action_dim=10. All learned modules participate in the joint public-plus-auxiliary loss; full system remains under the public 3x B0 capacity check.
change_summary: Initial independent scientific design: shared relational message passing and jointly generated future contact/motion channels, with native-world actions. No fitted circle, explicit phase gates, extra demonstrations, pretraining or performance feedback.
design.coverage_gap: Two LL/HH demonstrations provide many approach/contact/opening transitions but almost no independent layout combinations. Pure action imitation can memorize the layout-correlated path and miss the distinction between a nearby hand and a hand that actually moves the handle. There are no failure/recovery demonstrations or large-yaw examples.
dependencies_preserved: Each node has world position, cabinet-relative goal displacement, motion, and node identity; handle nodes additionally have full current/native-previous orientation represented by two rotation columns, and hand nodes have current/native-previous aperture.

Directed edges carry current and native-previous relative positions, relative motion and distances in cabinet coordinates, plus world displacement. Robot/world anisotropy, cabinet yaw and fixed-gripper effects are not removed.

A deterministic 28-feature geometry bypass retains explicit hand-handle and handle-goal relations, hand and handle motion, aperture, cabinet yaw, world hand/goal positions and handle pose. Both whole causal observations are processed.
The cabinet obstacle remains located/oriented through goal, observed handle pose and cabinet yaw. No obstacle oracle, collision planner, simulator hinge field or absent object2 state is introduced.

evidence_refs.use: Exact two-episode evidence scope; no development states or measurements.
Identical causal raw fields, world translation actions, fixed native rotation, handle geom center and allowed xyzw/yaw inputs.

One episode per observed cell, 105 and 115 transitions, constant gripper command and substantial translational variation; interaction phase must be inferred from geometry and motion rather than action-gripper labels.
Separated hand and handle with fixed cabinet and goal/world context.
Hand aligned above stationary handle; mere xy proximity is not yet opening.
Interaction produces handle and door motion.
Hand remains related to the moving handle late in opening.
A corresponding approach in the second layout.
Comparable open-door outcome in HH.
Observable hand/handle motion changes across the interaction; motivates future contact-relative and object-displacement labels from complete support observations.
Near-height hand motion and emerging handle motion are distinct causal quantities.

expected_failure_signature: Joint diffusion can learn spurious future handle motion from only successful demonstrations: an action chunk may assume contact before the real handle moves, causing low-yaw/IID competence but failure to recover after a miss.
Without a radial action-frame prior, large-yaw extrapolation can still rotate translations incorrectly despite the relational features. Native world-action output intentionally tests this limitation.

The six auxiliary channels may compete with scarce action data or propagate erroneous generated geometry into denoising. If this dominates, both approach precision and opening consistency may degrade rather than improve.
Learned edge attention may collapse to world layout identity instead of contact/goal relations because N=2 does not independently cover those factors.

required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Identity encode/decode inherited from CandidateDesign. The first four joint channels are exactly native world_dx, world_dy, world_dz, gripper, with native xyz scale 0.01 m and unchanged gripper actuator semantics. Only the host clips the native cube and executes four of sixteen actions. The appended geometry uses the observed fixed chunk-start cabinet frame, not a future frame, and is never decoded into a planner/controller.
required_runtime_fields.inference: Conditioning is strictly causal. The host's single common diffusion generator initializes all ten channels; the same U-Net jointly generates actions and auxiliary geometry over 16 DDIM steps. No ground-truth future observation or training mask is read at inference; predicted geometry is discarded after sampling and only action4 is executed.
required_runtime_fields.source: Only causal_context.raw_history [B,2,41] and raw_current [B,41] from common observations. Normalized history is accepted; the representation uses metric raw fields with declared fixed scales. No fitted geometry or runtime state cache.

design.reusable_regularity: Use shared learned directed relation messages among hand, handle and goal, rather than treating every raw coordinate as an unrelated scalar. Contact-relative displacement and handle motion are reusable outcomes of actions. Jointly denoising these future geometric quantities with native action4 may make the action model represent contact-to-motion causality and distinguish approach from opening without a hand-coded hinge or stage partition. This is a learned relational/outcome prior, not a fitted articulation model.
design.support_fit: No additional support-fit statistics. Future training labels are constructed from only the exact D_N windows and are not stored on the deployed design. Deployment state is empty; all learned modules and fixed node-identity buffer are reconstructed in build_modules and restored by host checkpoints.
design.title: Relational hand-handle-goal encoder with joint action/contact-dynamics diffusion

training_only_targets.loss: Append after untouched encoded action4. Additional loss = 0.2 * sum(mask * squared auxiliary epsilon error)/(mask.sum()*6), with a denominator floor of 1 for the empty-mask case. Fixed common action epsilon loss remains weight 1 with denominator mask.sum()*4, not diluted over ten channels. No unmasked auxiliary regression or modified action loss.
training_only_targets.name: future_geometry
training_only_targets.padding: Invalid tail labels are zero; no index beyond terminal obs[T] is read. The common action validity mask supplies all auxiliary loss validity, never conditioning.
training_only_targets.source: For support window starting at t, horizon k=0..15 uses obs[t+k+1] only when the corresponding action exists. First three channels are future hand_xyz - future handle_xyz, rotated by cabinet yaw at obs[t] and divided by 0.1 m. Last three are future handle_xyz - handle_xyz at obs[t], in that same chunk-start cabinet frame, divided by 0.2 m.

design.architecture: Condition features: contact3 + goal-error3 + hand-displacement3 + handle-displacement3 + aperture2 + full-orientation-chart current3/previous3 + world-hand3 + cabinet-yaw2 =25 per observation. Exactly one factory action4 U-Net, no additional modules, common action epsilon weight1 and denominator mask.sum()*4. The host performs a fresh fixed 20,000-update training slot and final EMA evaluation.

change_summary.change: Based on the completed A1-A3 feedback and q3=A1. Remove A1's redundant previous relative-position vectors, explicit world handle/goal copies and aperture-difference feature; replace each six-column orientation encoding by a three-coordinate full-orientation chart. Change condition44 to condition25, preserving A1's static cabinet action map and all physical observation dependencies. This is one new scientific training slot, not an edit or checkpoint selection for A1. A2/A3 negative E results remain recorded; their extra mechanisms are not inherited.

design.coverage_gap: The same exact N20 LL/HH support leaves C combinations and extreme E cabinet yaws unobserved during training. Development now shows A1 at 1.00 C and 1.00 E, versus A2 at 1.00/0.90 and A3 at 1.00/0.60. A1 is already at the observed score ceiling, so the revision tests whether its cabinet-frame bias can retain transfer with less representational redundancy, fewer complete-system parameters and potentially lower fixed-method latency. It does not invent a failure mechanism to explain aggregate truncations.
dependencies_preserved: Let R=Rz(cabinet_yaw), u=hand-handle in cabinet coordinates and v=goal-handle in cabinet coordinates after undoing feature scales. Then handle_world=hand_world-R*u and goal_world=handle_world+R*v. Keeping world hand and yaw therefore preserves absolute robot/world/goal geometry even though direct world-handle/world-goal copies are removed.

From cabinet hand/handle displacement vectors dh,do: previous_hand=hand-R*dh and previous_handle=handle-R*do. Previous relative errors in A1 are recoverable by linear arithmetic. Both current and previous apertures remain explicit and determine aperture change.

Each current/previous xyzw object quaternion is normalized, left-multiplied by inverse cabinet yaw, and assigned a deterministic w>=0 hemisphere. Store p=q_xyz/(1+q_w). The inverse is q_xyz=2p/(1+dot(p,p)), q_w=(1-dot(p,p))/(1+dot(p,p)); multiply by cabinet yaw to recover world orientation. Thus the full physical orientation is preserved up to quaternion double cover, not reduced to a guessed hinge angle. Exactly w=0 uses a deterministic vector-component sign convention.

World hand position and cabinet sine/cosine remain direct features, retaining workspace, table/world and fixed-finger alignment dependence. Physical panel orientation and relative geometry preserve the supplied door/cabinet obstacle dependencies. Only declared absent object2 zeros are omitted.

Native actions retain exactly A1's mapping: xyz encode=Rz(yaw_start)^T native_xyz, decode=Rz(yaw_start) encoded_xyz. This is one fixed chunk-start frame for every one of the sixteen predictions. No scaling, action offset, clipping, learned controller, gripper transformation, future frame or executor modification. Host still clips native world action4 and executes four actions.

evidence_refs.detail: A1 C=20/20 and E=20/20, all C/E cells at 1.0; A2 E LL=3/5 with two native_truncated episodes; A3 E HH=0/5 and LH=2/5 with eight native_truncated episodes. A1/A2/A3 frozen-rule scores are 1.00/0.95/0.80. These bundled changes do not isolate a causal effect of action frame, graph or auxiliary loss.

Measured fixed-method latencies: A1 0.1375758955036872 s, A2 0.12381885749346111 s, A3 0.1228789985034382 s. A1 has 4,732,484 parameters and the fewest parameters among those three but is not the fastest measured. Reducing A4 dimensions is only a latency hypothesis; the frozen measured latency tie-break, not a parameter proxy, will govern selection.
Selected A1 as the unique C/E-score maximizer; neither IID nor training loss nor faster losing candidates were used to override the score rule.
Same door__N20__rep0 twenty demonstrations, no additional support or development-state reads.
Static cabinet yaw, world hand/handle/goal positions, full current/previous xyzw orientation, fixed native gripper orientation and action cube require preserving frame and world dependencies.
Robot and fixed table/world context must not be discarded while canonicalizing layout.
Dynamic panel rotation motivates retaining full current/previous orientation despite compacting its representation.
Previously inspected obs 0-2, 35-40 and 60-64 distinguish approach/descent from handle motion; h-handle, goal-handle and displacement features remain direct.
Previously inspected obs 113-114 retain small contact offset late in opening; the direct hand-handle vector is not compressed away.
One common U-Net, condition per whole observation, causal action frames, unchanged optimizer and mask-normalized action epsilon loss.

expected_failure_signature: Information preservation does not imply equal learnability. If redundant A1 features supplied useful shortcuts, A4 can have poorer acquisition or late-pull precision despite retaining enough information to reconstruct them. Any loss of C/E success disproves the useful-compression hypothesis for this slot.

The hemisphere orientation chart has a discontinuity at a relative rotation of pi. A rollout approaching that boundary can exhibit abrupt conditioning changes even though the physical orientation changes smoothly. Unlike a planar-angle simplification it retains tilt, but is less globally smooth than A1's rotation columns.

With no A1 development failures, no success improvement can be inferred in advance. Matching the observed ceiling on these finite episodes is not evidence of perfect population success. Fewer condition coordinates also may not lower measured latency because U-Net convolutions dominate.
If A4 ties A1 on the fixed C/E score but is slower, it will not be chosen merely because it has fewer parameters. No checkpoint search, new seeds or extra training will be used to repair this result.

required_runtime_fields.source: Shared causal_context.raw_history[B,2,41] and raw_current[B,41] only

design.reusable_regularity: World hand position plus cabinet-relative hand-handle error, goal-handle error, hand/handle displacements and cabinet yaw suffice to reconstruct all current/previous positions. Explicit redundant copies of those positions/errors and the aperture difference need not be supplied separately. A sign-canonical unit quaternion can also be expressed by three modified Rodrigues parameters without dropping tilt information. Keep the successful parent's static cabinet action frame and physical feature scales while reducing condition_dim from 44 to 25.
design.support_fit: None. Retain A1's fixed 0.1 m contact, 0.5 m scene and 0.01 m displacement scales. No other-dataset statistics, chart fit, pretraining, auxiliary loss, trainable feature encoder or weights transferred from the parent.
design.title: Compact sufficient cabinet chart: redundancy-reduced revision of A1

design.change_summary: Initial scientific design: 53 deterministic per-observation features, one unchanged common action4 U-Net, fixed common epsilon loss weight 1 with mask.sum()*4 denominator, no additional losses. No structural repairs or performance feedback at authoring.
design.coverage_gap: The exact N20 support is 10 LL and 10 HH episodes; peg_y and box_y are correlated. LH/HL require independent reaching and transport corrections, and E extends both coordinates. Absolute-coordinate marginal normalization alone need not expose those separate errors.
dependencies_preserved: World hand and goal coordinates scaled by 0.5 m retain robot reachability, the table/world placement and the box location; no whole-scene translation or rotation invariance is assumed.
Signed world x/y/z errors preserve the fixed box insertion axis and gravity. Goal-relative yz distance is only an added feature, not a controller or collision-free claim.
pegHead minus pegGrasp, both current/previous object quaternions, hand/object displacements, aperture and its change preserve tool geometry and causal grasp/slip information.
Native previous hand/object states are recoverable from current coordinates and differences. Object2 channels are omitted only because the public schema declares object2 absent with zeros.

evidence_refs.use: Exact peg-insert-side__N20__rep0 support boundary and 20 episode identities.
Source slices, pegGrasp vs pegHead semantics, absent object2, native world action4 and LL/HH versus C/E split.
cell_counts=10 LL/10 HH; inspected demo_00 through demo_05 summaries show different peg and box coordinates and nearly constant object quaternion.
Actual frame shows separated peg, gripper, tabletop and side-opening box.
Actual frame shows acquisition at the peg rather than at the box goal.
Actual frame shows held peg directed toward the box opening.
Observed approach, aperture closure, tool transport and changing lateral/vertical corrections; initial head-grasp offset about [-0.13,0,-0.01] m.
HH starts with a different hand-to-peg lateral sign while the box-to-peg lateral displacement remains negative.
Frozen common DP, conditioning and action/mask interfaces.

expected_failure_signature: If separate metric errors are insufficient, missed grasps should depend less on box_y than transport failures, while reversed lateral-transfer C/E layouts can still fail because negative transfer errors dominate support.
The ungated U-Net may interpolate incompatible reach and carry actions near closure, producing premature translation or dropped pegs.

Fine tanh features saturate by design; if the network ignores their accompanying linear errors, far E layouts may stall. World coordinates remain available, so layout shortcuts are reduced in salience but not prohibited.

required_runtime_fields.action_semantics: Identity encode/decode. Channels 0:3 remain world dx/dy/dz with 0.01 m native scale and channel 3 remains the gripper scalar. The public executor alone clips to [-1,1], executing four of sixteen actions.
required_runtime_fields.normalization: Explicit physical metric scales, not fitted range clipping. No support statistics, extra runtime observations, clock, stage oracle or future labels. The host's normalized history is not used in this representation.
required_runtime_fields.raw_history: [B,2,42] from causal_context only; use current hand 0:3, gripper 3:4, pegGrasp 4:7, quaternion xyzw 7:11, previous hand 18:21, previous gripper 21:22, previous pegGrasp 22:25, previous quaternion 25:29, goal 36:39 and pegHead 39:42 in each of the two observations.

design.reusable_regularity: Represent hand-to-pegGrasp and pegHead-to-goal separately in world metric coordinates. Give the fixed U-Net linear signed errors for long-range extrapolation and tanh errors at a 3 cm scale for local alignment, plus observed motion and distances. The grasp and insertion sites have different physical roles. This is an action4-only deterministic representation, with neither stage gating nor an auxiliary objective.
design.title: Two-site multiscale metric relational diffusion

design.change_summary: Initial independent scientific design: shared 21->64->32 relation MLP, 18->48->16 world MLP, 21->48->4 causal phase MLP, 119-dimensional per-observation conditioning and one unchanged common action4 U-Net. Add only masked phase cross entropy; common epsilon action loss remains weight 1 / (mask.sum()*4). No structural repairs or performance feedback at authoring.
design.coverage_gap: Only diagonal LL/HH demonstrations couple peg and box positions. A monolithic representation can use box_y as a proxy for where to grasp and peg_y as a proxy for where to transport. Acquisition and insertion also occupy different observation/action regimes despite continuous raw coordinates.
dependencies_preserved: World hand and goal positions remain direct conditioning channels as well as inputs to the world encoder; box placement, robot workspace and gravity are retained.
No coordinate rotation is imposed: signed xyz edge vectors, source/target heights and yz alignment preserve the fixed insertion axis.
Both role streams remain nonzero (gate floor 0.15), including during uncertain closure, so box/obstacle context is not removed in an early stage.

Aperture and previous aperture, current/previous xyzw object quaternions, observed hand/peg displacements and the head-grasp offset retain temporal/contact/tool dependencies. Carry-edge source motion uses pegGrasp displacement as a translation proxy; the two actual pegHead history positions and orientation information remain in conditioning through the two relation inputs.
Object2 is omitted because the public schema declares it absent. There is no inferred box simulator state or runtime contact flag.

evidence_refs.use: Exact N20 source boundary, with no other support or evaluation states.
LL/HH versus C/E coverage, world action/control semantics, site names and state slices.
10 LL/10 HH support; inspected episode summaries show aperture minima around 0.293 and gripper action extremes -1 and +0.6.
Actual frame shows the gripper approaching the peg away from the box.
Actual frame shows the low acquisition configuration, distinct from insertion.
Another actual support frame shows the gripper at the tabletop peg.
Actual support frame shows the peg held near the side opening.
Aperture declines from 0.825 at t40 to 0.346 at t51; transport actions begin near t51, followed by yz alignment. This motivates a coarse 0.36 aperture proxy, not a contact/success threshold.
Different hand-to-peg lateral relation in HH despite the same reset hand.
Learned modules in build_modules; future/label isolation and auxiliary interface.
Training-only named targets, current-window mask and unchanged action epsilon objective.

expected_failure_signature: If aperture is an unreliable holding proxy off support, predicted carry probability may rise for an empty grasp; expected result is transport without the peg or a premature retreat from acquisition.
If the learned phase classifier uses correlated goal position instead of local closure geometry, closure timing will change across C cells even at a similar hand-to-peg state.
The soft gate may still blend acquisition and transport near a transition; early box motion or delayed insertion is the falsifiable boundary failure.
World skips deliberately prevent false invariance but can retain layout shortcuts. Edge-weight sharing may underfit the role-specific distinction between grasp approach and side insertion.

required_runtime_fields.action_semantics: Identity encode/decode: world dx/dy/dz with 0.01 m native scale plus untouched scalar gripper; public clipping and four-of-sixteen execution only.
required_runtime_fields.causal_stage: All four logits and probabilities are predicted solely from each causal observation's geometry, finite differences and aperture. No labels, episode ID, time index, masks or future states enter condition/denoise.
required_runtime_fields.normalization: Fixed 0.1 m relation/height and 0.5 m world scales; displacements divided by native 0.01 m. No support-fitted deployment state or weights outside the joint optimizer.
required_runtime_fields.raw_history: [B,2,42] causal_context raw_history. Each row uses hand 0:3, aperture 3:4, pegGrasp 4:7, quaternion xyzw 7:11, previous hand 18:21, previous aperture 21:22, previous pegGrasp 22:25, previous quaternion 25:29, goal 36:39 and pegHead 39:42.

design.reusable_regularity: One learned edge encoder is shared between hand-to-pegGrasp and pegHead-to-goal relations, with explicit role tags. A small causal four-phase classifier softly gates the two relation embeddings and their direct metric errors. It learns open approach, closure, transport and lateral/vertical alignment proxies from the same demonstrations. A separate world encoder and direct world skips preserve constraints outside local relations. This is a learned conditional representation, not an expert switch or multi-policy controller: all actions still come from one common action4 diffusion U-Net.
design.title: Causal role-sharing encoder with softly supervised control phases

training_only_targets.inference: No label cache and no training mask at runtime; predicted phases alone condition the DP.
training_only_targets.loss: 0.15 times cross entropy on predicted current-observation phase logits, reduction none, multiplied by batch mask[:,0], divided by its valid-start sum clamped to one. Nonnegative and separately normalized. No new loss on the action predictions and no action reweighting.
training_only_targets.name: control_phase
training_only_targets.shape: One integer label per chunk-start window.
training_only_targets.source: For each (episode,t) from exact D_N, native actions[t,3] and obs[t] only: class0 if gripper command<0; otherwise class1 if aperture>0.36; otherwise class2 if norm(goal_yz-pegHead_yz)>0.035 m; otherwise class3. These are coarse control-phase proxy labels, not successful-contact or evaluator-success ground truth.

design.change_summary: Initial independent scientific design: 55 deterministic chart/world features per observation, a single common U-Net with ten joint diffusion channels, invertible chunk-start yaw action mapping and a masked six-channel outcome objective. No stage gating, additional learned encoder, structural repairs or performance feedback at authoring.
design.coverage_gap: The diagonal support covers only a narrow family of negative lateral peg-to-box displacements. C and especially E change both transport distance and horizontal direction, including lateral sign. Action-only imitation can also confuse moving the empty hand with successfully carrying the peg.
dependencies_preserved: The chart is a coordinate change, not an assertion of arbitrary task rotation symmetry: raw world hand and goal coordinates, world xyzw current/previous quaternions, world heights, world yz pegHead-goal errors, and the chart cosine/sine remain conditioning inputs.
The fixed world x insertion axis is recoverable in chart coordinates as [cosine,-sine,0]. World gravity remains chart z. The robot workspace and box placement are not discarded.
Separate pegGrasp and pegHead positions, their difference, hand/object finite differences and current/previous aperture preserve grasp geometry and motion coupling.

All translations in both history observations and all sixteen action/outcome steps use one frame derived only from the latest chunk-start observation. Predicted future tool states never define a new frame.
Object2 is omitted only under the declared absent-zero schema. No simulator geometry, contacts, reward, success flags or collision-free path information are requested.

expected_failure_signature: An excessive learned rotation-invariance bias would produce diagonal approaches into the box face instead of final world-x insertion, especially in large-lateral-offset E cells. Retained world-axis features are intended to prevent, not guarantee against, that failure.
Because the chart depends on the goal even during initial acquisition, poor handling of world-axis metadata could reintroduce box-dependent grasp errors across C layouts.
Outcome/action coupling may be wrong after a missed grasp: generated tool motion can remain optimistic while the actual peg stays on the table. A repeated empty-hand carry is the observable failure.
Ten joint diffusion channels increase modeling burden at the same optimizer budget; auxiliary fitting can hurt action fidelity near closure or short terminal windows.

A near-zero horizontal head-goal displacement makes the heading poorly determined; the deterministic world-axis fallback is finite and invertible but may cause a chart discontinuity. Inspected support keeps a substantial horizontal separation through the reported late rows.

required_runtime_fields.action_semantics: For c=cosine and s=sine, encode [world_dx,world_dy,world_dz,grip] as [c*dx+s*dy,-s*dx+c*dy,dz,grip]; decode by the transpose. No action mean subtraction, scaling, gripper rotation, action clipping or per-future-step frame change. Native displacement remains 0.01 m per action unit. Public executor alone clips world action4 and executes four of sixteen.
required_runtime_fields.normalization: Fixed metric scales from config, no extra fitted statistics or data. No future motion labels or masks enter condition, denoise or decode.
required_runtime_fields.raw_current: The current chunk-start observation only defines horizontal heading from goal[36:38]-pegHead[39:41]. At norm<=1e-6 m use world x and y. Both history rows may use the current chunk frame; neither uses data beyond the chunk start.
required_runtime_fields.raw_history: [B,2,42] causal_context raw_history using hand 0:3, aperture 3:4, pegGrasp 4:7, quaternion xyzw 7:11, previous hand 18:21, previous aperture 21:22, previous pegGrasp 22:25, previous quaternion 25:29, goal 36:39 and pegHead 39:42.

design.reusable_regularity: Use a chunk-fixed horizontal orthonormal frame whose first axis points from the current observed pegHead toward the goal, whose second is its horizontal perpendicular and whose third is world up. Relative geometry and translational actions are expressed in that same frame. Jointly diffuse action4 and six future cumulative hand/pegHead displacement channels. Motion-outcome co-denoising encourages the common network to distinguish acquisition from actual tool transport without a discrete stage rule, dynamics rollout, planner, or future inference observation.
design.title: Gravity-preserving transport chart with joint hand/tool outcome diffusion

training_only_targets.diffusion_mapping: Rotate both displacement vectors in the causal chunk-start chart and divide by 0.1 m. Append after the unchanged encoded action4, giving joint dimension 10.
training_only_targets.inference: All ten channels are sampled from the host-owned diffusion noise and denoised jointly. Only the first four are decoded and executed; sampled outcomes are not ground-truth conditioning, action replacements or inputs to a planner. No target cache is stored on the deployed model.
training_only_targets.loss: 0.2 times auxiliary epsilon squared error on channels 4:10, multiplied elementwise by the common valid-step mask and divided by mask.sum()*6 (clamped to one for empty masks). All padded timesteps are excluded. The separate action epsilon loss remains weight 1 with denominator mask.sum()*4; never averaged over all ten channels.
training_only_targets.name: world_outcome_displacements
training_only_targets.shape: [number_of_windows,16,6]; hand cumulative xyz followed by pegHead cumulative xyz in world metres.
training_only_targets.source: For every exact D_N window at t and offset k=0..15, obs[t+k+1,0:3]-obs[t,0:3] for hand and obs[t+k+1,39:42]-obs[t,39:42] for pegHead. If t+k+1>T, repeat obs[T] solely to give a finite padded tensor.

design.change_summary: One new revision slot derived from A1, trained from scratch without inherited weights. Keep static cabinet action frame, four local position/motion vectors and aperture. Replace two rotation columns plus their differences (12 coordinates) by full reference-centered SO(3) log and relative rotation log (6); drop three deterministic distances and the redundant absolute goal bypass, retaining the world hand anchor. Conditioning changes 37 to 25. Batch the four vector rotations. Fit only an initial orientation chart reference from D_N. A2/A3 feedback motivates not adding their mechanisms, but neither is a code/architecture parent. No edits to submitted A1-A3 and no performance-driven repeated debug.
design.coverage_gap: A1 achieved 20/20 C and 20/20 E successes in the supplied development feedback, so there is no observed A1 failure cell to repair. Those finite samples do not establish perfect generalization. A2 failed all five E-LL episodes and A3 failed five E-HH plus four E-LH episodes, despite all candidates succeeding on C. The feedback provides native truncation categories, not contact trajectories; it cannot identify the mechanical cause. The remaining testable gap is whether A1's larger lifted representation is necessary, or whether a compact information-preserving pose chart can retain robustness at lower complete-system inference cost under the same training budget.
dependencies_preserved: Let r=R^T(hand-handle), d=R^T(handle-goal). With the explicit world hand and observed cabinet rotation R, handle=hand-R*r and goal=hand-R*(r+d). Thus removing A1's explicit world goal does not remove its dependency; full robot, handle and goal world positions remain recoverable. The two translational differences similarly recover previous hand and handle.

Orientation is three-dimensional, not reduced to a single yaw. From the restored reference q0 and the SO(3) exponential of the current log one recovers the current cabinet-local orientation q0*exp(log). Given delta=log(inv(q_previous)*q_current), previous orientation is q_current*inv(exp(delta)). Multiplication by observed cabinet yaw recovers both world orientations up to the physically irrelevant quaternion sign.

The rotation chart is unique away from the standard pi cut. The task's closed-to-open motion motivates this chart, but failure at its cut is explicitly acknowledged. Quaternion normalization and hemisphere handling make ordinary q/-q changes equivalent.

Current/previous aperture, hand/handle motion, world hand, cabinet yaw, goal relation and complete handle orientation still expose fixed-finger alignment, world workspace, door sweep and contact dependencies. No fixed-end-effector rotation is changed by the action frame.

Only deterministic redundancies and declared absent object2 zeros are removed. Both whole causal observations are transformed independently. No future observations, masks, elapsed episode time, simulator geometry or planner are introduced.

evidence_refs.fact: All support fitting is restricted to the exact ten episodes of door__N10__rep0.
Observed cabinet sin/cos yaw, xyzw handle orientation, handle geom center, current/previous native state, world action cube and fixed gripper orientation.
Five LL/five HH support episodes and diagonal position-yaw coverage motivate preserving A1's canonical relations.

A consistent closed handle frame, separate hand/handle motion, and changing quaternion through the door swing support a reference-centered full orientation plus relative angular motion representation.
Another initial cabinet yaw and world pose; the orientation reference must be fitted after removing cabinet yaw, not from raw world quaternions.

Visible door articulation and nearby hand require retaining both object pose and hand-relative coordinates.

expected_failure_signature: If explicit Euclidean distance lifts were crucial to A1's learned contact transitions, A4 may hover or descend incorrectly despite retaining enough information to reconstruct those distances. This would falsify the sufficiency of the compact inductive bias, not its mathematical recoverability.

The goal now enters through relative geometry instead of an absolute-goal bypass. Asymmetric C or E failures would indicate that the new factorization makes needed world-contact dependencies harder to learn under the fixed budget.

Near a relative rotation of pi, the minimal logarithmic chart has a cut; abrupt response or orientation-history inconsistency there is a specific representation failure mode. Full rotation columns in A1 do not have that chart cut.

Reducing the conditioner by twelve scalars reduces parameters, but rotation-log computations and denoiser-dominated execution may eliminate a latency advantage. Equal success with unchanged or higher fixed-method latency would not meet the intended cost benefit.
No A4 outcome or inference speed is claimed before formal evaluation. A1 remains immutable and eligible even if this single revision is negative.
