design.reusable_regularity: Preserve A1's static cabinet frame and orthogonal action mapping, but replace redundant geometric lifts by a 25-dimensional kinematic coordinate chart: cabinet-frame hand-minus-handle (3), handle-minus-goal (3), hand and handle finite differences (6), current/previous aperture (2), support-centered full SO(3) orientation log (3), full relative angular-motion log (3), world hand anchor (3), and cabinet sin/cos yaw (2). The orientation reference is the sign-aligned mean initial cabinet-local handle quaternion of the exact D_N. Centering the rotation chart at the closed handle avoids encoding a large constant handle-frame rotation and is not a planar-only approximation. No learned encoder, stage gates, articulated-frame fit or joint future channels are added. The common DP alone is learned from scratch.

support_fit.algorithm: Normalize each xyzw quaternion, left-multiply by inverse observed cabinet yaw, align sign with the first support reference, average the ten initial quaternions and renormalize. Store that orientation and count as JSON; register its conjugate and fixed metric scales as nonlearned buffers in build_modules. No actions, future trajectories or development states are used for fitting.
support_fit.inference: The reference is constant after restoration. Neither fit_support nor any temporal adaptation runs in deployment.

change_summary.scientific_revision: Reduce conditioning53->34 using physical sufficiency while keeping successful A1 action semantics and contact/attitude cues. A2/A3 outcomes argue against adding their more elaborate machinery in this one revision, but do not isolate why they failed.
change_summary.scope: One fresh A4 training slot, not checkpoint selection, a rerun of unchanged A1, or a modification of frozen candidates. No claim of A4 success or latency until the outer runner evaluates it.

The open question is whether its 53-channel redundant chart is necessary, or whether a smaller physically sufficient chart can retain success with less conditioning cost and fewer explicit layout-correlated shortcuts. dependencies_preserved: Let R be observed cabinet yaw, d=R^T(h-o), v=R^T(g-o), dh=R^T(h-ph), do=R^T(o-po), undoing known feature scales. Given retained h and R, reconstruct o=h-Rd, g=o+Rv, ph=h-Rdh and po=o-Rdo. Thus hand, handle, goal and native-previous world positions are not discarded as physical dependencies; they are no longer duplicated as direct features.

Current and previous handle attitudes are each represented by two cabinet-frame rotation-matrix columns, preserving full physical orientation up to irrelevant quaternion sign. Both apertures are retained, so aperture difference remains available by subtraction. Cabinet yaw and world hand position still allow fixed robot orientation, table height, reachability and world-clipping dependence.

Retain 3D contact distance, planar contact distance and handle-to-goal distance as explicit nonlinear conditioning features. The two whole observations and each one's native previous fields remain causal. No episode clock or future stage label is introduced.

Cabinet/panel placement and attitude available in raw observations remain reconstructable; there is no extra collision or simulator state. The only omitted independent raw slots are schema-declared absent object2 zeros, as in A1.

expected_failure_signature: If direct world handle/goal coordinates were an important shortcut for fixed-gripper or reach constraints, the compact chart may lose E success even though it retains their information. This would falsify practical sufficiency for the fixed training budget, not geometric reconstructability.

Removing explicit native-previous relative vectors and aperture difference may make motion/contact transitions harder to learn. New truncations after apparently reasonable approach, or a C decrease, would argue that redundant features were useful.

The denoiser backbone dominates inference cost, so a smaller condition dimension need not reduce fixed-method latency. If success ties but measured latency is worse, A1 remains preferred under the frozen rule even if A4 has fewer parameters.

change_summary: Revision after the single permitted A1-A3 feedback round; q3 recorded as A1 by the frozen C/E rule, not IID or training loss.

Reduce conditioning dimension 46->36. Remove native-previous local hand-handle vector (3), explicit aperture difference (1), and duplicate world hand-handle/goal-handle vectors (6). Keep all source physical dependencies, explicit distances, full pose history and world anchors.

The removed previous-contact vector equals current contact minus hand increment plus handle increment in the same cabinet frame; aperture difference is derivable from the two apertures; world vectors are inverse rotations of retained local vectors.

Vectorize the eight cabinet-frame vector transforms and the two quaternion-to-column conversions in one batched computation. This is an implementation/conditioning efficiency change, not a change in control semantics.

Do not import A2's support-fitted circle/phase experts or A3's graph/joint future-state channels. Their feedback informs parsimony but does not prove any one component harmful. A1-A3 remain immutable; A4 is one fresh scientific training slot.
design.coverage_gap: The support remains just one LL and one HH demonstration. Development feedback now shows A1 at 20/20 C and 20/20 E, A2 at 20/20 C and 19/20 E, and A3 at 20/20 C and 6/20 E. No A1 failure mechanism was observed. A4 therefore tests whether A1's redundant coordinates can be removed while preserving its successful physical bias and reducing conditioning cost; it does not invent a failure-specific repair.
dependencies_preserved: World hand position, world goal position and cabinet sin/cos remain direct conditioning channels; fixed robot orientation, workspace anisotropy and cabinet obstacle placement are not marginalized out.

The local current hand-handle and goal-handle vectors and local hand/handle increments retain all current/native-previous position information. Given world goal g and cabinet R, o=g-R*v_goal; h and native previous h/o are recoverable from retained relations and increments. World h is also explicitly retained rather than requiring this reconstruction.

Both current and native-previous handle orientations remain as first/third rotation columns in the cabinet frame. Both apertures remain. Contact and goal distances remain explicit for stage discrimination. Both whole causal observations are used.
Goal/handle/hand heights and the obstacle's cabinet yaw are preserved. No fitted hinge, new sensor, simulator state, planner or oracle is introduced. The absent object2 zero fields remain omitted.

design.change_summary: Initial pre-feedback design with learned soft skill routing, four role-specific bounded MLP encoders, an always-on world encoder and a weak stage cross-entropy auxiliary. Unlike the deterministic contact-chain candidate, representation specialization is learned and stage-supervised. Common DP backbone and world action4 are unchanged.
design.coverage_gap: Only paired low/low and high/high layouts occur in N10. An unconstrained joint representation can couple where to grasp to where to insert, and can conflate closing, lifting and inserting because their relative hand/peg offsets are similar. Independent peg/box shifts require reusing skills without assuming the demonstrated timing or y correlation.
dependencies_preserved: all branches use signed world coordinates; reach and transport roles separate peg placement from goal placement
a 0.025 per-branch routing floor prevents any geometry branch from being completely discarded
the ungated grasp gap and pegHead-to-goal error keep robot/object/box relations accessible through stage uncertainty

an always-on world encoder receives absolute hand/goal, current orientation, orientation difference and hand/object motion, retaining finite-workspace, fixed box orientation and robot dependencies rather than claiming global translation or rotation symmetry
gripper aperture, gripper change, measured object movement and absolute heights distinguish approach, contact and carrying
the head-to-grasp offset remains explicit in transport encoders; the two sites are never substituted for one another

design.expected_failure_signature: The key falsifiable risk is routing error under extrapolation: contact may be predicted too early before a secure grasp, or the transport branch may persist after height alignment. This would produce grasp misses or repeated rise/descend transitions despite reasonable initial reaching. Weak labels are not physical stage or success oracles; the 0.03 m height band can label a laterally misaligned peg as insertion, so large transverse E offsets may still cause premature insertion. Small N may also overfit the learned world branch. No performance claim is made.

design.reusable_regularity: Learn four soft representation branches for approach, contact/closing, transport and insertion. Approach/contact branches see peg-relative hand geometry rather than goal coordinates; transport/insertion branches see the pegHead-to-goal error and grasp contact. A causal router is trained with weak stage annotations made from support gripper/z commands and measured head height. At deployment it predicts solely from geometry, aperture and motion, without labels or a time clock. The DP consumes all soft-gated branches, a world-context encoder, an ungated metric safety skip and router logits (124 features per observation). Gates never prescribe native actions or plan a path.
design.support_fit: No fitted statistics, persistent episode cache or auxiliary pretraining. Learned encoders and router are registered in build_modules and optimized only jointly in the common fixed updates.
design.title: Weakly supervised causal skill routing with role-specific relational encoders

training_only_targets.definition: 0 if gripper command is negative; otherwise 1 if head is more than 0.03 m below goal and z command is nonpositive; otherwise 2 if still below that band; otherwise 3. These are weak skill labels, not evaluator stages or success thresholds.
training_only_targets.inference_isolation: Labels exist only in training_targets/training_loss. condition uses measured raw_history, and denoise exposes its router logits for the training loss. No teacher stage is concatenated at inference or training.
training_only_targets.loss: 0.05 times cross-entropy of the causal router, separately normalized by mask[:,0].sum()*2. All class labels are on valid history points. Public action epsilon loss stays weight 1 and denominator mask.sum()*4.

training_only_targets.source_fields: Only this D_N: actions[u,3], actions[u,2], obs[u,41] (pegHead z), obs[u,38] (goal z), with u=max(0,t-1) or t

design.change_summary: Initial pre-feedback design. Adds seven jointly diffused contact-state channels and their independently normalized epsilon objective, and applies an invertible causal goal-bearing yaw frame to translation controls and relational conditioning. Uses 48 direct features and one common U-Net; no learned stage router, secondary denoiser, simulator or planner.
design.coverage_gap: The N10 LL/HH support covers only a narrow set of horizontal pegHead-to-goal bearings and hand/peg/box alignments. Recombined and extrapolated y factors change both the sign and size of lateral transfer. An action-only world-coordinate model may memorize one bearing and may not learn that carrying requires maintaining grasp contact while reducing tip/goal error.
dependencies_preserved: the chunk frame orientation and absolute world hand coordinates remain in conditioning, so finite workspace, robot reach and fixed side-opening orientation are not treated as rotation invariant
current and previous peg orientation columns are rotated into the same frame; the physical pegHead-to-pegGrasp offset is retained separately
world z is never rotated away; hand, grasp, head and goal heights retain table and raised opening dependencies
the goal-to-hand edge exposes box proximity and can reconstruct the goal with the world hand anchor; the other contact edges reconstruct the distinct physical sites
step displacements, aperture/change and two whole observations remain causal; no runtime stage, simulator model or success signal is used
the action rotation is orthonormal and invertible, gripper is untouched, and only the native executor clips after world decoding

PUBLIC_CONTRACT.md, contracts.py and learning.py: joint channels after action4, fixed chunk-start transforms, independent mask-normalized auxiliary epsilon objective
design.expected_failure_signature: A wrong learned joint trajectory may confidently imagine maintained contact after a missed grasp, producing empty-gripper transport; this is a testable failure even if reaching is good. Very large bearing changes can expose unseen relationships between the canonical bearing and fixed side-opening axis. Near zero horizontal goal distance the bearing can turn rapidly or use its fallback, so last-stage sideways oscillation is a specific risk. The auxiliary may compete with action fitting at N10. No improvement or measured performance is claimed.

required_runtime_fields.action_frame: encode computes local xyz=R^T*native_xyz; decode computes native_xyz=R*local_xyz. XYZ scale remains 0.01 m per native unit, with no translation of displacement actions. Gripper is the fourth unchanged scalar. Encoded coordinates may exceed the native component cube; no candidate clipping occurs. The executor alone clips decoded world action4 and executes the common four-action prefix.
required_runtime_fields.conditioning_source: causal_context.raw_history [B,2,42]; raw_current [B,42] fixes the frame for both history observations and the whole sixteen-action chunk
required_runtime_fields.frame_definition: At chunk start, e1_xy=normalize(goal_xy-pegHead_xy), e2_xy=(-e1_y,e1_x), e3=world z. If the horizontal goal vector is at most 0.0001 m long, use normalize(pegHead_xy-pegGrasp_xy); if that too is degenerate use (-1,0). Both bases are proper rotations. The frame is recomputed only from the given causal chunk context, never from any future label or denoised auxiliary state.
required_runtime_fields.omitted: Only declared absent object2 zero fields. No runtime auxiliary truth, stages, factor values, episode time, reset state or additional sensors.

design.reusable_regularity: Denoise a joint 11-channel trajectory: four encoded native controls, future hand-to-grasp gap (3), future tip-to-goal error (3), and future aperture (1). The auxiliary geometry encourages the same denoiser to represent approach versus carrying without scripted phases. A proper horizontal frame has its first axis along the measured chunk-start pegHead-to-goal bearing, second perpendicular in the plane, and third world up. All actions and relative geometry in the chunk use that one causal frame. During inference auxiliary state is generated jointly from noise, not provided as ground truth, and is discarded after sampling. This is learned diffusion, not a rollout model or planner.
design.support_fit: None. Fixed metric scaling, no population statistics or pretraining beyond the host normalizer. There is no persistent training-label or episode cache on the deployment module.
design.title: Goal-bearing joint action and contact-state diffusion

training_only_targets.inference_isolation: All eleven channels are sampled by the one common U-Net and host diffusion RNG. Inference has no call to training_targets or diffusion_targets. Auxiliary predictions affect joint denoising internally but are never used as measured conditioning, a plan, or an alternative controller; only action4 is decoded.
training_only_targets.loss: 0.15 times joint-channel epsilon squared error, sum over mask[...,None] divided by mask.sum()*7. Public action epsilon loss remains separately weight 1 with denominator mask.sum()*4. No clean-state or action loss replacement occurs.
training_only_targets.name: future_contact_world
training_only_targets.representation: Both future vectors rotate with the same causal chunk-start R; divide contact gap by 0.1 m and goal error by 0.15 m. Aperture maps to 2*aperture-1. These append after encoded action4. Repeated terminal labels only fill padded positions and receive zero valid-mask weight.
training_only_targets.source_fields: For each exact-support window (episode,t), u=min(t+k+1,T); use obs[u,4:7]-obs[u,0:3], obs[t,36:39]-obs[u,39:42], obs[u,3]. Only valid k with t+k<T enter the objective.

design.action_frame_semantics: Identity encoding and decoding of native world_dx, world_dy, world_dz, gripper. xyz retains native 0.01 m/unit and gripper retains [g,-g] actuation. Only the host clips the world action cube and executes the fixed four-action prefix.
design.architecture: Per-observation 51-dimensional deterministic representation into one unmodified factory U-Net; no additional trainable modules. Common action epsilon loss only.
design.change_summary: Initial independent design. Replaces normalized-raw conditioning by explicit, physically scaled relation features while preserving native action4 and necessary world dependencies. No performance evidence was available.
design.coverage_gap: The exact D5 contains three LL and two HH episodes and no independent peg-y/box-y combinations. The observed initial peg-to-goal y offsets are all negative and small (about -0.041 to -0.059 m), whereas C/E can change their magnitude or sign. Absolute-y regression can therefore substitute peg location for box location. Only 415 support transitions are available.
dependencies_preserved: Hand-to-pegGrasp and goal-to-pegHead are separate signed world vectors; the head-to-grasp shaft offset is retained rather than confusing the two object points.
World z and the signed x insertion direction are not quotiented away. Four absolute heights retain table and vertical clearance dependence.
Coarse absolute hand and goal xyz preserve robot reachability and box/world placement; together with the relative vectors they retain all relevant current positions.
Current and native previous hand/peg differences preserve lag and transport motion; current and previous aperture and xyzw quaternion are retained. The two whole observations are both encoded.

The absent object2 channels are omitted only because task_materials declares object2_present=false. Box geometry is represented only by the provided goal and fixed world axes, not by any simulator query.

Raw slices, world action semantics, fixed orientation, distribution gap and object2 absence.
LL=3/HH=2, 415 transitions, small negative initial peg-to-goal y offsets, approximately constant quaternion, and peg/head height ranges.

expected_failure_signature: If merely exposing relations does not overcome one-sided training offsets, C/E trials with positive goal-minus-head y should move in the training-negative direction or stall in lateral alignment.
Near-contact soft features may saturate at larger errors; failure to use the accompanying metric channels would appear as correct motion signs but insufficient transport distance.
No explicit stage separation means a long novel transport can trigger insertion-height or gripper behavior too early. These are hypotheses, not measured results.
design.reusable_regularity: Approaching the pegGrasp site and aligning the pegHead with the box goal require different displacement vectors. Expose both directly to the common DP in fixed world axes. Pair unsaturated metric vectors, which retain extrapolation magnitude, with bounded componentwise near-contact features. Do not fit a narrow sample-standard-deviation normalization for these derived errors. This candidate has no extra learned encoder, stage gate, auxiliary loss, or action transformation.
design.support_fit_statistics: None. Geometric feature scales are declared constants, not additional fitted normalization or data. The common host still fits its frozen raw normalizer from this D5; the candidate uses raw causal geometry.
design.title: Metric multi-resolution reach and insertion relations

design.action_frame_semantics: Identity native world xyz and gripper action4. No action reweighting, residual controller, rotation, clipping or chunk-length change. Public action epsilon loss remains weight1 with mask.sum()*4 denominator.
design.architecture: One factory DP with per-observation condition_dim116 and native diffusion_action_dim4. Reach and insertion MLPs20-64-32, world MLP6-32-16, stage MLP10-32-3; all SiLU. Concatenate two softly weighted32-vectors, world16, phase probabilities3 and ungated geometry33. Auxiliary motion head116-64-6 is jointly trained. No additional optimizer or pretraining.
design.change_summary: Initial independent design. Adds jointly trained modular causal encoding, soft stage routing and masked stage/motion supervision; retains native action frame. This is not a performance-driven revision of A1 and no development feedback was used.
design.coverage_gap: The five correlated LL/HH demonstrations do not show the range of relative peg-to-box lateral offsets in C/E. Their lengths are 77-91 actions, and a much longer lateral transfer can break a policy that encodes demonstration time or absolute y as a proxy for stage. A2 tests learned interaction-specific features and geometric phase supervision rather than a single deterministic feature expansion.
dependencies_preserved: Reach encoder sees hand/peg relative position, their native previous-step displacements, aperture, grasp height and xyzw orientation.

Insertion encoder sees the provided goal relative to the provided pegHead, the head-to-grasp offset, peg motion, aperture, absolute heights and orientation. It cannot replace the box by the initial peg position.
A world encoder and direct coarse absolute hand/goal xyz preserve robot reachability, fixed-world insertion direction and table/box placement. No full translation or rotation invariance is asserted.
Both causal observations are encoded. Native previous quaternion and aperture are also retained in the ungated path. Only explicitly absent object2 channels are dropped.

Router predictions are soft and based on observed contact proximity, aperture, vertical state, transverse alignment and motion. No phase oracle, future label, demonstration index or elapsed timestep is an inference input.

evidence_refs.use: Exact D5 scope; no additional demonstrations or feedback.
Separate pegGrasp/head channels, native history and fixed world action semantics; independent evaluation factors.
Three LL/two HH episodes, episode lengths and aperture/height ranges; narrow layout coverage.

expected_failure_signature: A closed but empty or slipping grasp can be misclassified as transport by the surrogate router; expect lift/insert motion without corresponding pegHead movement.
If the router learns the short support chronology instead of its geometric inputs, longer E transport should trigger insertion prematurely or fail to transition when alignment is reached.

The learned bottlenecks and auxiliary displacement regression can overfit D5. In that case phase confidence may be high while the action y sign is wrong on positive goal-to-head offsets; this candidate does not impose lateral reflection symmetry.
A sufficiently biased short-horizon motion target can hurt multimodal recovery even if it helps ordinary support transitions. No performance has yet been observed.
design.reusable_regularity: Reach/grasp, lift/transport, and aligned insertion are recombinable interaction regimes. Separate 20-input reach and insertion encoders use hand-to-grasp versus goal-to-head information. A learned causal three-way router weights the encoders, while ungated metric skip features and a nonzero gate floor permit corrections. A training-only short-horizon hand/head displacement head encourages features to describe real motion instead of only fitting a stage label.
design.support_fit_statistics: None. Fixed physical scales and declared surrogate thresholds. training_targets uses only current D5 and does not cache labels in deployment state.
design.title: Learned reach/insert factorization with causal stage routing

training_only_targets.loss: 0.05 times cross entropy on predicted probabilities, normalized by valid first-action masks. Labels are never supplied to condition or denoise.

training_only_targets.source: Each exact D5 chunk-start observation obs[t]. Contact surrogate: aperture<0.5 and ||pegGrasp-hand||<0.065 m. Aligned surrogate: |goal_y-head_y|<0.035 and |goal_z-head_z|<0.035 m. Labels are approach/close, contact-but-not-aligned transport, contact-and-aligned insertion, with0.05 smoothing. These are designer surrogates, not reward or simulator phase labels.

training_only_targets.loss: 0.1 times SmoothL1 over six coordinates, divided by6*sum(mask[:,3]); denominator floored safely for an empty valid set. The head reads learned causal conditioning, never future data. It is skipped at inference.

design.action_frame_semantics: Identity encode/decode. First three components are native dimensionless world dx,dy,dz, scaled by 0.01 m by native control; fourth is native gripper scalar, never translated or rotated. Only the public executor clips the native cube. Horizon16 and executed prefix4 are unchanged.
change_summary: Initial independent model: deterministic multiscale geometric representation with identity action frame.
No optimizer updates, rollouts, performance feedback, or architecture search used in construction.
design.coverage_gap: D_N has one LL and one HH trajectory, 168 transitions in total. Their initial goal_y minus pegGrasp_y is about -0.059 and -0.049 m. The specified C and E layouts change that relation independently and can reverse its sign. Normalizing separate world coordinates on two layouts risks encoding layout identity rather than reach and insertion errors.
dependencies_preserved: World axes, gravity, heights of hand/grasp/head/goal, and a low-gain absolute hand workspace channel are retained; no rotation or full workspace-translation symmetry is assumed.

Absolute hand position plus signed grasp-hand, head-grasp and goal-head differences reconstruct every present position, including the static box goal. Thus target/box clearance information is not discarded while emphasizing relations.
Current xyzw peg quaternion and its native previous difference preserve orientation without magnifying tiny near-constant quaternion noise with a learned support scale.

Aperture, its previous difference, hand and peg native previous displacement, and the observed inter-history pegHead displacement preserve causal motion and contact cues. The first history slot's head difference is zero because an older pegHead is not supplied.
Absent object2 channels are omitted only because common_spec declares them absent zeros. No unobserved obstacle locations or contact flags are used.

Independent peg_y and box_y evaluation factors; world action4; separate pegGrasp and pegHead channels; fixed end-effector orientation.
LL/HH counts, 77/91 transitions, nearly identity peg quaternions, initial geometry and goal heights.

expected_failure_signature: If relative lifting is insufficient, grasping should remain plausible but transport lateral commands may retain the demonstrated negative-y bias in positive-offset C/E layouts.
This has no explicit manipulation-mode representation; closure/lift switches may average across similar geometric states, causing premature lift, prolonged table pressure, or stalled insertion.
Absolute workspace context allows but does not guarantee robot-boundary generalization. Extreme E layouts can still fail at reach or box clearance.
design.loss_and_capacity: 44 conditioning features per observation, one unchanged common DP, no extra modules or auxiliary losses. Common masked action epsilon loss has weight1 and denominator mask.sum()*4.

required_runtime_fields.normalization: Use raw fields for fixed physical scales, not common normalized coordinates. The common host normalizer and budget are unmodified; no fitted statistics are added.
required_runtime_fields.source: causal_context.raw_history [B,2,42], containing only shared deployment observations

design.reusable_regularity: Direct signed hand-to-grasp and head-to-goal differences expose compositional geometry without requiring subtraction to be learned from two correlated layouts. Near-contact tanh features at 0.025 m supplement linear 0.1 m features to resolve both centimeter alignment and long-range transport. These scales are physical design constants, not measured optimal hyperparameters. Both histories use the same deterministic feature map; native state differences retain approach direction and closure dynamics. Actions remain learned entirely by the common action4 diffusion process.
design.support_fit: None; deployment_state_dict is the empty base state. No demonstration rows or phase schedules are cached.
design.title: Multiscale signed metric relations with workspace context

design.action_frame_semantics: Identity native world dx,dy,dz and gripper encode/decode. Native translation scale0.01 m; gripper stays scalar. Public executor is sole clipper; fixed horizon16 and executed prefix4.
change_summary: Independent initial design: supervised causal mode routing with separate relation encoders, distinct from an ungated deterministic representation or joint motion diffusion.
No performance feedback or training used in design. No structural repairs before first check.
design.coverage_gap: Only two LL/HH support executions cover correlated source and destination positions. They share a recognizable open-hand approach, closure near the resting peg, then lifted movement to the side opening. The transition between downward contact and upward transport is sharp even when hand and peg positions change little. A purely continuous monolithic conditioning representation can entangle these modes with the two absolute layout identities.
dependencies_preserved: All three specialist features remain world-axis metric relations; the action frame is unchanged. Goal-to-head and goal-to-hand relations enter the carry expert, and goal-to-head enters the ungated scene skip at every stage to preserve the box dependency even during approach.

Low-gain absolute hand workspace position, hand/grasp/head/goal heights, and the directed head-minus-grasp shaft offset are always supplied. Goal, peg and head world positions can be reconstructed from these and the signed relations.

Native previous hand/grasp positions, aperture and quaternion are retained as differences; current quaternion is raw xyzw. The current history slot also receives causal pegHead displacement from the older supplied whole observation.

Router inputs include aperture and its change, relative hand/peg displacement, relative and separate motion, height above fitted resting grasp height, hand-grasp vertical separation, and shaft vertical offset. They include neither environment phase flags nor timestamps nor goal coordinates.
The common observation declares object2 absent zeros; no extra obstacle pose, contact force, success flag, planner or simulator state is assumed.

evidence_refs.detail: Current support is exactly demo_00 and demo_01; no evaluation observations are available.
C/E factor crossing, two-whole-observation history, aperture and physical pegHead fields, four native actions.
One LL and one HH; 77 and 91 transitions; gripper command extrema -1 and +0.6.

Read actions 0-76 and observations 31-34,48-53,64-68. Closure commands begin before aperture is fully closed; at 50-52 the aperture is roughly 0.37 to 0.33 and the policy switches from pressing down to lifted transfer. Later head height approaches goal height.
Read observations 50-53 and 86-91: corresponding closure state and later elevated peg with aperture near 0.30 in the different layout.
Open hand over resting peg.
Near-table gripper approach/closure geometry.
Held peg elevated at box opening.
Second-layout approach to the peg, before transfer to the box.
Second-layout lifted transfer configuration.

expected_failure_signature: Misclassified closure versus transport should appear as repeated down/up switching, lifting before secure grasp, or staying at the table with a closed aperture. Soft routing reduces but does not eliminate that risk.
The impending-lift label is only a kinematic proxy, not measured grasp contact. A dropped peg or unusual gripper contact could receive an incorrect mode probability.

Even correct mode routing may leave a same-sign lateral transfer bias because neither demonstration teaches a positive goal_y-minus-head_y carry. That would cause failures concentrated after a successful pickup in crossed/extreme layouts.
Three encoders and a supervised router may overfit 168 support transitions; mode confidence could be high away from the demonstrated relative distances.
design.loss_and_capacity: One frozen common DP with 110 conditioning channels (three 24-dimensional gated encodings, 35 ungated scene features, three logits). Specialist MLP hidden width64, router width48; all registered during build_modules and trained jointly. Common action epsilon loss is unchanged with weight1/denominator mask.sum()*4. Extra nonnegative masked mode CE has weight0.1; no joint diffusion channels or action-loss reweighting.

required_runtime_fields.fitted_state: One float rest_grasp_z restored before module construction. Raw metric features bypass common normalized values without modifying the common normalizer. No other runtime state or cache.
required_runtime_fields.source: causal_context.raw_history [B,2,42] from shared deployment observations

design.reusable_regularity: Three small learned relation encoders specialize in reach, grasp/contact, and carry/alignment. A soft three-way router is computed only from causal local hand/peg/gripper state, so absolute goal_y cannot act as a mode label. Training-only supervision encourages prediction of open-command, closed-command with peg still near rest, and closed-command with impending elevated peg. The four-step lookahead matches the fixed execution prefix but is never read at inference. Soft weights have a 0.1 floor and an ungated scene skip retains all present geometry; this is not a hard-coded controller, state machine, or separate diffusion expert ensemble.
design.support_fit: Median of pegGrasp_z in obs[0:min(10,T)] over each of the exact two supplied episodes; no final observation, action optimization, or data outside D_N. Only this scalar is saved in deployment state. It is also used by training-only mode labels.
design.title: Locally routed manipulation-mode encoders with causal deployment

training_only_targets.inference: Unavailable and unused. Only the learned causal mode logits condition the U-Net.
training_only_targets.name: mode_label
training_only_targets.source: Exact D_N actions[t,3] and obs[min(t+4,T),6]. Class0 if current native gripper command <=0; otherwise class1 if future pegGrasp_z <= fitted rest_grasp_z+0.025 m, class2 otherwise.

training_only_targets.mask: Auxiliary CE uses mode_valid * common mask[:,0] and divides by its sum clamped to at least1. No terminal extrapolated label contributes.
training_only_targets.name: mode_valid
training_only_targets.source: Exact episode action length; 1 only when t+4<=T.

action_frame_semantics.causal_frame_definition: At the current chunk start, contact=(aperture<0.5 and norm(pegGrasp-hand)<0.065m). Set s=-1 only if contact and goal_y-pegHead_y>0.005m, otherwise s=+1. This intentionally leaves reaching in native coordinates and retains a near-alignment identity deadband.
action_frame_semantics.decode: Use the identical chunk-start s: [encoded_dx,s*encoded_dy,encoded_dz,gripper]. S squared equals I; y reflection preserves the native action cube and Euclidean translation scale. Gripper remains its scalar native command. Only the executor clips and executes the fixed four-action prefix.
action_frame_semantics.encode: For all16 native action4 rows use [dx,s*dy,dz,gripper]. No translation, rescaling, clipping or action generation is performed.
action_frame_semantics.future_channels: All future labels are reflected by this same chunk-start s, never a future-state-derived frame. Sampled future channels never select the frame.
action_frame_semantics.quaternion: Reflection is a coordinate mapping, not an executable wrist rotation. Orientation channels use S R S; the native end-effector orientation is unchanged.

design.architecture: Single unchanged factory U-Net with condition_dim50 per observation and diffusion_action_dim10. No additional learned encoder, auxiliary head, planner or support-fit statistics. Deterministic physical-scale feature map and orthogonal involutive action encoding.
design.change_summary: Initial independent design with a contact-conditioned lateral action frame and joint future-geometry diffusion. Unlike A1 it modifies the diffusion variable/frame; unlike A2 it has no learned router or auxiliary regression head. All three scientific designs were specified before any development performance feedback.
design.coverage_gap: All five support layouts start with the goal below the peg in world y, by roughly0.041-0.059 m, although reach directions from the hand have both signs. C/E can require the opposite transport direction and a much larger displacement. A3 explicitly folds the undercovered positive post-contact lateral direction into negative-error coordinates and learns action/outcome correlations jointly, rather than asking signed-feature regression alone to extrapolate.
dependencies_preserved: The frame is S=diag(1,s,1), not a full task-goal rotation: x insertion direction and z/table clearance stay in native axes.

Signed reflected reach, insertion and shaft vectors preserve both pegGrasp and pegHead dependencies; both native previous-step motion vectors and both whole causal observations use the same chunk-start frame.
Current and previous xyzw quaternion transform by (s*qx,qy,s*qz,qw), the axial-vector rule for S R S, so orientation remains consistent with vector reflection.

Unreflected coarse absolute hand and goal xyz, all relevant heights and explicit reflection parity preserve robot/world and obstacle placement dependencies. This allows the DP to learn deviations from ideal lateral mirror symmetry.
Aperture is never reflected and the absence of object2 is the only reason its zero channels are omitted. The box is located by the provided goal, never by a hidden box pose or simulator call.
The deterministic contact surrogate uses only current aperture and hand-to-grasp distance. It is neither a contact oracle nor an inferred action command.

evidence_refs.use: Exact five-episode evidence scope; no performance or additional task data.
Independent peg_y/box_y evaluation factors, fixed orientation, native action cube, world axes and explicit head channel.
All initial peg-to-goal y offsets negative; initial hand-to-peg y has both signs; only LL and HH demonstrations. This motivates reflection only after the contact-like stage, not during reaching.

expected_failure_signature: If approximate lateral mirror symmetry is invalid because of robot or box-side interactions, previously unseen positive transport may approach the correct y but show different contact or overshoot errors than matched negative transport.

The contact surrogate can reflect a closed empty gripper; this would produce transport commands without a corresponding carried peg. A failure to recognize contact instead leaves positive transport in its unsupported native frame.
Parity changes near the5mm boundary or contact threshold can cause chunk-to-chunk y oscillation despite exact within-chunk invertibility.

Joint auxiliary diffusion may memorize the narrow support's future path and interfere with actions for longer E transports; predicted lateral outcome range would then remain too short. No such outcome or performance is claimed as observed.
design.reusable_regularity: Once the hand is near the grasp point with a small aperture, reversing a lateral goal error approximately reverses lateral transport without reversing gravity, insertion x, or gripper closure. Use only this partial symmetry, and retain world/asymmetry information. A ten-channel common U-Net jointly denoises encoded action4 and six future geometric-error coordinates so the diffusion model learns correlations between grasp maintenance, head alignment and actions. It does not optimize a plan or query a forward model.
design.support_fit_statistics: None. All target arrays are produced only through training_targets on exact D5; no trajectory or label cache is stored in deployment state.

training_only_targets.loss: Auxiliary epsilon MSE weight0.15 on channels4:10, divided by6*sum(valid_mask) with a safe zero-valid denominator. Invalid padded elements contribute zero. The host's action epsilon loss remains weight1 and denominator4*sum(valid_mask). At inference these6 channels start from host noise and are sampled jointly; there are no future targets in context and no auxiliary decoding controller.

training_only_targets.source: For k=0..15, current D5 obs[t+k+1]: concatenate (pegGrasp-hand)/0.1m and (goal-pegHead)/0.2m. Beyond the final transition, repeat obs[T] for finite padding only. Convert to the chunk-start reflected coordinates in diffusion_targets and append after encoded action4.

action_frame_semantics.basis: e_long=(goal_xy-pegHead_xy)/norm at chunk start, e_trans=(-e_long_y,e_long_x), e_up=world z; use e_long=(-1,0) when horizontal norm<=0.0001 m.
action_frame_semantics.decode: Apply exact inverse horizontal rotation to first three generated channels, pass gripper unchanged. One identical frame across the entire horizon. Rotated coordinates can exceed the unit cube; only the public executor clips after decoding to native world action4.
action_frame_semantics.encode: a_local=[dot(e_long,a_world_xy),dot(e_trans,a_world_xy),a_world_z,gripper]. No position offsets, action rescaling, or clipping.
action_frame_semantics.native_semantics: World translation has 0.01 m native scale, gripper is scalar, horizon16 and executed prefix4 remain fixed. Auxiliary channels never command an actuator.

change_summary: Independent initial design combining an invertible causal horizontal action frame with joint action/hand/pegHead motion diffusion; not an A1/A2 clone.
No performance feedback, optimization, or rollouts used for design. No structural repairs before first check.
design.coverage_gap: The two demonstrations both transport the peg toward smaller world x and smaller y; evaluation explicitly recombines and extrapolates peg_y and box_y. World-axis diffusion must otherwise extrapolate lateral sign and movement length from a narrow range. The demonstrations also have very different peg motion before versus after closure: the hand moves while the peg rests, then hand and peg move together. These observations motivate a distinct frame-equivariant and generative-kinematic design rather than categorical mode routing.
dependencies_preserved: The same chunk-start horizontal basis is used for both whole observations, all sixteen action vectors, and all auxiliary motion targets. Gravity/world z is unchanged; gripper is never rotated.

The actual observed shaft vector pegHead-minus-pegGrasp is supplied in the transport frame, preserving the distinction between the insertion axis and the line of transport. Raw world xyzw quaternion and its native previous difference are also retained.

World basis direction (cos,sin), low-gain absolute world hand position, and hand/grasp/head/goal heights remain available. Thus the design does not assert full robot or box rotation symmetry. These world cues plus local signed relations reconstruct all present positions and the box goal.

Native previous hand and pegGrasp motion, aperture change, and outer-history pegHead motion preserve causal contact and momentum cues. The older history slot has no extra pegHead predecessor and uses zero for that difference.
The absent object2 zeros are omitted, not replaced with simulator geometry. No obstacle oracle, reward, contact state, expert source or time-indexed trajectory lookup is used.

evidence_refs.detail: Exactly two current-support episodes and sixteen available demonstration frames; no dev/test observations.
Independent layout factors; shared pegHead site field; world native action4 with fixed orientation and native-cube clipping after decoding.
Both initial interaction-to-goal y components are negative, with x motion dominant; LL and HH only.
Read observations 0-4,31-34,48-53,64-68 and actions 0-76. Peg stays near fixed x/y through approach, moves with hand after closure, and pegHead differs from pegGrasp by about [-0.13,0,-0.01] m.
Read observations 50-53 and 86-91. Held peg and hand move together late; side insertion keeps shaft nearly world -x despite changing position.
Resting peg and raised box side opening are distinct physical features.
Held peg reaches the opening; translation to the box is not identical to arbitrary rotational task symmetry.
Lifted transport of peg to the different box layout.
Late insertion geometry motivates preserving world and shaft directions.

Public capability: fixed action loss independently uses only first four channels; training-only targets are isolated from causal inference; candidate extra loss must be mask normalized.

expected_failure_signature: If the model overuses transport equivariance and underuses shaft/world context, it may steer diagonally into the box face before lateral alignment, especially at extreme opposite-sign source/destination offsets.

The moving frame depends on the current pegHead-to-goal line. Near horizontal coincidence it can turn rapidly; below 0.1 mm distance it deterministically falls back to world -x. Oscillation or action discontinuity near such coincidence is a falsifiable frame-specific failure.

Joint future displacement channels may diffuse implausible peg motion or consume too much learning capacity from two demonstrations, giving correct approach direction but delayed closure or failed pickup. They are predictions, not contact guarantees.
Before pickup, the frame depends on the box even though the hand is reaching the peg. Large unseen frame yaw may harm grasp approach despite retaining world basis cues.
design.loss_and_capacity: 46 deterministic condition channels per observation. Exactly one common DP with diffusion_action_dim10; no architecture mutation or added denoiser. Action epsilon loss remains weight1 divided by mask.sum()*4. Additional nonnegative motion epsilon MSE uses only channels4:10, weight0.15, and denominator6*mask.sum() (clamped for all-zero auxiliary masks). Valid motion transitions exactly match the common action mask. No parameters outside joint training loss.

required_runtime_fields.normalization: Fixed metric scales applied to raw fields. Common support normalization is not modified. Basis comes only from raw_current goal_xy minus pegHead_xy; there is no inferred future frame or persistent rollout state.

design.reusable_regularity: Use the observed horizontal pegHead-to-goal direction as the positive longitudinal coordinate for the entire chunk. Signed geometry and translational actions share this causal orthonormal frame. This can express transport toward either lateral side through a consistent forward component while retaining the peg shaft and world axes needed for final side insertion. Append six diffusion channels describing future hand and pegHead displacement from their chunk-start positions. Joint generation encourages temporally coherent object coupling without a separately learned planner or future-state input. At inference all ten channels are generated from the host diffusion noise; only the decoded first four are executed.
design.support_fit: No fitted statistics or support caches. Only training_targets accesses future support rows; base deployment state remains empty.
design.title: Causal transport-frame action and hand/peg-motion joint diffusion

training_only_targets.inference: Future truth is never supplied. All six channels are denoised jointly with actions from host-generated initial noise and then ignored by the native executor.
training_only_targets.mapping: Rotate both displacement vectors using the causal chunk-start action basis and divide by 0.1 m. Append after encoded action4 as diffusion channels4:10.
training_only_targets.name: motion_world_m
training_only_targets.source: For each exact D_N window start t and valid action t+k, concatenate obs[t+k+1,0:3]-obs[t,0:3] and obs[t+k+1,39:42]-obs[t,39:42]. Terminal obs[T] may label its preceding valid transition. Invalid tail slots are zero.

design.change_summary: One new revision training slot, not a checkpoint selection or ensemble. Replace A3's pure yaw chart with lateral reflection followed by yaw; parity-transform its direct yz alignment feature and add parity to frame metadata, increasing per-observation dimension from 55 to 56. Keep the ten-channel common U-Net interface, target definitions, auxiliary weight 0.2, all physical scales and native control/execution semantics. No A2 stage model is imported because the feedback does not establish a causal stage failure. A1-A3 remain immutable. No structural repair or extra performance-driven debug has been performed.
design.coverage_gap: A3 was the q3 maximizer at 0.875: C=1.0 and E=0.75. Its E-LH cell had 0/5 successes while E-HL, E-LL and E-HH each had 5/5. A1 failed both E off-diagonals, and A2 achieved 1/5 E-HL and 2/5 E-LH. In the public factor schema, E-LH puts the low-y peg below the high-y box, reversing and enlarging the lateral transfer compared with the initial diagonal support. These small-cell results suggest a signed-geometry gap; they do not identify a failed stage, contact event or collision.
dependencies_preserved: World x (box insertion axis) and z (gravity) are not reflected. The chart additionally rotates xy as in A3. The chart metadata [cosine,sine,parity] exactly describes the world axes: world x maps to [cosine,-sine,0], world y to [parity*sine,parity*cosine,0], and world z to [0,0,1].

Unmodified world hand and goal positions, world heights, and world current/previous xyzw quaternions remain explicit conditioning. The robot workspace, table relation and box placement need not obey reflection symmetry. Parity remains visible so the learned network can break the local symmetry when these dependencies matter.

The direct yz alignment pair is now [parity*(goal_y-head_y),goal_z-head_z]. Together with parity this preserves the signed original alignment and the side-opening geometry while using the same convention as other local features.

Both pegGrasp and pegHead, their offset, observed hand/object displacements, previous reach error and gripper history are retained. Quaternions are explicitly world quaternions; they are not incorrectly reflected as translation vectors.

All sixteen actions and outcome targets and both history observations use a single chunk-start frame. No frame is recomputed from future labels or generated future states. Object2 is omitted only because the public schema declares it absent.

expected_failure_signature: Primary falsifiable expectation: E-LH improves relative to A3 while C and the other E cells remain strong. With only five episodes per E cell, this remains a testable design hypothesis rather than an estimated guaranteed gain.

A parity discontinuity at goal_y=pegHead_y can change the transverse convention near alignment. If harmful, one expects late oscillation or loss of insertion precision, including regressions in cells A3 already solved.

If the dominant E-LH failure actually comes from workspace reachability, empty grasp or box interference rather than signed local geometry, canonicalization may not improve it. The available native_truncated categories cannot distinguish those possibilities.

Parity is more often negative near alignment in support than during long transport. The network may treat the retained parity bit as a phase shortcut and insert too early on positive-lateral E layouts.

World-coordinate skips preserve dependencies but can prevent the desired sharing if the network overuses correlated world positions. Conversely excessive sharing can ignore real robot asymmetry, harming a reflected layout.
Joint outcome channels can still predict optimistic tool motion after a missed grasp. This revision deliberately does not add a contact detector or claim to repair that distinct failure mode.

required_runtime_fields.action_semantics: Encode native translation v as [c*v_x+s*p*v_y,-s*v_x+c*p*v_y,v_z]. Decode u as [c*u_x-s*u_y,p*(s*u_x+c*u_y),u_z]. Gripper is unchanged. Native scale remains 0.01 m, no candidate clipping or action shifting/scaling. The public executor clips decoded world action4 and executes four of sixteen.
required_runtime_fields.causality: Only chunk-start observations define p,c,s. No distribution labels, episode IDs, clock, future ground truth, masks, simulator handles or support caches are available to inference. Fixed metric scales use no fitted support statistics.
required_runtime_fields.frame: From raw_current only: d=goal_xy-pegHead_xy; p=-1 if d_y>0, otherwise +1. For norm(d)>1e-6 m, c=d_x/norm(d) and s=p*d_y/norm(d); otherwise c=1,s=0. Retain p in both cases. This fixed frame can be an improper orthogonal frame (determinant p), appropriate for expressing translational vectors; no rotation actuation or quaternion reflection is inferred.
required_runtime_fields.raw_history: [B,2,42] from causal_context. Use hand 0:3, gripper aperture 3:4, pegGrasp 4:7, object quaternion xyzw 7:11, previous hand 18:21, previous aperture 21:22, previous pegGrasp 22:25, previous quaternion 25:29, goal 36:39, pegHead 39:42.

design.reusable_regularity: Revise A3's transport chart by first reflecting the lateral coordinate when current goal_y-pegHead_y is positive, then applying the original gravity-preserving horizontal alignment. Opposite lateral transfers now share the same canonical heading half-plane and transverse coordinate convention. This is an invertible observation/action representation, not mirrored extra demonstrations or a controller. Keep A3's joint action/hand-displacement/pegHead-displacement diffusion, scales, losses and training budget unchanged.
design.title: Lateral-parity canonical transport chart with joint motion diffusion

training_only_targets.inference: Host-owned diffusion noise supplies all ten channels; only generated action4 is decoded/executed. Generated outcomes are neither oracle observations nor planner inputs.
training_only_targets.loss: Unchanged weight 0.2 times masked auxiliary epsilon MSE on six channels, divided by mask.sum()*6, clamped to one for empty masks. Common action epsilon loss remains independently weight 1 and normalized by mask.sum()*4. No padded steps contribute to either additional loss.
training_only_targets.mapping: Transform both vectors using the same causal parity chart as actions, divide by 0.1 m, append after encoded action4. Total joint dimension 10.

design.action_frame_semantics: Identity encode/decode. First three channels remain native world dx,dy,dz in units of .01 m per unit command at 80 Hz, gripper unchanged. No candidate clipping; only the common executor clips after decoding. Horizon16 and execute4 are unchanged.
design.architecture: Exactly one common DP factory call with per-observation condition_dim=62 and diffusion_action_dim=4. Two 26D instantaneous relation blocks plus 9D translational motion and 1D aperture motion. No learned encoder or auxiliary loss; all learned parameters are in the frozen common U-Net.
change_summary: Initial independent design: analytic world-anchored relation chain rather than normalized raw coordinates. No interface repairs or feedback-driven revisions at creation.
design.coverage_gap: The exact D20 contains ten LL and ten HH episodes and no crossed layouts. Raw stick_x and target_y can serve as correlated layout identifiers. E also changes both factor magnitudes beyond their narrow training intervals. A direct relational representation reduces the subtraction and extrapolation burden without claiming complete translation invariance.
dependencies_preserved: For each native current/previous block, the hand world xyz anchor plus stick-hand, object2-stick and goal-object2 reconstruct all four world positions. Absolute workspace and world vertical are not discarded.

Both native gripper apertures and both objects' xyzw quaternion channels remain available, with an invertible constant gain on quaternion vector components. The absent object2 orientation stays zeros, not an invented orientation measurement.
The outer two-observation history and the native previous18 fields are both used. Motion features are current-minus-native-previous, never future differences.

object_xyz is the stick COM; object2_xyz remains exactly insertion site+[0,.09,0]. No unobserved stick tip, obstacle pose, contact flag, reward, or collision-free route is assumed. World anchors retain dependence on the fixed table and robot workspace. There is no extra variable obstacle channel in this schema.

evidence_refs.use: Exact stick-push__N20__rep0 support scope and episode list.
LL/HH-only train cells, C/E factor intervals, observation point definitions, world action4 semantics.
Ten LL and ten HH; small y action spread and substantially larger x/z action spread motivate anisotropic but fixed metric scales.

expected_failure_signature: If explicit geometry alone is insufficient to identify the phase, errors should concentrate at the close/lift and lift/push transitions, despite plausible approach directions.

If fixed table contacts or robot kinematics dominate, crossed/extrapolated layouts may still fail even though all positions remain recoverable; world anchors are available but not hard-coded constraints.
Quaternions with a sign convention different from the support can produce a discontinuity in the direct quaternion conditioning. This candidate does not impose rotation equivariance.
required_runtime_fields: context.raw_history[B,2,39] from shared native observations; slices 0:18 current hand/aperture/stick/pushed pose,18:36 native previous equivalents,36:39 goal_xyz.

The host's normalized history argument is accepted but not used; all metric feature scales are declared in config.json. No episode identity, step number, support lookup, future state or environment handle is required.
design.reusable_regularity: Tool manipulation can be represented as hand-to-tool, tool-to-pushed-object, and pushed-object-to-goal relations. Fine local distances, coarser transport distances, causal motion, and explicit world heights give the shared U-Net separate coordinates for approach, acquisition and pushing. Fixed metric scales, rather than division by tiny support variance, keep extrapolated y and near-constant quaternion channels moderate.
design.support_fit_statistics: None. Fixed physical scales are architectural choices; there are no support-derived hidden tables or externally fitted weights. Host normalization and optimizer are unchanged.
design.title: World-anchored interaction chain with physical-unit conditioning

design.action_frame_semantics: Identity encode/decode of world dx,dy,dz,gripper. Native xyz command scale .01 m, frequency80 Hz; no phase-based action overrides or clipping. Common action epsilon weight1 and denominator mask.sum()*4 remain untouched; horizon16/execute4 unchanged.
design.architecture: Four independently parameterized two-layer SiLU encoders: contact30->64->32, transport36->64->32, goal19->64->16, world24->64->16. Goal-blind phase66->64->4 uses only contact/transport input. Soft gates weight contact by phases0+1, transport by1+2+3 and goal by2+3, each with floor .15. Direct relation/world/motion skips plus logits produce condition_dim131. One standard factory U-Net, diffusion_action_dim4. All modules registered in build_modules and trained by the unchanged optimizer through action loss and/or phase loss. No dropout or test-time random stream.
change_summary: Initial independent scientific design: learned typed encoders with causal soft phase factorization and a separately normalized training-only command-phase loss. This is not a clone or a feedback revision of the analytic candidate; no interface repairs at creation.
design.coverage_gap: With only LL/HH demonstrations, an unconstrained global encoder may use target_y as a proxy for stick_x or for progress through the nearly synchronized trajectories. This design allocates separate learned capacity to hand-stick acquisition, stick-object transport, and object-goal error, with a phase estimator that cannot observe goal position.
dependencies_preserved: Contact encoder sees current and native-previous hand-stick differences, relative and individual hand/stick motion, world heights, aperture change and stick orientations. It cannot see target_y.
Transport encoder sees object2-stick relations, both motions, vertical positions, apertures and both objects' current/native-previous quaternion channels.

Goal encoder retains goal-object2 current/previous errors, goal/object2 height and object2 motion/orientation. The world branch retains all current/previous hand/stick/object2 world positions, all current world heights including goal_z, and apertures.

Direct metric skips carry the current hand world anchor, three chain edges, aperture and current quaternion channels; all gates have positive floor .15 and their logits are included, so current world poses remain recoverable rather than made invariant to robot/table constraints. Motion skips preserve all three measured translational differences.

All offsets use the declared stick COM and observed object2 point insertion site+[0,.09,0], not an invented tool tip or center. Fixed table/robot dependence is retained via world features; there is no obstacle oracle or collision planner.

evidence_refs.use: Only this exact D20 may supervise the encoder and gate.
Correlated training factor cells, fixed-orientation native actuator, and available causal history fields.
Ten LL and ten HH episodes with a native fixed pushed-object start; relative and world channels should be distinguished rather than globally normalized into correlated identities.
Hand starts above the tabletop acquisition area.
Lowered hand near the tool region motivates an acquisition representation.

Late object displacement motivates a separate goal/object relation.

Sampled commands show opening, closing while lowering, positive-z lifting, then strong positive-x driving. The coarse label thresholds separate these observed command regimes; they are not claimed as ground-truth physical contacts.
Aperture change, lift, hand-stick co-motion and late object2 motion are causal observables relevant to phase.
Acquisition/lift pattern also appears in the other support cell.

expected_failure_signature: If coarse command labels do not transfer to off-support states, the gate may remain in acquisition after an unsuccessful grasp or declare transport without holding the stick. Such failures should involve wrong transition timing rather than initial target choice.

If the training-only phase regularization makes the learned representation overconfident, recovery after a dropped tool may be poor. The positive gate floor and label smoothing mitigate but do not eliminate this risk.

If absolute kinematic constraints dominate local relations, the coarse world branch can underfit and E may fail even with plausible relation-conditioned actions. Conversely, the shared U-Net can still learn spurious factor interactions: the factorization is a bias, not a proof of disentanglement.
required_runtime_fields: context.raw_history[B,2,39] containing current0:18, native-previous18:36 and goal36:39 for each of the two outer observations.

No demonstration command, phase label, progress index, success flag, training mask, future pose or environment state is supplied to condition or inference denoise. Inference phase probabilities come only from the goal-blind causal phase MLP.
design.reusable_regularity: A manipulation chain reuses acquisition and transport skills across goals. Separate contact, transport, goal and world MLPs are trained jointly with one common diffusion U-Net. A soft four-way causal gate emphasizes the relevant relation while never deleting the others. Training-only coarse command-mode labels orient the gate without creating an inference-time controller or a hard transition schedule.
design.support_fit_statistics: None beyond the frozen host normalizer. Feature metric scales and command thresholds are declared constants; no extra optimizer or learned support fit.

training_only_targets.definition: 0 if gripper<0; otherwise 3 if world_dx>.5; otherwise 2 if world_dz>.04; otherwise 1. These denote open approach, closed acquisition, lift and drive command modes, not contact or success labels.
training_only_targets.inference_use: None. Only the learned causal logits/probabilities are used; target tensor is never cached in deployment state.
training_only_targets.loss: 0.05 times four-class cross entropy with .05 label smoothing, weighted by mask[:,0] and divided by mask[:,0].sum().clamp_min(1). Scalar target per valid chunk start; no padded horizon targets are used.
training_only_targets.name: command_phase
training_only_targets.source: support_view[e].actions[t] for the exact D20 window start t

design.action_frame_semantics: Let R_t have the current observed stick's local axes as world columns. For row vectors encode xyz_world @ R_t; decode xyz_local @ R_t^T. R_t is fixed for all16 commands at chunk start. The .01 m native magnitude and80 Hz rate are unchanged. Gripper is concatenated unchanged and never rotated/translated. Neither local actions nor predicted-clean actions are clipped by the candidate; only the host clips decoded world action4 to the native cube. Execution remains prefix4.
design.architecture: One common DP factory call with per-observation condition_dim83 and diffusion_action_dim13. Two32D geometric instantaneous blocks,9D local translational motion,1D aperture change and9D world-frame orientation. The frozen U-Net is used without modification other than allowed factory dimensions. There is no separate encoder/head; every learned parameter participates in the joint epsilon loss.
change_summary: Initial independent design: reversible tool-frame action coding, explicit observed-point/insertion-site distinction, sign-invariant stick rotation features and joint future-motion diffusion supervision. No pre-feedback performance search, inherited checkpoint, or interface repair at creation.
design.coverage_gap: LL/HH-only supervision can entangle layout with action timing, and behavior cloning may imitate hand motion without representing whether the stick or pushed object actually follows. This design tests object-centric frame consistency and joint action/motion supervision rather than a phase classifier. It uses no extra transitions beyond this exact D20.
dependencies_preserved: Both outer observations and their native previous blocks are represented in one chunk-start stick rotation basis. Positions are never transformed in a future or per-predicted-step frame.

Each instantaneous block retains the world hand anchor, local hand-stick, observed object2-stick and goal-object2 relations, aperture, relative stick rotation, object2 xyzw channels and world heights. Appending the world chunk rotation recovers absolute orientation as well as world positions. Stick orientation features are sign invariant under q -> -q.

object_xyz is the stick COM, not its tip. Both the declared object2 point and the derived insertion site are included. The latter is exactly object2_xyz-[0,.09,0], as specified in task_materials, with the world offset subtracted before rotating. There is no assumed tool length or inferred unprovided collision geometry.
All current-minus-native-previous hand/stick/object2 motions and aperture change are retained. Absent object2 quaternion channels remain raw zero channels rather than fabricated measurements.

World hand/height/rotation anchors preserve access to gravity, the fixed table and robot workspace. This is partial geometric factorization, not a claim of unrestricted SE(3) symmetry or a collision-free path model.

evidence_refs.use: Exact D20 episode provenance and evidence boundary.
