expected_failure_signature: Primary falsifiable hypothesis: separating source geometry from large destination-frame yaw should improve crossed E relative to A3 without sacrificing its C success. Aggregate feedback does not establish that pickup was the previous failure; A4 may therefore fail to improve.

If the physical coupling proxy changes too early, the action basis can rotate during unsecured closure and generate lateral peg disturbance. If it changes too late, transfer geometry may still extrapolate poorly in the shaft action frame.

If failures are actually due to box-face collision or insufficient lateral alignment after pickup, contact-adaptive coordinates alone may leave E-HL/E-LH failures unchanged. Shaft and world context are retained but must still be used by the learned policy.
An empty closed gripper near the peg can falsely appear coupled; a dropped peg can cause basis switching and oscillation. This is an observation proxy, not a runtime contact oracle.

A normalized blend of nearly opposed shaft and goal directions can become ill-conditioned. The deterministic source-axis fallback makes outputs finite but not necessarily behaviorally smooth in such out-of-support geometry.
design.loss_and_capacity: One unchanged common DP with action_dim10 and 48 conditioning channels per observation, versus46 for A3. Action epsilon loss remains weight1/denominator mask.sum()*4. Motion epsilon loss is exactly A3's weight0.15 with independent denominator6*mask.sum() (clamped for zero masks). No new learned encoders, mode loss, optimizer setting, update budget, scheduler change or checkpoint choice.

required_runtime_fields.normalization: Same fixed metric0.1 m, near0.025 m, workspace0.5 m scales as A3; native displacements scaled by common native_xyz_scale_m. No common-normalizer change or fitted statistic.
required_runtime_fields.source: Shared causal_context.raw_history [B,2,42] and raw_current [B,42]

design.reusable_regularity: Approach and grasp are local to the peg, while carried transport depends on the box. A destination-defined frame need not rotate the source-reaching representation before a grasp. A4 uses a peg-shaft chart for hand-to-grasp, shaft, and motion features; a head-to-goal chart for insertion displacement; and a smooth contact-cue interpolation for the action frame. The contact cue is aperture closure times hand-grasp proximity, computed from current physical observations, not an environment phase or stored schedule. It only chooses coordinates, never prescribes an action. A3's joint hand/pegHead displacement diffusion is retained unchanged except that auxiliary vectors share the new action basis.
design.support_fit: None. Empty deployment state, no episode caches or copied weights. A4 is a fresh training slot at the fixed initialization/update recipe, not continued training of A3.
design.title: Contact-adaptive two-chart motion diffusion

training_only_targets.inference: Unavailable as truth. All ten channels are generated jointly by the fixed diffusion procedure and only first four decoded actions are executed. No auxiliary label or generated motion is fed into the contact cue.
training_only_targets.mapping: Rotate hand and head displacement by the one causal action basis and divide by0.1 m; append after encoded action4.
training_only_targets.name: motion_world_m
training_only_targets.source: Unchanged from A3: exact D_N future hand and pegHead displacements obs[t+k+1]-obs[t] for each valid t+k<T, with terminal obs[T] allowed for its preceding valid transition. Zero invalid tail slots.

design.change_summary: Initial independent design: four differently scoped 24-channel skill feature encoders, learned causal four-way gate with training-only mode supervision, direct 41-channel physical skip, and orthonormal chunk-fixed planar action transform. Total conditioning dimension 141; unchanged action4 common U-Net. This is neither a coordinate-only model nor a joint object-motion diffusion graph. All modules are built once in build_modules. No structural repairs at authoring time.
design.coverage_gap: The small LL/HH support ties initial tool position to the target location, and the same nearby hand/stick configuration can occur during downward acquisition and upward lift. A monolithic representation may encode an episode clock or layout-dependent stage boundary instead of composing reusable acquisition, lift and drive behavior.
dependencies_preserved: A 41-dimensional direct path retains current hand/world position, the three scene-link vectors, hand/stick/payload per-step displacements, both apertures, current and native-previous stick/payload quaternions, and the two components of the action-frame axis. With the serialized xy origin, all common physical state can be recovered.

The 20-dimensional gate excludes absolute xy and goal to discourage factor shortcuts but keeps hand-stick and stick-payload geometry, absolute hand/payload height, stick elevation above its support-estimated rest height, aperture, aperture change and body motion. A nonzero expert gate floor avoids irrevocable hard routing.

World z is never rotated. World orientation, robot base-relative position and the scene frame remain available, so the representation does not assume gravity/fixtures or fixed robot orientation are invariant to arbitrary rotations.
The tool is the observed stick COM, and payload is the observed insertion site plus [0,.09,0]. No inferred hidden tip, contact flag, planner, reward, simulator state or task progress oracle is used.

evidence_refs.observation: Defines exactly the current ten-episode training support.
World action4, xyzw orientation convention, native previous state, two-observation DP history, and crossed/extrapolated layouts.

Open approach actions precede positive gripper commands; downward acquisition changes to upward lift around action 26; strong positive x drive starts at action 45. Observed stick orientation changes modestly after acquisition. Labels are descriptive action-pattern surrogates, not asserted ground-truth contact states.
Stick starts rising while the aperture closes and the payload stays fixed in the other training cell; supports causal geometric stage cues.
Lift-to-positive-x-drive switch occurs at action 42, not the same absolute step as demo 00; motivates inferred stage instead of an episode clock.
Real grasp-period frame provides visual evidence of the acquisition configuration.
Real early frame again shows the acquisition configuration near the original fixture position.
Real late frame shows displacement of the pushed assembly, distinct from acquisition.

design.expected_failure_signature: Falsifiable risks: action-pattern stage labels may fit the demonstrator's switching convention rather than physical grasp success, causing a high-confidence lift/drive gate after a missed grasp. The planar stick-axis projection is poorly supported for near-vertical or strongly rotated tools; a deterministic world-x fallback is used only at projection degeneracy, not as a controller. Expert routing may still mistime the descent/lift transition in extrapolated layouts. Such failures would argue against this stage/frame bias even if individual local regressions are accurate; no performance gains are claimed.

required_runtime_fields.action_semantics: Normalize chunk-start stick xyzw quaternion and take the xy projection of its rotated local x axis. Let (c,s) be the resulting unit vector. Encode [ax,ay,az,g] as [c*ax+s*ay,-s*ax+c*ay,az,g]; decode with the transpose inverse. Use world x if projection length is <=1e-4. One frame from raw_current is shared by all sixteen actions and both conditioning observations. Neither action normalization nor candidate clipping is applied. Public native cube clipping, 0.01 m xyz control scaling and four-action execution are unchanged. Gripper is a scalar, not rotated.
required_runtime_fields.source: causal_context.raw_history [B,2,39] and raw_current [B,39] from the common causal observation only
required_runtime_fields.support_fit: Hand xy population mean uses only D_N obs[0:T]; nominal stick rest z is the mean of the ten initial observed COM heights. These constants alone are serialized; no support actions or stage labels are stored for inference.

design.reusable_regularity: Use four soft representation experts for open approach, closing descent, lift/alignment and drive. The learned gate receives only present/past local geometry, heights, aperture and motion, not time, future labels or goal coordinates. Training-only action-pattern labels disambiguate those modes. Local approach experts exclude the goal, whereas the drive expert explicitly receives payload-to-goal error. All commands still come from one common diffusion U-Net; there is no expert action controller or hard state machine. The observed stick orientation also defines a chunk-fixed orthonormal planar action frame.
design.title: Causal manipulation-stage features in a chunk-fixed stick-yaw frame

training_only_targets.inference: Labels and native actions are unavailable to the gate at deployment. The probability vectors are predicted from causal observations, concatenated into conditioning, and softly weight feature encoders. No auxiliary future target is supplied to denoise, encode or decode.
training_only_targets.loss: Additional nonnegative negative-log-likelihood on the four learned causal gate probabilities, weight 0.1. For each window, mask[:,0] marks both history labels valid; normalize separately by the sum of these two-history weights. Empty-mask safe. The public action epsilon objective retains weight 1 and denominator mask.sum()*4.
training_only_targets.name: support_stage
training_only_targets.source: Use only D_N native actions at max(t-1,0) and t. Label 0 when gripper<0; otherwise label 3 when world_dx>0.4; otherwise label 1 when world_dz<-0.1; otherwise label 2. No environment state machine or reward source. Thresholds are pre-feedback coarse separators motivated by inspected action ranges.

change_summary: Initial A1 authored from this bundle: a 65D metric relational condition, one unchanged common U-Net, no learned side modules or auxiliary loss. No performance information was available.
design.coverage_gap: D5 contains three LL and two HH episodes but no LH or HL. Stick x and goal y are confounded, and normalizing nearly fixed coordinates by tiny support standard deviations can magnify extrapolation. No failed grasp recovery is demonstrated.
dependencies_preserved: World-aligned vectors, absolute heights, and stick position relative to a fixed support-fit world origin preserve table/gravity, workspace, and fixed native hand orientation dependencies; no rotational or translational task symmetry is assumed.
The origin is the mean initial object2_xyz across only these five support episodes, restored in deployment state. Given this origin and the edge vectors, all input point positions remain recoverable.

Current and previous hand, stick, and pushed-object motion, gripper aperture/change, and both object orientations are present. Zero object2 quaternion remains zero; only the physical quaternion double cover is canonicalized.

Goal is the declared goal_xyz, not an inferred reward location. Object2 is the declared insertion-site-plus-[0,.09,0] point; no unobserved contact location or obstacle state is substituted. Fixed scene dependencies are retained through absolute geometry.

expected_failure_signature: If explicit metric edges do not break the support correlation, grasp alignment error will vary with target y even when stick pose is matched.

A representation-only model may average the abrupt descending-to-lifting transition, close or lift too soon, or continue a pushing motion after losing the tool. It has neither learned phase supervision nor future-effect consistency.
Orientation departures and contacts far beyond support may still fail; world dependencies are preserved, not modeled by a planner. These are predictions, not measured results.

required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Identity encode/decode: world_dx, world_dy, world_dz in native 0.01m action units and unchanged scalar gripper. Host-only native cube clipping; fixed chunk16/executed4.

required_runtime_fields.support_fit_state: world_origin: mean of D5 obs[0,11:14] only

design.reusable_regularity: Expose signed hand-to-stick, stick-to-pushed-object, and pushed-object-to-goal edges directly in world axes. Use centimeter-scale motion and grasp features but decimeter-scale scene features, rather than forcing the denoiser to subtract independently standardized positions. Two full observations and each native previous pose are retained. This is an explicit nonlearned representation, not a controller or a phase rule.
design.title: Metric interaction edges with a retained world anchor

change_summary: Initial A2: a new three-stream learned causal encoder and weak phase supervision with a complete metric world skip, 114D condition. This differs structurally from A1's fixed edge map. All decisions preceded performance feedback.
design.coverage_gap: Only five correlated LL/HH demonstrations cover acquisition, lift and transfer but no crossed factor cells or failed grasps. A single unrestricted conditioning stream can use target y as a proxy for the stick location or demonstration phase.
dependencies_preserved: The router and acquisition encoder do not see goal or absolute x/y, but they retain absolute hand/stick heights, their orientations and local temporal motion. This restricts a shortcut without claiming the whole task is translation invariant.

Every stream has routing weight at least .05. The U-Net also receives a nonzero .25-gain deterministic 39D world-pose skip including all current/previous hand, stick, object2, gripper, orientations and goal. Workspace/table dependencies and required world geometry are never removed by the router.

The pushed object is the declared object2 site-offset point, not an assumed body COM or hidden contact point. Fixed-object and fixed-native-end-effector dependencies remain encoded in world poses and heights.
Two whole observations are processed; native previous slots provide motion. Quaternion sign canonicalization identifies only equivalent physical rotations, and absent zero quaternions remain zero.

evidence_refs.detail: D5-only evidence; no historical candidates or performance.
Confounded factor coverage, observation point conventions, native world action semantics.
Three LL and two HH, all with open-to-closed gripper and large x/z command variation.

Read actions 0:20 (open approach then close/descent), 25:45 (z changes from descent to positive lift), 45:60 (x=1 transfer). Read obs 23:29 and 48:52 showing aperture closure and elevated carried stick. These motivate three weak command-regime labels, not hidden stages.
Read obs 24:27 showing a similar low hand and closing aperture at a different stick x/y and goal y.
Low acquisition posture.
Lifted tool and aligned hand posture.
HH low-grasp posture resembles LL local interaction.
HH lifted-tool posture.
Learned module registration and separation of causal conditioning from training targets.
Chunk-start mask, loss hooks, and separately normalized nonnegative auxiliary supervision.

expected_failure_signature: A failed grasp may look locally similar to a completed lift; the router may then over-weight transfer while the tool is not secured. This predicts premature horizontal motion rather than a target-y-dependent initial grasp offset.

Action-regime labels are imperfect stage labels: elevation can end before transfer begins, and transition observations may be ambiguous with a two-observation history. Soft gating should soften but cannot eliminate these mistakes.

The unrestricted world skip can still relearn support correlations, while an overly restrictive local router may miss obstacle or target-dependent stage timing. If routing is ineffective its phase probabilities will not separate the demonstrated motion regimes. No such behavior has been measured here.

required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Identity encode/decode, native world xyz units .01m and unchanged scalar gripper; only host clips [-1,1]. Fixed 16-step prediction, four-step execution.
required_runtime_fields.raw_history: [B,2,39] all declared fields. Router uses current/previous hand_xyz, object_xyz, gripper, stick quaternion and current absolute z only. Other branches/skip also use object2 poses and goal.
required_runtime_fields.support_fit_state: Mean D5 initial object2_xyz as fixed world origin, JSON-restored

design.reusable_regularity: Use three learned encoders with different receptive fields, routed by a learned soft stage estimator that sees only causal hand/stick relations, heights, aperture and motion. The acquisition encoder cannot see the goal. The elevation encoder adds the pushed-object relation. Only the transfer encoder adds goal edges. A weak training-only action-regime classifier encourages the causal router to distinguish descending acquisition, upward lift, and +x transfer. All actions remain generated by one common conditional U-Net, not by expert action rules.
design.title: Locally routed acquire, elevate, and transfer streams

training_only_targets.inference: Labels and actions[t] are unavailable and unused. Router probabilities are predicted exclusively from causal local state, once per condition call.
training_only_targets.loss: 0.05 times cross entropy against causal router probabilities at the newest observation. Weighted by mask[:,0], divided by mask[:,0].sum(), floor 1. No horizon-padding target contributes. Action epsilon weight 1 and denominator mask.sum()*4 unchanged.
training_only_targets.name: stage_label
training_only_targets.source: For each valid D5 chunk start t, actions[t]: transfer if world_dx>.8; otherwise elevate if gripper>0 and world_dz>.02; otherwise acquire. Thresholds annotate demonstrated commands, never generate deployment actions.

change_summary: Initial A3: one 14-channel common U-Net with explicit action/effect joint diffusion, a 58D causal metric tool-frame condition, and invertible planar action encoding. No stage encoder or phase labels; no performance feedback informed this design.
design.coverage_gap: D5 has correlated initial stick x and goal y and only successful short acquisition-to-push sequences. It contains no examples of recovery after losing the tool, and few transitions where the pushed object actually begins to move. Action-only imitation does not explicitly require representing which bodies should move together.
dependencies_preserved: The frame is computed only from raw_current[7:11], the observed stick xyzw quaternion. Its body x axis is projected into world xy and normalized; a degenerate horizontal projection falls back to the world axes. World z is unchanged. All sixteen action/effect timesteps use the exact same chunk-start basis.

Action xyz is an orthogonal coordinate change in native action units, with no origin subtraction, rescaling, clipping, or gripper rotation. Decode uses the inverse rotation and the host alone clips in the native cube. Thus this does not presume that rotation of the whole task preserves robot or collision behavior.

The 58D condition includes local hand-stick, stick-object2, and object2-goal vectors for current and previous native poses, both quaternions and apertures, all three observed motions, explicit heights, world stick positions relative to a restored fixed world origin, and the frame cos/sin. Original physical point positions are recoverable. Absolute robot/table dependencies are retained rather than discarded under a symmetry claim.

Effect sources use exactly object_xyz (stick COM) and object2_xyz (declared insertion-site offset), not hidden contact sites. No simulator body state, contact flag, planner or runtime oracle is requested.

evidence_refs.detail: Only this exact five-episode support can supply effect targets.
xyzw stick orientation, fixed native hand orientation, world action .01m units, goal and object2 source conventions.
LL=3/HH=2, stick orientations near identity, object2 initially fixed and displaced late in each support episode. Action y is much smaller than x/z.

Read obs 0:4 (stick and object2 nearly stationary), 23:29 (hand descends and stick begins responding), 48:52 (hand/stick move together while object2 stays fixed), 72:75 (object2 x increases). These motivate distinct motion channels instead of a single progress target.
Initial tabletop tool and pushed assembly.
Tool acquisition posture.
Lifted tool posture prior to the late object translation.
Translated pushed assembly, consistent with numeric object2 motion.
Joint diffusion may append auxiliary channels while retaining encoded native action4 first.
Host separates fixed action epsilon loss from auxiliary loss, and deployment jointly samples all channels but decodes only the first four.

expected_failure_signature: If the auxiliary predicts demonstration-time motion rather than physical coupling, the model can generate plausible tool effects even after a missed grasp and continue pushing without the tool. Generated effects are not a verified dynamics model.

Ten extra noisy channels may dilute the action-learning signal at a fixed update budget. A failure would appear as broadly worse action precision or noisier gripper/vertical motion, not necessarily a specific layout cell.

The tool frame may help small orientation changes but has little orientation coverage in these demonstrations. Near-vertical tools trigger the documented basis fallback, which can cause discontinuity; large departures from support remain untested.
Late pushed-object motion is sparse, so the joint model may over-predict stationary object2 effects or delay forward transfer. These are prospective signatures, not measured results.

required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Encode [c*dx+s*dy, -s*dx+c*dy, dz, gripper]; decode [c*ux-s*uy, s*ux+c*uy, uz, gripper]. c/s from observed chunk-start stick body x projection. No local clipping; host native-world clipping only, horizon16/executed4.
required_runtime_fields.raw_current: Observed current stick quaternion defines the one horizontal chunk frame
required_runtime_fields.support_fit_state: Mean initial object2_xyz from D5 as fixed world origin; JSON-restored, no trajectories cached

design.reusable_regularity: Jointly denoise native action4 and ten motion-effect channels: cumulative displacements of the hand, stick, and pushed-object observation point, plus aperture change, relative to the chunk start. This encourages the one denoiser to model the changing coupling of robot, carried tool, and pushed object. Express vector channels in a single causal horizontal tool-axis frame for each chunk, while retaining world position, orientation and vertical geometry in conditioning. The generated effects are not used for planning or action correction.
design.title: Chunk-fixed tool-axis action and effect diffusion

training_only_targets.diffusion_mapping: First nine channels rotated in groups of three into the causal chunk-start horizontal tool frame and divided by .10m; aperture difference divided by .50. Appended after the exact encoded action4. No target-dependent frame.
training_only_targets.inference: No future state is read. Host starts all fourteen channels from diffusion noise, jointly denoises them, discards generated effect channels, and decodes only action4.
training_only_targets.loss: 0.15 * sum(mask[...,None]*(epsilon_aux-noise_aux)^2)/(mask.sum()*10), denominator floor 1. Common action epsilon loss remains weight 1 with mask.sum()*4, unaffected by the auxiliary channel count.
training_only_targets.name: effect_world
training_only_targets.source: For support window (episode,t), obs[t+k+1] minus obs[t] in hand_xyz[0:3], stick_xyz[4:7], object2_xyz[11:14] and aperture[3:4] for valid k=0..15. Terminal obs[T] is used only for the valid final transition; padding is zero and masked out.

design.action_frame_semantics: Identity world action4 encode/decode inherited from CandidateDesign. Native xyz magnitude .01m per unit command, fixed end-effector orientation and80 Hz remain unchanged; gripper is untouched. No clipping except common post-decode native cube clipping, and no change to horizon16, execute4 or diffusion sampling.
design.architecture: Exactly one common factory DP with condition_dim39 and diffusion_action_dim4. Fixed nonlearned linear39x39 buffer maps raw history to current21D chain/pose plus18D native-history differences. No auxiliary head, learned pre-encoder, joint channels or additional loss. Every trainable parameter belongs to the unmodified common U-Net; action epsilon weight1 and denominator mask.sum()*4 remain the sole objective.
change_summary: Revision from A1, not a modification of its submitted files: reduce per-observation conditioning62->39 by replacing the second expanded native-previous chain with complete entity pose differences, encoding the goal only once, and dropping duplicate heights and planar norms.
Preserve all39 raw fields through an invertible map. Increase hand world-z gain to the prior explicit height scale so world vertical remains salient after removing duplicate height channels.
Compute the fixed map in one matrix multiplication with a nontrainable buffer. Keep world-frame action4, no auxiliary loss, common U-Net topology and all training/control budgets unchanged.
This is the single feedback-informed A4 experiment. No interface repairs at creation, no additional training runs, no new checkpoint selection and no claimed A4 performance before outer evaluation.
design.coverage_gap: The original support remains only LL/HH D20. After the one permitted initial development evaluation, A1,A2,A3 all attained C=1.0 and E=1.0 in every reported subcondition. No failure category was observed to justify a targeted behavioral repair, and these finite samples do not establish universal success. The revision instead tests whether A1's redundant expansion is necessary to preserve its observed generalization, while reducing conditioning cost under the frozen latency tie-break.
dependencies_preserved: Features0:3 are current hand world xyz,3:6 stick-hand,6:9 object2-stick,9:12 goal-object2. The hand anchor and three edges reconstruct all four current world positions.

Feature12 is current aperture;13:17 current stick xyzw and17:21 current object2 xyzw, with a constant vector-part gain10 and scalar-part gain1. Absent zero orientation fields are retained; no inference-time field is pruned merely because it was constant in D20.

Features21:30 are current-minus-native-previous hand/stick/object2 xyz differences divided by .01m;30 is aperture difference;31:39 are stick/object2 quaternion differences with the same gain as the current quaternions. All18 native-previous fields are therefore recoverable. Both outer observations are still supplied.

World vertical remains explicit in the hand z anchor scaled by .1m and is linearly recoverable for stick and object2 from the chain z components. This retains table/robot/workspace dependence while removing duplicate absolute-height features. World x/y anchors use .4m scaling.

The source points remain exactly stick COM and object2 insertion site+[0,.09,0]. No unprovided tip, contact, obstacle, collision-free route, success flag or dynamics oracle is introduced. Full world pose dependence is preserved.

evidence_refs.use: Same exact stick-push__N20__rep0 support provenance; no additional demonstrations.
Current18+native-previous18+goal3 schema, public object point definitions and world action4 semantics.
Correlated LL/HH support and anisotropic metric action/position variation still motivate physically scaled relations.
Robot and fixed tabletop anchor matter during approach.
Acquisition configuration makes relative hand/tool geometry relevant.
Raised tool configuration requires preservation of world height information.
Late pushing connects the tool and target object geometry.
Causal hand/stick/object2 changes distinguish approach, acquisition and delayed pushing without needing a second explicitly expanded relation chain.
Corresponding acquisition changes in the other support cell.

All three completed20000 updates and scored C=E=1.0. A1 latency0.10404845999437384s is lower than A2 0.10644499450427247s and A3 0.10710104800091358s. Thus q3 is A1; there is no reported accuracy failure to repair.

expected_failure_signature: If A1's nonlinear planar distance features were important for transfer, the compressed model can fail near approach-to-descent or close/lift boundaries even though no raw information is lost. That would falsify the sufficiency of minimal coordinates under this finite training budget.
Removing separately repeated heights and previous goal relations can make them harder for the shared U-Net to reconstruct; failures could include premature lateral driving before adequate lift.
The latency hypothesis may fail because fixed denoising overhead dominates the smaller conditioning projection. Lower condition dimension is not claimed to guarantee measured latency improvement.
Like A1, direct xyzw features can be sensitive to quaternion sign changes or off-support recovery states. The development ceiling does not test all such conditions.

feedback_basis.interpretation: Observed success is tied at the ceiling, so test representation economy rather than add supervision with no demonstrated accuracy benefit. The C and E95% intervals reported for each were approximately[.839,1], and no hidden-test results were used.

required_runtime_fields: context.raw_history[B,2,39]: current0:18, native-previous18:36, goal36:39 for both outer observations.
One fixed registered39x39 coefficient buffer built from config applies the physical-unit change of coordinates. It contains no fitted episode state, labels, parameters or support lookup.
No phase, future trajectory, step count, evaluation identity or environment handle. The normalized-history argument is accepted but raw causal fields supply this representation.
design.reusable_regularity: A current world anchor plus an interaction chain and entity-wise native-history differences is a minimal causal coordinate system. Relative positions expose manipulation geometry; instantaneous changes expose motion without concatenating a second full relation chain. The map is linear and invertible over the entire39D raw observation, not a learned compression and not a removal of constant support channels. The U-Net, rather than handcrafted norm features, must compute any remaining nonlinear interaction distances.
design.support_fit_statistics: None. No weights or checkpoints are inherited. A4 is trained from the host's seeded initialization for the full fixed budget as one new slot. The buffer is deterministic geometry, checkpointed/restored by the common module state mechanism.
design.title: Minimal invertible causal interaction chain

design.change_summary: One new revision training slot. Primary parent A1 supplies the selected deterministic relative/world bias, exact physical scales and action semantics. A2 contributes the compact recoverable direct-state representation idea; its learned graph and joint future-motion channels are not inherited. Compared with A1, replace 55 channels by a 39-channel full-rank affine state/difference map, remove three explicit norms and duplicate previous geometry, and retain individual motions plus all quaternion/aperture information. No A3 gate, no auxiliary loss, no learned encoder and no action-frame change. The single factory DP now has the same condition/action dimensions as B0, without changing the fixed U-Net recipe. A1--A3 are immutable; A4 is initialized and trained from scratch, not a checkpoint reuse. No structural repairs at authoring time.
design.coverage_gap: The original LL/HH factor coverage gap remains, but the released development results reveal no observed C/E failure for any initial candidate. They therefore do not justify inventing a failure-specific repair. The testable remaining design question is whether A1's redundant geometric conditioning is needed, or whether an invertible smaller representation can preserve its measured success with less representation and conditioning overhead.
dependencies_preserved: Output 0:3 is current hand minus a support-only world-xy origin divided by 0.2 m; 3:6 is stick-hand divided by 0.05 m; 6:9 is payload-stick divided by 0.2 m; 9:12 is goal-payload divided by 0.1 m. These vectors reconstruct every current world position, including goal, and preserve absolute height and world axes.

Output 12:16 and 16:20 retain both current xyzw object quaternions with vector components scaled by 0.1 and scalar component unscaled. Output 20 is current aperture. Output 21:30 retains hand/stick/payload displacement from native previous state, in units of 0.01 m. Output 30 is aperture difference divided by 0.1. Output 31:35 and 35:39 retain native-previous quaternions. Previous body positions and aperture are reconstructed by subtraction; no declared physical field is removed.

The same 39-dimensional map is applied to each of the two whole observations. No last-history compression, episode clock, stage oracle, contact flag or future label is introduced. Displacement is a measured observation difference, not a prediction.

The tool point is the declared stick COM and payload point is the declared insertion site plus [0,.09,0]. Retained robot/world position, gravity and orientation preserve the available fixture dependencies. No unobserved geometry, obstacle map, planner or simulator data are used.

evidence_refs.observation: A1, A2 and A3 each achieved 20/20 C and 20/20 E successes, with every cell at 1.0. Fixed-method latencies were A1=0.1028795154998079 s, A2=0.11209302950010169 s and A3=0.10644192000472685 s. Thus q3 is A1 by latency. Each C/E 95% binomial interval has reported lower endpoint 0.8388748419471806; the ceiling on this finite development set does not prove population-perfect success.
evidence_refs.source: development_feedback in the revision user message

evidence_refs.observation: The selected 55-channel deterministic chain retained both pose snapshots, their explicit motion differences, and redundant link distances. A4 preserves its units, world anchor and native action semantics but removes representational redundancy.
evidence_refs.source: submitted A1 design and implementation in this session

evidence_refs.observation: The successful graph model included a compact 39-channel recoverable geometric skip. This supports testing a compact direct path, but is not an ablation proving the graph or its motion auxiliary loss unnecessary.
evidence_refs.source: submitted A2 design and implementation in this session

evidence_refs.observation: All support fitting remains confined to the exact ten listed demonstrations; no new evidence or training episodes are added.
Defines the 39 raw channels, explicit native previous state, scene-point semantics and world action4.
Observed body displacements distinguish stationary tool, lifting stick and subsequently moving payload, so A4 retains these signals explicitly rather than simply deleting the native previous state.
Real initial fixture/robot layout motivates retaining world anchors.
Real manipulation frame motivates the separate hand-tool-payload relations.
Real displaced-payload frame motivates preserving payload and goal as separate state roles.

design.expected_failure_signature: A4 is not claimed faster or equally successful before its formal evaluation. Although the map is invertible, the unchanged finite U-Net must now derive link lengths and previous relative errors itself. Reduced feature redundancy could make grasp/lift switching harder, producing new failures even with no information removed. Conversely, matching C/E success with lower fixed-method latency would support the compact representation hypothesis. Small observed timing changes may be noisy; final selection will use the frozen reported latency rule without extra benchmarking or retries. No A1--A3 observed failure is fabricated.

required_runtime_fields.action_semantics: Identity encode/decode of native [world_dx,world_dy,world_dz,gripper], not a rotated, residual or normalized action space. The host alone clips the world action cube, applies 0.01 m xyz scaling and executes four of sixteen actions at 80 Hz.
required_runtime_fields.source: Only causal_context.raw_history [B,2,39] from the common deployment observation
required_runtime_fields.support_fit: Population mean of current hand xy over exactly D_N obs[0:T], with world z origin zero, identical estimator to A1. The xy constant is serialized; a fixed 39x39 affine matrix and 39-vector offset are registered nonlearned buffers during build_modules and rebuilt on deployment. No learned parameters are fitted outside the common optimizer, and the common normalizer is not changed.

design.reusable_regularity: Positions form a serial hand--stick--payload--goal chain; current chain geometry plus body displacements and orientation history is a sufficient coordinate system for the same causal raw state. A4 keeps the physical scales and world anchor of A1, removes duplicated previous chain snapshots and explicit link norms, and expresses the full transformation as a single fixed affine operation. This introduces a minimal-sufficient-state bias rather than a learned compression bottleneck or a new controller.
design.title: Compact causal difference chain: sufficient physical state without redundant channels

change_summary: One new revision training slot based on the selected A1, not an edit or checkpoint substitution. A1/A2/A3 remain frozen.
Retained A1's fixed support world origin, metric signed interaction edges, quaternion convention, identity world actions, and action-only loss.

Removed redundant pushed-object-to-hand edges, repeated distances and separate absolute-height scalars. Replaced the full native-previous spatial graph with explicit translational, aperture and quaternion-feature changes. This produces a 39D sufficient physical representation instead of 65D and reduces factory conditioning parameters without changing any common backbone width.

The revision is motivated by the empirical success tie and measured A1 latency advantage, not by a fabricated failure diagnosis. It tests representational sufficiency and efficiency with one fixed new training run.
design.coverage_gap: The original D5 still contains only three LL and two HH episodes. Development feedback reports no failures for any initial candidate in the sampled C/E cells, so there is no observed failure mode to repair. The unresolved question is whether A1's explicit but redundant conditioning is necessary for its empirical success, or whether a compact information-preserving relational state can retain that success with less inference work. Twenty C and twenty E trials per candidate do not establish perfect population generalization.
dependencies_preserved: Current stick world position equals origin plus .20 times its anchor feature; hand equals stick minus .05 times the grasp edge; pushed object equals stick plus .20 times its edge; goal equals pushed object plus .20 times the goal edge. Thus all absolute heights and workspace positions remain available, though they are no longer separately duplicated as scalar heights or lengths.

Native previous hand, stick and pushed-object positions are current positions minus .01 times their temporal features; previous aperture is current aperture minus .10 times its change. Previous quaternion features are current quaternion features minus their differences. Both common history entries remain, preserving every causal native previous slot.

Quaternion normalization and canonical sign preserve physical orientation, and zero absent quaternions remain zero as in A1. The fixed origin is fitted only to D5 initial object2_xyz and is restored for fresh deployment. No varying runtime object is treated as a fixed world anchor.

World axes, observed stick COM, declared object2 insertion-site-plus-[0,.09,0] point, goal, hand orientation constraint and scalar gripper semantics are unchanged. No obstacle state is invented or discarded; fixed scene dependencies remain represented by absolute positions and orientations.

evidence_refs.detail: Same exact five support episodes; no additional training data in revision.
Native current18+previous18+goal3 and world action schema define the 39D physical information being preserved.
LL/HH-only support and centimeter-scale acquisition motion justify retaining A1's local/scene/motion scale separation.
Previously read obs 23:29, 48:52 and 72:75 exhibit changing hand/stick/object2 motion coupling; explicit temporal changes preserve this signal while removing duplicate pose edges.
Inspected low grasp posture motivates keeping the direct 5cm-scaled hand-stick edge.
Inspected elevated tool posture motivates retaining absolute z via the world anchor rather than declaring a translation symmetry.
Inspected pushed-assembly translation is retained through the stick-object2 edge and object2 motion.

A1/A2/A3 each have equal-cell dev_C=1.0 and dev_E=1.0. Latencies are A1 .10132629299914697s, A2 .10616329000185942s, A3 .10361592249682872s; q3 selects A1. All have 20000 updates. No measured failure is attributed to a phase, frame or cell; no IID or hidden-test outcome selects.
evidence_refs.source: revision message development_feedback and q3 record_selection result

evidence_refs.detail: Condition dimension controls only allowed factory input capacity; action loss, backbone widths, sampling and update recipe stay frozen.

expected_failure_signature: If A1 depended on explicit redundant hand heights, point-to-point distances, or the duplicated previous graph for stage transitions, A4 may hesitate at lift onset or start forward transfer early even though it retains the same physical information. Reduced information redundancy is not assumed harmless for a finite learner.

If temporal quaternion differences are poorly conditioned away from support, orientation changes can cause worse contact behavior; crossing the quaternion canonical-sign boundary remains a potential discontinuity inherited from the physical representation.

If the common U-Net convolutional cost dominates, reducing conditioning from 65 to 39 dimensions may not improve measured latency enough to win the tie-break. No latency improvement or success result for A4 is claimed before evaluation.
The representation still has no recovery supervision, and empirical all-success development feedback does not validate tool loss recovery or broader extrapolation.

required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Identity encode/decode: world_dx, world_dy, world_dz in native .01m displacement-control units; unchanged scalar gripper. Host clips in native [-1,1], predicts sixteen and executes four. No support actions enter conditioning.
required_runtime_fields.raw_history: [B,2,39] all declared current/previous positions, apertures, object quaternions, and goal_xyz
required_runtime_fields.support_fit_state: world_origin: mean D5 obs[0,11:14], as in parent A1

design.reusable_regularity: Replace A1's redundant 65D representation by a 39D spatial-tree-plus-temporal-change representation. A fixed world anchor and the three edges hand-to-stick, stick-to-pushed-object and pushed-object-to-goal span all point positions. Explicit hand/stick/pushed-object motion, aperture change, and quaternion feature differences encode the native previous pose without separately listing a second complete graph. Keep the physical metric scales and direct short-range grasp edge that were present in the successful A1. No learned router, joint target, planner or controller is added.
design.title: Compact kinematic spanning-tree relations

design.change_summary: Initial scientific candidate: deterministic metric chain with lossless world anchor and explicit causal finite differences. Uses the unchanged factory U-Net and common action epsilon loss only. No structural repairs or prior models.
design.coverage_gap: D_2 has one LL and one HH episode, not independently varied stick_x and target_y. Absolute-coordinate, per-channel standardization can let target_y identify an entire demonstrated reach/lift/push sequence; the unobserved LH/HL and extrapolated cells need these relations recombined.

dependencies_preserved.goal: Goal is explicitly relative to the pushed-object observation, not used as a demo identifier or replaced by an average.
dependencies_preserved.objects: Both observed positions and xyzw quaternions remain recoverable from the anchor and chain. Object2 is the declared insertion-site-plus-offset point, not an inferred body COM.
dependencies_preserved.robot: Absolute hand xyz and aperture remain available at both native time slices; one-step hand and aperture changes retain motion and closure information. End-effector orientation and native cube are not assumed rotation-invariant.
dependencies_preserved.world_and_obstacles: World axes and absolute hand anchor retain workspace/table dependence, while both object poses retain the visible tool/fixture dependence. There is no extra obstacle channel, assumed collision-free route, planner or simulator state. Gravity-relative heights are recoverable.

evidence_refs.detail: Exact two-episode current support identities; no development or test states.
World action4, fixed orientation, object2 point semantics, LL/HH-only training and independent C/E factors.
One LL and one HH; goal_y differs between the two episodes; total 148 transitions; pushed-object y variance is only about 0.00027 m. These motivate metric rather than tiny marginal-variance scales.
Read obs 0:7, 20:35, 43:51 and actions 0:16, 25:45, 45:57. Aperture closes and stick height rises before the long positive-world-x motion; hand and stick move together with nonzero offset.
Actual initial frame shows tool and raised pushed-object/fixture near the robot in a tabletop workspace.
Actual frame at grasp/lift transition; hand/tool position relative to fixture matters.
Actual later frame after the observed lift.
Actual late frame shows interaction with the pushed assembly; not an independent hand-to-goal reach.
One frozen DP, two observations, action4 loss and native decode/execution requirements.

design.expected_failure_signature: If geometric edges alone do not identify grasp/lift readiness, the policy will reverse vertical motion too early or too late, miss the grasp, or push before attaining contact height. A competing falsifier is successful reaching but x-directed pushing insensitive to target_y: the representation exposes target error but does not impose its correct causal use. World-anchor shortcuts can still survive with only two demonstrations. No performance claim is made.

required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Identity encode/decode: world_dx/world_dy/world_dz retain native 0.01 m scaling and gripper remains an independent actuator scalar. No candidate clipping. The executor alone clips in the native cube and executes four of sixteen commands.
required_runtime_fields.condition: 52 channels per observation: 21 current-chain, 21 previous-chain, 10 one-step change channels. Fixed physical scales, no support-fit or external statistics.
required_runtime_fields.source: Only causal_context.raw_history [B,2,39] from shared deployment observations.

design.reusable_regularity: Represent the manipulation as three directed metric edges: hand to stick COM, stick COM to the observed pushed-object point, and pushed-object point to goal. Separate near-grasp and long-tool scales expose small contact errors without amplifying nearly constant world coordinates. Duplicate this invertible representation for the native current and previous states and expose one-step displacements. All edge components stay in world axes, with a weak but lossless world hand anchor. No learned extra encoder or stage clock is used.
design.title: World-axis metric interaction chain

design.change_summary: Initial independent scientific design: jointly learned shared interaction encoding, causal relation attention, and separately mask-normalized multistep motion supervision. Unlike a deterministic relation-only input, salience and motion abstractions are learned in the common optimizer. No earlier candidate feedback or structural repair is used.
design.coverage_gap: Two LL/HH demonstrations confound object and goal placement, and have few examples near the closing/lift/transport switches. A flat representation can interpolate whole trajectories rather than reusing interactions, while purely geometric input alone does not force the denoiser to represent whether the tool is being acquired or transported.

dependencies_preserved.objects_and_goal: All observed object positions, current/previous xyzw quaternions and goal remain recoverable. No real orientation is invented for the hand or goal: graph endpoint orientation placeholders are zeros with role tags. Object2 remains the declared observation point, not an inferred COM.
dependencies_preserved.robot: Both native hand poses and apertures plus hand/closure finite differences survive the bypass. Absolute hand world position and fixed-world action components preserve robot workspace and actuator dependence.
dependencies_preserved.stage: Three attention weights are learned salience, not oracle stage labels or a persistent state machine. Every value is recomputed from the two causal whole observations. All goal and long-range dependencies also remain in the bypass and edge embeddings.
dependencies_preserved.world_and_obstacles: World coordinates and physical heights are retained. Encoded interaction edges explicitly include the second object/fixture; no independent obstacle geometry, collision oracle, analytic path or unobserved contact flag is introduced.

evidence_refs.detail: Exact current D_2 identities and permitted evidence bundle.
Only shared raw pose/aperture/goal observations at inference; fixed-world native action4 and object2 insertion-site-plus-offset semantics.
One 75-transition LL and one 73-transition HH sequence; no factorial coverage or recovery episodes.

Inspected obs 20:35 and 43:51: aperture drops from about 0.88 to 0.34, hand-stick z offset settles near 0.043 m, then both rise before positive-x transport. Inspected actions 25:45 show descent-to-lift reversal.
Inspected obs 22:27 and 43:48: analogous closing and raised co-motion at different initial stick/goal positions. These are evidence for reusable relations, not observed performance of this candidate.
Actual inspected acquisition/lift frame with tool adjacent to the raised fixture.
Actual inspected second-demo closing-stage frame; similar manipulation geometry despite changed factors.
Actual inspected late second-demo frame with hand at the pushed assembly.
All learned modules registered in build_modules; auxiliary targets are training-only.
Public action epsilon loss remains independent of additional mask-normalized losses. Auxiliary head need not execute during deployment.

design.expected_failure_signature: The learned attention could collapse onto a single relation or learn a nominal aperture/height schedule that fails after a missed grasp. Future-motion supervision could encourage averaging across the lift/transport transition, observed as correct approach but premature horizontal transport or stalled lifting. If the auxiliary representation truly helps causal reuse, its gains should not require IID goal/stick pairing. No measured gains are asserted; the bypass can still permit shortcuts and the 16-step motion prediction can overfit two trajectories.

required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Identity world action4 encode/decode; no action normalization, rescaling or candidate clipping. Gripper is not rotated. The common executor clips world native commands and executes four of sixteen.
required_runtime_fields.condition: 124 channels per observation: 49 lossless hand-rooted pose/goal/change channels, three 24-dimensional shared edge encodings modulated by causal softmax weights, and those three weights. The gate is 14->32->3 and shared edge encoder is 24->64->24. All scaling is fixed physical scaling, without support-fit statistics.
required_runtime_fields.source: causal_context.raw_history [B,2,39], the identical shared deployment input. Normalized history is accepted but physical-scale raw features are used.

design.reusable_regularity: A single shared MLP encodes the three physical relations hand-stick, stick-pushed-object, and pushed-object-goal, with explicit role tags, relative position history, relative displacement, endpoint heights and observed orientations. Learned soft attention over these relations depends only on causal aperture, hand-stick error, heights and hand/stick motion; it does not use target coordinates as an episode-specific phase clock. The U-Net receives these gated edge embeddings plus a lossless metric hand-rooted bypass. Training-only prediction of hand, tool, pushed-object and aperture evolution encourages embeddings to identify acquisition versus coupled transport, without imposing a hand-coded controller or supplying future states at inference.
design.title: Causally gated shared-edge encoder with future-motion supervision

training_only_targets.loss: 0.2 times sum of squared error over public valid-action mask intersected with future_motion_valid, divided by 10 times that intersected mask sum (denominator floor 1 for empty masks). Nonnegative additional loss; public action epsilon weight 1 and mask.sum()*4 denominator unchanged.
training_only_targets.name: future_motion
training_only_targets.predictor: 124->128->160 MLP from the causal encoded current observation, reshaped [B,16,10]. Evaluated only in training_loss; no future values or auxiliary caches at inference.
training_only_targets.source_fields: For each current D_N window (episode,t), use obs[t+j+1,0:3], obs[t+j+1,4:7], obs[t+j+1,11:14], obs[t+j+1,3:4] minus the corresponding chunk-start fields for j=0..15 while t+j<T. Includes only the terminal observation of valid final actions, never another episode.
training_only_targets.units: Hand/stick/pushed-object world displacement divided by 0.1 m, followed by unscaled aperture change; ten channels.

design.change_summary: Initial independent scientific candidate: causal invertible action/observation yaw frame and a 13-channel common U-Net jointly diffusing actions and interaction relations. No learned motion-head or interaction gate, no support fitting, and no use of candidate performance. No structural repair before the initial check.
design.coverage_gap: D_2 does not show independent stick and goal variation or the extrapolated target directions. It also sparsely covers the transition from approaching a free tool to maintaining a grasped offset and moving the pushed object. Training an action-only denoiser in world coordinates need not discover either directional reuse or those coupled geometric constraints.

dependencies_preserved.goal: The complete goal relative vector, its frame direction and world anchor remain recoverable; no mean target or sampled factor label replaces it.
dependencies_preserved.history: Every rotation is derived from raw_current at chunk start. Previous poses are expressed in that same frame, not a changing frame that confounds velocity with frame motion. Native one-step displacement and aperture change are explicit.
dependencies_preserved.objects: The chain plus hand anchors and frame recovers both native positions. Current/previous xyzw quaternions are transformed by the inverse frame yaw and retained, so tool/fixture orientation relative to the intended displacement is visible. Object2 uses the declared insertion-site-plus-offset observation and its all-zero quaternion stays an all-zero placeholder under rotation; no physical orientation is invented.
dependencies_preserved.obstacles: Both observed objects and their relative geometry remain available. No hidden body poses, contact forces, table collision queries, simulated paths or additional obstacle channels are introduced. The frame is not a collision-free path.
dependencies_preserved.world_and_robot: The frame is an invertible coordinate choice, not an assertion of exact workspace rotational symmetry. Absolute current and previous hand anchors remain in world coordinates, frame cosine/sine is explicitly conditioned, and z is the native gravity axis. Fixed end-effector orientation and the world action cube remain relevant.

evidence_refs.detail: Only the two current-support episodes and their provided images/trajectories are used.
World xyz displacement plus scalar gripper, fixed rotation, goal/object2 observation definitions and C/E factor directions.

Initial pushed-object-to-goal vectors approximately [0.1995,-0.0301,0] and [0.2001,-0.0146,0] define nearby but distinct horizontal directions. Pushed-object y has very little observed variation, cautioning against assuming exact yaw symmetry.

Read obs 20:35 and 43:51 and actions 25:45,45:57: hand-stick offset stabilizes during lift, then the positive-x action persists while approaching the second object. This motivates coupled relation/action modeling, not a direct hand-to-goal point model.
Read obs 22:27 and 43:48 show a similar raised hand-tool offset at different stick and target placements.
Actual inspected tabletop view with raised pushed assembly and nearby tool/robot.
Actual inspected lifted-tool stage near the assembly.
Actual inspected later interaction supports retaining both objects rather than treating only the stick as the goal object.
Actual inspected late second-demo frame; world fixture and robot constraints are not rotated by changing target_y.
Joint diffusion is permitted with encoded native action4 first; gripper is not a translation vector; native clipping remains outside the candidate.
Shared diffusion generator samples all joint channels at inference, action4 is decoded, and the fixed action epsilon loss remains separate from auxiliary epsilon loss.

design.expected_failure_signature: If the task is predominantly world-axis constrained, goal-axis generalization may be inappropriate: extrapolated target_y could induce unnecessary sideways tool commands, a missed fixture, or early grasp errors despite a correct forward push component. The exposed world frame and relative orientations allow, but do not guarantee, learning that correction. Joint relation diffusion may learn nominal contact geometry even when a grasp actually fails, causing confident transport without a tool. A further failure is increased denoising error/latency from nine auxiliary channels at the unchanged budget. No outcome is claimed.

required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Let (c,s)=normalize(goal_xy-object2_xy) at chunk start, falling back to world +x only below 1e-6 m. Encode (a_x,a_y,a_z,a_g) as (c*a_x+s*a_y,-s*a_x+c*a_y,a_z,a_g). Decode by the inverse horizontal rotation. No translations of displacement actions, scaling, per-step re-framing, sample clipping or gripper rotation occur. Only the host clips the decoded world action cube and executes four of sixteen. Local translations can legitimately exceed individual [-1,1] coordinates.
required_runtime_fields.condition: 54 physical-scale channels per observation: two 21-channel pose/relation/quaternion blocks, ten finite-difference channels and two chunk-frame horizontal direction components. Scales are fixed physical constants; no fitted statistics or learned external encoder.
required_runtime_fields.source: Only shared causal_context.raw_history [B,2,39] and raw_current [B,39]. No cached trajectory, episode ID, time index or future labels.

design.reusable_regularity: Express translation commands and relative geometry in a horizontal frame whose forward axis is the observed pushed-object-to-goal displacement at chunk start. Keep world vertical fixed. Use one fixed frame for the entire sixteen-action chunk, both whole observation histories and both native subframes. Simultaneously diffuse action4 and nine next-state relation coordinates (hand-stick, stick-pushed-object, pushed-object-goal). The joint distribution is a learned coupling of actions with contact/transport geometry, not a planner, trajectory lookup, deterministic controller or inference-time future-state conditioning.
design.title: Causal goal-axis frame with joint action-relation diffusion

training_only_targets.joint_layout: Channels 0:4 are exactly encoded native action4. Channels 4:7 are next hand-to-stick relative coordinates, 7:10 next stick-to-pushed-object coordinates, 10:13 next pushed-object-to-goal coordinates. All are jointly noised by the shared scheduler. At deployment all thirteen channels start as host-generated noise; auxiliary channels are generated latent outcomes and discarded after sampling, never observations or a condition hook input.
training_only_targets.loss: Additional 0.25 times auxiliary epsilon squared error, normalized separately by 9 times sum(public action mask intersect relation_valid), with denominator floor 1 for empty masks. The fixed action epsilon loss retains weight 1 and denominator mask.sum()*4; no auxiliary error is added to its denominator or its channels.
training_only_targets.name: future_relations_world
training_only_targets.source_fields: For each exact D_N window (episode,t) and each valid action j with t+j<T: next observation obs[t+j+1] provides stick_xyz-hand_xyz, object2_xyz-stick_xyz, goal_xyz-object2_xyz. Nine world-meter values are rotated into the causal chunk-start frame, not a future-derived frame, then scaled by grasp/tool/goal metric scales. Padded entries are zeros and excluded from loss.

design.change_summary: Single post-feedback architecture revision from A2: edge_width 24->8 reduces total condition_dim 124->76, the shared edge output layer, the common DP conditioning projections and the auxiliary head input width. All edge inputs, gate structure, physical bypass, action frame, auxiliary labels/weight/masks, other hidden widths and common training recipe are unchanged. Candidate class is renamed only for clarity. This is fresh initialization and one new fixed-budget training slot, not pruning, distillation, warm-starting, a checkpoint change, or a repair to any submitted candidate. A1/A3 results inform the choice but their code is not used as a parent.
design.coverage_gap: The exact two-episode LL/HH support still lacks independent and extrapolated factor coverage. Revision feedback gives A2 a perfect finite C/E sample, so no observed A2 failure mechanism is available to target. Its wider conditioning interface has more parameters and slightly higher fixed-method latency than A1. This revision tests whether the learned relational abstraction can be retained in a narrower interface without losing extrapolation robustness.

dependencies_preserved.causal_stage: Attention is computed from aperture, its change, hand-stick error, heights and hand/stick one-step displacements, not time, episode ID, factor label, target-as-phase clock or future state. The goal still affects explicit physical and learned relational channels.
dependencies_preserved.objects_and_goal: Both object positions, current/previous xyzw quaternions and complete goal vector remain recoverable from the hand-rooted coordinates. Learned edge inputs retain relative position history, edge motion, endpoint heights, observed quaternions and explicit roles. Object2 is the declared observed insertion-site-plus-offset point. Zero graph quaternions for hand/goal are absence placeholders, not invented orientations.
dependencies_preserved.robot: Current and previous absolute hand anchors, aperture, hand motion and closure change remain in the 49-channel physical bypass. World orientation and native control semantics are unchanged.
dependencies_preserved.world_and_obstacles: All positions and actions stay in world axes; absolute hand position and all heights are retained. Both objects/fixture dependencies remain represented, with no hidden obstacle data, oracle contact labels, planner or simulator internals.

evidence_refs.detail: Exact current D_2 support identities remain unchanged.
Identical causal raw pose/aperture/goal channels, native world action4 and declared object2 point semantics.
One LL and one HH sequence, 148 transitions total; no factorial recovery coverage is added for this revision.
Previously inspected obs 20:35 and 43:51 show closing followed by a stable hand-stick offset and coupled lift/transport; these motivate retaining motion-sensitive causal relation attention.
Previously inspected obs 22:27 and 43:48 show analogous acquisition and raised co-motion at the other support placement.
Actual inspected grasp/lift frame; the revision retains geometric fixture/tool dependence.
Actual inspected second-demo acquisition frame supports the same role-specific manipulation structure.
Actual inspected late second-demo interaction; the second object is not removed by compression.

Reported C=1.0 and E=1.0, all C cells 10/10 and all E cells 5/5; 5,346,303 parameters and 0.10788568950374611 s fixed-method latency. This motivates preserving the learned-encoder family while testing a smaller conditioning width, not a new checkpoint selection.

Reported C=1.0, E=0.6, 4,789,828 parameters and 0.10627669300447451 s latency; eight native truncations. The smaller deterministic model is not selected merely for speed and does not establish a specific grasp-failure mechanism.

Reported C=0.65, E=0.25 and 0.11014286049612565 s latency, with 25 native truncations. A4 does not adopt the goal-action frame or joint auxiliary diffusion; these results cannot isolate which A3 component caused its lower success.
Same fixed optimizer, final-update EMA, U-Net family, native action loss and separately mask-normalized auxiliary hooks. Only conditioning dimensionality changes with the compact architecture.

design.expected_failure_signature: If A2 needs more than eight learned features per role, compression will lose transition or off-diagonal/extrapolated robustness even though all raw geometry is still available. This could manifest as more native truncations, possibly at closing/lift/transport transitions; no phase-specific diagnostic has been observed. If success is retained but the fixed latency is not lower, the efficiency hypothesis fails under the frozen tie rule. A2's finite 20/20 C and 20/20 E observations do not imply population perfection, and A4 has no measured outcome yet.

required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Identity action4 encode/decode exactly as A2: native world xyz displacements at 0.01 m scale plus independent gripper scalar. No action projection, rescaling, candidate clipping or controller correction. The common executor alone clips the native cube and executes four of sixteen.
required_runtime_fields.condition: 76 channels per observation: the unchanged 49-channel lossless physical bypass, three gated 8-dimensional role embeddings, and three causal attention weights. Shared edge encoder 24->64->8, gate 14->32->3. Fixed physical scales, no fitted statistics.
required_runtime_fields.source: Only causal_context.raw_history [B,2,39] from shared deployment observations. No labels, extra sensor values, environment handles, caches or earlier model weights.

design.reusable_regularity: Preserve A2's shared, role-tagged hand-stick, stick-pushed-object and pushed-object-goal encoder, causal learned relation attention, physical hand-rooted bypass and training-only motion supervision. Reduce each role's learned embedding from 24 to 8 dimensions; keep roles separate rather than pooling them. The hypothesis is that a low-dimensional interaction salience/contact state can supplement exact geometry, instead of encoding a full trajectory or episode identity in a large latent vector. Because the bypass remains lossless, narrowing the learned augmentation does not remove a raw physical dependency.
design.title: Compact typed-interaction bottleneck

training_only_targets.loss: Same 0.2 times future-motion MSE as A2, summed only over the intersection of public mask and future_motion_valid and divided by 10 times the intersected mask sum, with empty denominator floor 1. Public action epsilon loss retains weight 1 and mask.sum()*4 denominator.
training_only_targets.name: future_motion
training_only_targets.predictor: 76->128->160 MLP from the causal conditioned current observation, producing [B,16,10]. This head executes only in training_loss. No future data is ever passed to condition or deployment denoising.
training_only_targets.source_fields: Unchanged from A2: for valid j=0..15 with t+j<T in each exact support window, use obs[t+j+1] minus obs[t] for hand[0:3], stick[4:7], pushed-object[11:14] positions and aperture[3:4]. Positions are divided by 0.1 m; aperture change is unscaled. Padding is zero and invalid.
